items.description: Release: llm-gemini 0.36 Gemini 4 Carbon was announced two weeks ago for "a subset of cyber defenders", but today it's available to everyone else .

items.title: Medical Image Segmentation: Foundation Model Adaptation versus Task-Specific Training
items.description: Foundation models pretrained on large natural-image collections are increasingly adapted for medical image segmentation, in the expectation that they will replace models trained for each task.
items.ai_summary: Researchers adapted the DINOv2 foundation model for medical image segmentation and found it generalized better on external datasets compared to task-specific models.

items.title: Toward Foundation Detection Models via Example-Based Grounding in EM-DETR
items.description: DeepLearning (DL)-based Computer-Aided Diagnostic (CAD) systems have shown great promise in supporting clinicians, but their performance heavily depends on the availability of large, well-annotated datasets.
items.ai_summary: Researchers introduce a student-teacher training strategy and adapt the EM-DETR framework to build a multi-domain foundation model for medical lesion detection.

items.title: TorchCurves: Differentiable Parametric Curves
items.description: TorchCurves is a PyTorch library that enables differentiable, learnable vector-valued parametric curves for integration with neural models and applications such as continuous embeddings, Kolmogorov-Arnold networks, and functional regression.
items.ai_summary: TorchCurves is a PyTorch library that treats vector-valued parametric curves as learnable primitives for applications like continuous feature embeddings and functional regression.

items.title: AutoScaffold: AI-Guided Scaffolding for Reinforcement Learning of Language Models
items.description: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) produces rich training experience, yet outcome rewards reduce each attempt to a single number and leave most of this information unused.
items.ai_summary: AutoScaffold is an AI-for-AI framework that automatically generates and adapts training scaffolds from student experience, outperforming standard reinforcement learning baselines across four diverse domains.

items.title: Contrastive Discovery: Open-Ended Scientific Discovery over Competing Explanations
items.description: LLM agents are increasingly used for open-ended, data-driven scientific discovery, yet most of them evaluate hypotheses pointwise, testing an empirical claim $h$ only against its complement $\neg h$.
items.ai_summary: Contrastive Discovery replaces pointwise hypothesis testing with mutually exclusive competing explanations in LLM agents, resolving scientific questions more effectively and outperforming pointwise search.

items.title: Pyrite: Building and Benchmarking Protein-Ligand Pose Ranking Agents
items.description: Predicting how a ligand binds to its target is central to small-molecule drug discovery. Modern cofolding models can generate diverse candidate poses, but reliably ranking these candidates remains challenging.
items.ai_summary: Pyrite introduces a pairwise protein-ligand pose-ranking benchmark and LLM-based agents that use structured representations and feature discovery to exceed expert performance in small-molecule drug discovery.

items.title: When Does the Real Wiring Win? Testing connectome structure-function claims against unmeasured physiology
items.description: Connectome-constrained models are often used to argue that a measured wiring diagram outperforms shuffled or rewired wiring, and hence that structure shapes function.
items.ai_summary: A comparative study of connectome-constrained models reveals that tuning methodology and physiological assumptions critically impact whether biological wiring diagrams outperform shuffled null models.

items.title: Continual-ARC: Measuring Skill Acquisition over a Working Lifetime
items.description: Agent harnesses have emerged as a promising mechanism for continual learning, alongside test-time parametric learning.
items.ai_summary: Continual-ARC is a lifelong evaluation stream built from ARC-AGI tasks that measures both memorization and generalization across memory-based and weight-based learning systems.

items.title: Emergent Biological Capabilities in a Foundation Model for Molecular Interactions
items.description: Foundation models trained on large unlabeled corpora develop emergent capabilities, tasks that go beyond the training objective.
items.ai_summary: Bonbon is a multimodal foundation model for molecular interactions that exhibits zero-shot emergent functional, residue, and bond capabilities from paired protein-ligand sequences.

items.title: Measuring Robustness and Efficiency in a Connectome-Constrained Fly Visual System Model: Linking an Adversarial and a Perceptual Illusion
items.description: Biological visual systems compute reliably under tight metabolic and wiring constraints, whereas artificial vision systems consume far more energy and can be sensitive to adversarial perturbations.
items.ai_summary: FlyNet is a connectome-constrained neural network model of the fly visual system that achieves high computational efficiency and robust collision detection compared to standard artificial neural networks.

items.title: RS-JEPA: Remote Sensing Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture with Scan-Path Views for Cross-Sensor Image Retrieval
items.description: Cross-sensor remote sensing image retrieval aims to find scenes with the same content across heterogeneous sensors, such as SAR and optical or panchromatic (PAN) and multispectral (MS) imagery, without manual labels.
items.ai_summary: RS-JEPA is a compact joint-embedding predictive architecture using Vision Mamba encoders and scan-path views to achieve effective cross-sensor remote sensing image retrieval.

items.title: Comparative Analysis of Agent Evaluation Frameworks: Stability, Detection, and Discovery in Enterprise Analytics Agents
items.description: Deploying LLM-based analytics agents in enterprise settings requires evaluation frameworks that can reliably detect failures across complex, multi-tool workflows.
items.ai_summary: A three-phase comparative study of enterprise analytics agent evaluation frameworks demonstrates that trace-based evaluation and adversarial red-teaming provide complementary detection of failures.

items.title: ReTrace: Distilling Tool-Using Agents into Planner-Free Workflows
items.description: Business process automation runs the same Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) again and again on new inputs.
items.ai_summary: ReTrace distills natural language standard operating procedures and logged agent runs into efficient, reusable programmatic workflows that lower cost and latency while maintaining high task completion rates.

items.title: TimeSeek: Multi-Task and Multi-Domain Pretraining for Generalized Time Series Analytics
items.description: Time series analytics has been widely applied across various domains.
items.ai_summary: TimeSeek is a generalized time series model that combines multi-domain feature extraction and multi-task collaborative training to improve performance across diverse forecasting and anomaly detection tasks.

items.title: Re-Search: Dissecting LLM Ideation Through a Two-Player Questioning Game
items.description: Research ideation is iterative: researchers refine their ideas step by step based on feedback. Yet existing evaluations obscure this search process, making it difficult to understand how LLMs explore the space of research ideas and what limits their progress.
items.ai_summary: Re-Search is an evaluation framework based on Twenty Questions that tracks how large language models explore research ideas, revealing that generation is the primary bottleneck in automated ideation.

items.title: Mechanistic Interpretability Needs a Logic of Inference
items.description: Neural networks are increasingly studied not merely as predictive systems, but as complex systems whose internal computations are themselves objects of scientific inquiry.
items.ai_summary: This paper establishes five principles and a recursive logic of inference to improve how mechanistic interpretability identifies and validates neural network computations.

items.title: Pterodactyl: Pushing the Limits of Efficient Automated Translation Evaluation
items.description: In this paper, we present 1020 Group's submission to the WMT26 shared task on automated quality evaluation. Our system, Pterodactyl, was engineered specifically for subtasks 2 and 3, that is, segment-level quality score prediction and the detection of error-free segments.
items.ai_summary: Pterodactyl is an ultra-low-cost automated translation evaluation system designed for binary classification tasks like segment-level quality scoring and error-free detection using an LLM-as-a-judge approach.

items.title: FERN: Cross-Benchmark Table Retrieval for Text-to-SQL with Frozen Retrievers and Learned Ranking
items.description: Text-to-SQL systems over large pooled catalogs must first retrieve the tables a question needs. We compare against the published table recall of RASL, which uses Claude 3.5 models to extract keywords and select tables, on pooled BIRD, Spider, and Fiben catalogs.
items.ai_summary: FERN is a table retrieval system for Text-to-SQL tasks that combines frozen retrievers with a LightGBM ranker to efficiently select relevant database tables without using generative large language models.

items.title: BoviShift: A Six-Year Multi-Attribute Audit of Visual Cattle Phenotyping Across Animals and Time
items.description: Computer vision offers a scalable, non-contact means of estimating livestock traits, but correlated images and video frames make reliable evaluation difficult.
items.ai_summary: BoviShift is a six-year visual cattle dataset and evaluation framework that assesses computer vision model performance across changing animal cohorts, breeds, and time.

items.title: TanCRAFT: Context-Reasoned Anticipatory Feedback for Assembly Tasks
items.description: Preventing human error in physical assembly tasks requires assistance systems that can intervene before mistakes are made.
items.ai_summary: TanCRAFT is a real-time predictive assistance system that tracks assembly state, forecasts motion, and provides contextual feedback to prevent human errors during physical tasks.

items.title: C$^2$-Routing: Complementary Cropping and Compression for Efficient Vision-Language Inference
items.description: Visual Question Answering (VQA) imposes substantial computational overhead on vision-language models (VLMs), motivating model-agnostic input reduction methods that can be readily applied across diverse VLMs, including in black-box settings.
items.ai_summary: C2-Routing is an adaptive vision-language inference method that combines image cropping, compression, and a safety gate to reduce computational overhead while preserving accuracy across diverse tasks.

items.title: Bayesian inverse problems and epidemic-threshold uncertainty for a heterogeneous SIS reaction-diffusion model
items.description: We study Bayesian inference of persistence from early observations of a heterogeneous susceptible--infected--susceptible (SIS) reaction--diffusion model with standard incidence.
items.ai_summary: This paper uses Bayesian inference and a uniform second-order expansion to analyze epidemic thresholds and parameter uncertainty in early observations of a heterogeneous SIS reaction-diffusion model.

items.title: A Theory of Policy Optimization in Post-Training: Coverage Collapse and Reference Resets
items.description: Policy optimization is central to language model post-training, yet principled guidance remains limited.
items.ai_summary: This paper identifies coverage collapse in language model policy optimization and introduces reference resets within Approximate Policy Mirror Descent to guarantee global convergence.

items.title: One Curve, Different Weights: AUC, the Brier Score, Decision-Weighted AUC, and the Policy Youden Index
items.description: AUC and the Brier score are standard summaries of a binary risk score, yet they can rank models differently. We introduce a weighted AUC, AUC$_π$, which weights each pair of observations by how differently a decision maker with probability of acting $π$ treats them.
items.ai_summary: Weighted AUC, or AUC_pi, is proposed as a risk score summary that weighs observation pairs based on a decision maker's probability of acting to consistently evaluate models.

items.title: A Theory of Cross-Validation Variance
items.description: Cross-validation estimates predictive performance by repeatedly splitting the data into training and validation sets, fitting the model on the first and evaluating it on the second.
items.ai_summary: A finite-sample identity for cross-validation variance is proven, showing that K-fold and leave-pair-out schemes are variance optimal at first order.

items.title: Accurate predictions of properties of energetic materials with tabular foundation models
items.description: We use TabPFN, a recently developed tabular foundation model, to predict three properties of energetic materials: impact sensitivity, decomposition temperature and crystal density.
items.ai_summary: Tabular foundation model TabPFN is shown to outperform tuned machine learning models in predicting impact sensitivity, decomposition temperature, and crystal density of energetic materials.

items.title: When does text encoding matter for language modeling?
items.description: UTF-8's role as the de facto encoding standard in language models introduces cross-lingual inequities due to its variable-length design. However, the effect that this encoding choice has on model performance remains largely unexamined.
items.ai_summary: A hybrid text encoding scheme named Aether is proposed to evaluate how text encoding strategies impact the performance of byte-level language models across diverse languages.

items.title: A Lightweight Differentiable Method for Real-Time Skin Rendering and Digitization
items.description: Inverse rendering for skin typically relies on offline path tracing to estimate physical properties, which fail to map directly to the approximate shaders utilized in interactive applications, such as game engines.
items.ai_summary: A differentiable screen-space subsurface scattering framework is introduced for real-time skin rendering and digitization using lightweight, single-view inputs.

items.title: Nonparametric Maximum Likelihood Estimation for Mixtures of Logistic Regressions
items.description: Mixtures of logistic regressions provide a flexible framework for modeling binary responses, extending standard logistic regression to accommodate unobserved heterogeneity while retaining an interpretable regression structure.
items.ai_summary: A sieve nonparametric maximum likelihood estimator is analyzed for mixtures of logistic regressions to model binary responses with unobserved heterogeneity.

items.title: UGG: Unified Generative Geometry Model
items.description: Understanding 4D scenes is a core challenge in visual intelligence, requiring models to jointly capture scene geometry, appearance, and dynamics from partial observations.
items.ai_summary: Unified Generative Geometry Model jointly models RGB video, depth, and camera pose to improve 4D scene understanding and visual generation.

items.title: Metric-Aligned Group Relative Policy Optimization for Explainable Deepfake Detection
items.description: Deepfake detectors are commonly evaluated on real/fake classification alone, but real-world applications require explanations of the visual evidence behind each prediction.
items.ai_summary: Metric-aligned Group Relative Policy Optimization is applied to train a vision-language model pipeline for explainable deepfake detection.

items.title: One Policy for 100 Household Tasks: Our Solution for the 2026 BEHAVIOR Challenge
items.description: We describe our solution for the 2026 BEHAVIOR Challenge: 100 long-horizon household tasks in the OmniGibson simulator. We placed 9th on the final leaderboard, the only independent team in the top 10.
items.ai_summary: A single vision-language-action model trained on 211 million frames is demonstrated to handle 100 long-horizon household tasks in the OmniGibson simulator.

items.title: Two Communities, One Problem: Branch-and-Bound vs. A* for Resource-Constrained Project Scheduling
items.description: Branch-and-Bound (B&B) and $A^*$ are popular exact search methods originating from Operations Research and Artificial Intelligence, respectively.
items.ai_summary: A graph-based A* search method is shown to substantially outperform branch-and-bound variants when applied to resource-constrained project scheduling problems.

items.title: Quantifying the Sampling Frequency Invariance of Time-Series Foundation Models for Sensor Data Applications
items.description: Time-Series Foundation Models (TSFMs) are increasingly used in sensor applications, where sampling frequency (SF) varies across sensors, devices, and operating modes (e.g., power saving).
items.ai_summary: Stress-test study of four prominent time-series foundation models that quantifies their sampling frequency invariance and reveals how performance degradation under lower frequencies reflects information loss.

items.title: DnNP: Denoising Input Uncertainty in Neural Processes
items.description: Neural Processes (NPs) are flexible meta-learning models capable of uncertainty quantification across diverse applications. However, the standard NP framework assumes access to noise-free inputs.
items.ai_summary: Denoising Neural Processes extend the neural process framework using variational inference to explicitly model input uncertainty, significantly improving prediction and uncertainty quantification on noisy datasets.

items.title: Earlybird: Predictive Streaming Speech Recognition in 29M Parameters
items.description: Streaming speech recognizers output a word only after the speaker has finished it, typically 90-400 ms later. For a voice agent every millisecond counts: the sooner the words are outputted, the sooner the agent can start a search or plan its reply.
items.ai_summary: Earlybird is a 29M-parameter streaming speech recognizer that predicts words accurately before speakers finish them, enabling faster response times for voice agents.

items.title: OnlyAct: Extracting Action Representations from Foundation Models for World Models
items.description: Video world models promise general-purpose interactive simulators, but their training is limited by action supervision: action labels are scarce, fragmented across incompatible specifications, and do not scale with the unlabeled video pretraining corpus.
items.ai_summary: Label-free contrastive adaptation framework that extracts action representations from pretrained foundation models for video world models without requiring a reconstruction bottleneck.

items.title: Evaluating LLM-Generated World Models for Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning
items.description: Formal world models can support planning, verification, and safety reasoning, but constructing them from open-ended natural-language situations is difficult, particularly in multi-agent settings where several formalizations may be plausible.
items.ai_summary: Evaluation of five language models on generating formal world models as partially observable stochastic games, finding that mechanical validity does not guarantee structural agreement for downstream reasoning.

items.title: Precision on Demand: Escalating Weight Bits at Uncertain Decoding Steps in a Small Local Model
items.description: A dynamic weight precision allocation strategy is proposed, utilizing low-bit quantization and uncertainty-based gating to selectively upgrade weight precision during LLM generation, thereby optimizing computational cost.
items.ai_summary: Method that dynamically escalates weight precision from 4 bits to 8 bits only at uncertain decoding steps in small local language models to optimize memory and accuracy.

items.title: Exploring Post-Hoc Disentanglement of Audio Foundation Models for Music Similarity
items.description: Audio foundation models like CLAP, MuQ, and MERT excel at capturing general musical similarity. On the other hand, their entangled latent spaces limit interpretability and fine-grained attribute control.
items.ai_summary: Study on post-hoc disentanglement of audio foundation models using conditional similarity networks with frozen pretrained embeddings to improve attribute-specific music similarity and retrieval.

items.title: Claude Whiteboards, Claude Sheets, and Claude Data
items.description: Trending on Hacker News from claude.com. 170 points and 138 comments.
items.ai_summary: Suite of collaborative tools that lets teams brainstorm, build spreadsheets, and share dashboards directly with Claude.

items.title: Bits or permutations? Spending a fixed inference budget on weight precision or on option-order averaging in small local language models
items.description: Local language models can save memory by storing weights in fewer bits, and they can reduce sensitivity to the order of answer options by averaging a few reorderings. We ask whether the first makes the second worse, and which is the cheaper way to spend a fixed budget.
items.ai_summary: Investigation comparing weight precision reductions and option-order averaging for small local language models, providing cost-matched guidelines for spending a fixed inference budget.

items.title: Causal Concept Explanations for Deep Neural Models
items.description: Concept-based explanations in neural models are important for the development, certification, and adoption of autonomous systems. Yet, interpretability remains correlational.
items.ai_summary: Causal Concept Wrapper Network uses interventional mediation analysis to align concept-based explanations with neural model outputs, ensuring explanations are necessary, sufficient, and independent.

items.title: Discovering Equations for the Thermodynamics of South Asian Monsoon Precipitation
items.description: South Asian monsoon precipitation depends on the thermodynamic structure of the lower troposphere, but how its ingredients combine to shape precipitation remains unclear, partly because this dependence is nonlocal in the vertical.
items.ai_summary: Symbolic distillation approach combining neural networks and symbolic regression to discover interpretable closed-form equations for South Asian monsoon precipitation from reanalysis data.

items.title: REAL Loss: Optimizing Real Expected Acceptance Length for Speculative Decoding
items.description: Speculative decoding accelerates LLM inference by having a draft model propose multiple tokens for the target model to verify in one pass.
items.ai_summary: REAL Loss is a training loss for speculative decoding that directly optimizes real expected acceptance length using path weights and Rao-Blackwellization, improving language model inference speed without architectural changes.

items.title: A Margin Perspective on LoRA: Robustness to Catastrophic Forgetting and Adapter Merging (MaLoRA)
items.description: Low-rank adaptation (LoRA) is the de facto method for parameter-efficient fine-tuning of large neural networks, achieving strong task adaptation with minimal trainable parameters and low optimization cost.
items.ai_summary: A margin-based perspective on LoRA provides a theoretical explanation for its robustness to catastrophic forgetting and adapter merging by showing optimal adapters align with max-margin solutions.

items.title: Blurring the Block Boundaries: Overlapping Block Denoising for Efficient Diffusion Language Models
items.description: Diffusion Language Models (DLMs) have emerged as effective alternatives to autoregressive models for latency-critical tasks, enabling faster token generation.
items.ai_summary: Blurring the Block Boundaries is a training-free acceleration method for diffusion language models that refines two blocks in parallel within a shared forward pass, improving latency-quality trade-offs.

items.title: An Energy-Based Perspective on Machine Learning
items.description: Energy-based models (EBMs) define a distribution through a scalar energy, $p_θ(x)\propto\exp(-E_θ(x))$, and are usually presented as one model family among many.
items.ai_summary: This tutorial frames energy-based models as a unifying lens that connects diverse machine learning paradigms through their choice of energy function, inference procedure, and learning method.

items.title: Cognitive Mapping of Learning by Thinking Mechanisms in Large Language Models
items.description: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly exhibit capabilities that resemble human Learning by Thinking (LbT), the acquisition of new insight through internal processes such as explanation and reasoning, without new external input.
items.ai_summary: This paper proposes a Cognitive Learning by Thinking Framework that maps human-like insight acquisition mechanisms onto computational processes in large language models and analyzes their structural failure modes.

items.title: What Factors Matter for Collection-Level Counting with Human-AI Collaboration?
items.description: Many scientific and policy decisions require estimating the total number of target objects across a large image collection. Exhaustive human labeling is often infeasible, while raw model predictions can be biased, especially under domain shift.
items.ai_summary: This study evaluates human-AI collaboration strategies for collection-level counting across diverse tasks, finding that multimodal models provide strong starting points while fine-tuned detectors excel at larger labeling budgets.

items.title: Uncertainty-Aware Hybrid Offline Reinforcement Learning with Online Action Selection Enabled by Sparse Gaussian-Process Critics
items.description: Start-ups and grade changes remain largely operator-driven, while developing and maintaining dynamic models for model-based control requires substantial engineering effort.
items.ai_summary: A hybrid offline reinforcement learning approach uses a sparse Gaussian-process critic with uncertainty-adjusted action selection to eliminate failed start-ups in industrial control benchmarks.

items.title: From Video Frames to Robot Meta-Frames: A Unified Latent Interface for World Action Models
items.description: Pretrained video diffusion models (VDMs) offer a powerful foundation for World Action Models (WAMs), which jointly predict robot actions and future observations. Building such models requires injecting low-dimensional robot signals (e.g.
items.ai_summary: MetaWAM is a unified latent interface for robot world action models that packs all robot signals into a single frequency-domain meta-frame to align with pretrained video diffusion priors without architectural modifications.

items.title: ARE-bench: Benchmarking Agents' Research Ability in Real-World Researcher Sessions and Workspaces
items.description: Research agents achieve increasingly strong benchmark scores, yet these scores do not necessarily translate into reliable delivery in ongoing research projects.
items.ai_summary: ARE-bench is a benchmark of 75 tasks built on real researcher sessions and workspaces to evaluate whether research agents can successfully advance ongoing research projects.

items.title: The Unused Input: The Initial State as a Conditioning Interface for Recurrent TSFMs
items.description: Time series foundation models (TSFMs) forecast unseen series without task-specific training. Increasingly they are built on recurrent backbones, whose constant per-step cost makes long-context inference cheap, and which, unlike transformers, carry a state.
items.ai_summary: A novel method utilizes the initial recurrent state in time-series foundation models as a conditioning interface, improving zero-shot forecasting accuracy by injecting context vectors into the hidden state.

items.title: EngineAgent: Agentizing On-Device LLM Inference Engines with Inference Stack Hierarchy Awareness and Hardware Abilities
items.description: Rapidly evolving LLM architectures and heterogeneous mobile hardware make supporting new models in on-device inference engines a recurring and costly system challenge.
items.ai_summary: EngineAgent is an agentic system that automates on-device LLM model enablement by separating reusable engine knowledge from model-specific implementation to coordinate cross-layer changes.

items.title: CLADE: Category-Level Answering from Deficient Evidence in Retrieval-Augmented Language Models
items.description: Retrieval-augmented systems often retrieve passages that are accurate and relevant but state the answer at a coarser level of granularity than the question requires.
items.ai_summary: The study demonstrates that retrieval-augmented language models answer incorrectly when given coarse category-level passages instead of abstaining, a phenomenon termed Clade.

items.title: AI Isn't Getting Dumber, We're Getting Pickier: Rising Standards in Human Evaluation of Large Language Models
items.description: Users often complain that AI assistants such as ChatGPT are getting worse. Some versions do change, but human evaluation leaves a second possibility untested: the people judging may change.
items.ai_summary: An analysis of over one million blind votes on Chatbot Arena reveals that human evaluation standards for large language models have steadily risen over time.

items.title: Forward-Value Discretization: Faster Stochastic Diffusion Sampling Without High-Order Approximation
items.description: Stochastic diffusion samplers often require substantially more neural function evaluations (NFEs) than deterministic samplers to achieve comparable sample quality.
items.ai_summary: Forward-value discretization is a training-free framework that accelerates stochastic diffusion sampling by evaluating the prediction model at a lookahead estimate constructed from previous predictions.

items.title: When Should Agents Remember? Falsification-Gated Self-Evolution for LLM Agents
items.description: LLM agents increasingly operate in long-horizon, verifier-rich environments, but current self-improvement mechanisms often write episode-derived lessons directly into memory, making local success an unreliable signal for reusable and safe knowledge.
items.ai_summary: Falsification-Gated Self-Evolution is a verifier-grounded framework that tests candidate agent lessons as structured hypotheses against targeted probes before committing them to persistent memory.

items.title: Point-in-Time Encoders for Earnings Calls
items.description: Text encoders turn earnings calls into vectors for search, for language models that answer from retrieved passages, and for forecasting models.
items.ai_summary: Point-in-time text encoders trained on earnings calls without future data improve information retrieval for financial backtests and question-answering tasks.

items.title: Auditing the Judge: Internal Signals for LLM Reasoning Assurance
items.description: Language-model systems use self-judgment to decide which answers to release, review, or recompute. Because intervention is costly, an assurance score must rank errors well at the available budget, not merely over the full ranking.
items.ai_summary: Supervised correctness probes trained on internal model activations improve error detection and budget allocation compared to using self-judgment verdict scores alone.

items.title: Don't Just Trust Your Memory: Evidence-Linked Memory Reduces Memory-Induced Degradation in LLM Agents
items.description: WikiTrace links each distilled lesson to its source trajectory and rationale, enabling LLM agents to verify and correct memories before acting, improving performance and reducing memory-induced degradation across agentic benchmarks.
items.ai_summary: WikiTrace is an evidence-linked memory system that lets AI agents verify and correct past behavioral lessons against their raw execution trajectories to prevent performance degradation.

items.title: MammothDP: Private Boosted Decision Trees Ready for Trusted Hardware and Leakage-free Hyperparameters
items.description: Data spaces like the European Health Data Space (EHDS) require the protection of sensitive data in studies during the data's processing and the study's release alike.
items.ai_summary: MammothDP is a differential privacy gradient boosted decision tree system hardened against timing side-channels for secure execution within trusted environments.

items.title: PSL-RGHA: Parallel Split Learning with Reference Gradient Half-Space Alignment for Mitigating Gradient Divergence
items.description: The escalating complexity of deep neural networks hinders the deployment of federated learning (FL) on resource-constrained devices, especially for multimedia applications such as on-device image classification and speech recognition.
items.ai_summary: PSL-RGHA is a parallel split learning framework that uses a reference gradient half-space alignment mechanism to mitigate training divergence across heterogeneous client devices.

items.title: Multimodal Abstention That Preserves Acquired Correct Answers
items.description: Adding abstention to a task-adapted multimodal model can discard correct answers, including capabilities acquired during adaptation. We formulate abstention repair as maximizing correct abstention on unanswerable questions under a budget on newly lost correct answers.
items.ai_summary: ReFrain is a regression-free abstention method for multimodal models that preserves acquired correct answers while improving correct abstention rates.

items.title: MMDM: Measuring Massive Multitask Decision Making
items.description: System-1 Decision Models directly make structured probabilistic decisions over query-specified options given a state in a single forward pass, without autoregressively generating reasoning trajectories or textual responses.

items.title: TaoMate-R1: Temporal Role Specialization for Streaming Multi-Reference Video Generation
items.description: Streaming multi-reference video generation establishes a scene from specified people and objects, then continues it under changing instructions.
items.ai_summary: TaoMate-R1 is a streaming multi-reference video generator that uses temporal role specialization to organize adaptation parameters for scene establishment and continuation.

items.title: ForeseeDrive: Future-Token Conditioning for Anticipatory Generative Driving
items.description: Generative driving planners can represent diverse ego futures, but a downstream scorer can choose only among sampled candidates; it cannot recover an absent maneuver.
items.ai_summary: ForeseeDrive is an anticipatory generative driving planner that uses future-token conditioning to shape candidate trajectory generation and improve safety metrics.

items.title: LM-SimBench: A Unified Framework, Dataset, and Benchmark for Large Language Model Training Simulation
items.description: Evaluating candidate parallelization strategies through distributed training runs makes strategy selection prohibitively expensive at scale.
items.ai_summary: LM-SimBench is a unified framework, dataset, and benchmark for evaluating and comparing large language model training simulators across parallelization configurations.

items.title: Ninety-Six Ways to Measure a Scribe: Fragmented Evaluation of Ambient Scribes in Healthcare
items.description: Ambient artificial intelligence (AI) scribes have moved rapidly from experimental pilots to enterprise-wide deployment across health systems, promising reduced documentation burden and improved clinician experience.
items.ai_summary: This paper reviews evaluation studies of ambient AI scribes in healthcare to highlight metric fragmentation and the need for standardized assessment protocols.

items.title: UniFlow-RS: Unified Generative Prediction for Heterogeneous Remote-Sensing Tasks
items.description: Remote-sensing foundation models increasingly unify representations across sensing modalities and downstream tasks, yet their prediction mechanisms remain largely task-specific. Separate decoders, prediction heads, and objectives leave prediction fragmented across tasks.
items.ai_summary: UniFlow-RS is a remote-sensing foundation model that uses a shared latent flow-matching predictor to handle heterogeneous tasks and datasets.

items.title: AutoThreshold: Joint Confusion-Profile Learning for Adaptive Mask Binarization
items.description: A single validation-tuned threshold can become brittle when dense-score distributions shift. We introduce AutoThreshold, a post-hoc policy that predicts the joint mass of positive and negative pixels over score bins.
items.ai_summary: AutoThreshold is a post-hoc policy that predicts joint confusion profiles to enable adaptive mask binarization for any target objective without retraining.

items.title: Compositional random forest
items.description: Compositional data have been analysed in the literature from three main points of view: directly on the simplex, in log-ratio coordinates, and as directional data on the unit sphere.
items.ai_summary: This paper presents a random forest framework for compositional responses using log-likelihood gain as a split criterion across simplex, log-ratio, and directional spaces.

items.title: Federated Learning for Cross-Regional Epidemic Forecasting with Asynchronous Outbreaks
items.description: Objective: Epidemic outbreaks are often asynchronous across regions, yet collaborative forecasting is hampered by privacy laws and heterogeneous public health interventions.
items.ai_summary: This paper evaluates a federated learning framework for cross-regional epidemic forecasting using asynchronous COVID-19 data while preserving data privacy.

items.title: Achieving Robust Channel Estimation Neural Networks on Doppler effects by Designed Training Data
items.description: Channel estimation is crucial in wireless communication systems. Many existing works train and test their models using the same or similar channel.
items.ai_summary: This paper proposes design criteria for generating synthetic training data that enable offline-trained neural networks to perform robust channel estimation across high Doppler shifts.

items.title: Physics-Constrained Autoencoder for Interpretable Health Representation Learning in Turbofan Engines
items.description: Health Indices (HIs) summarize degradation from operational data and support diagnostic and prognostic tasks in Prognostics and Health Management (PHM). Their usefulness depends on capturing degradation and interpreting system condition.
items.ai_summary: Physics-constrained autoencoder that embeds system knowledge into the decoder and loss function to learn interpretable health representations and track degradation in turbofan engines.

items.title: Chain of Physics: Supporting Fault Diagnosis with Engineering-Inspired Large Language Model Reasoning
items.description: Fault diagnosis in complex systems requires linking observed changes in physical quantities to the failure mechanisms that produce them. Experienced engineers perform this task by combining sensor information with knowledge of system behavior and fault propagation.
items.ai_summary: Chain of Physics is an LLM-based fault-diagnosis framework that uses a constrained knowledge graph generated from reference documentation to retrieve and reason about failure modes and sensor data.

items.title: Recurrent Modular Structure in Spiking Neural Network Reinforcement Learning
items.description: Biological neural circuits are both modular and recurrent, with dense communities sparsely linked to one another.
items.ai_summary: Community Recurrent Spiking Neural Networks partition recurrent networks into communities with fixed roles to improve reinforcement learning performance and generate compressible spike activity.

items.title: Lilo: A Multi-Agent Conversational Sandbox for Children's Digital Communication
items.description: Children's peer conflicts increasingly play out in group chats, where tone and timing are stripped away, and a hurtful message is easier to send than to say aloud.
items.ai_summary: Lilo is a multi-agent conversational system that allows children to practice navigating peer conflicts and communicate more effectively through simulated group chat arguments and mentor interventions.

items.title: Elastic-WAM: Adaptive Spatiotemporal Imagination for Efficient Robot Control
items.description: World-Action Models improve robot control by predicting future visual dynamics, but iterative video denoising incurs substantial inference overhead. Recent approaches reduce this cost through partial future denoising, yet typically rely on fixed refinement budgets.
items.ai_summary: Elastic-WAM is a robot control framework that adaptively allocates world refinement computation across temporal and spatial regions to improve task success while reducing inference latency.

items.title: A Cross-Scenario Survey and Analysis of Self-Evolving Multimodal Agents
items.description: A survey analyzes why self-improvement mechanisms for multimodal agents transfer unevenly across reasoning, generation, navigation, and manipulation scenarios, framing them as trade-offs over scarce factors and task-structural resources.
items.ai_summary: Cross-scenario survey and analysis framework that evaluates the portability of self-evolving multimodal agent mechanisms by categorizing scarce factors and task-structural resources.

items.title: Location Matters: Sparse Latent-Variance Attacks for Face Privacy against Diffusion Personalization
items.description: Text-to-image diffusion models can learn and reproduce an individual's identity from only a few reference photos, creating risks of unauthorized and misleading content generation.
items.ai_summary: Sparse Encoder Attack on Latent Variance is a sparse adversarial protection framework that modifies a small fraction of facial image locations to disrupt identity acquisition in diffusion models.

items.title: Semantic Chains: From Reachable Facts to Justified Answers
items.description: How can the facts that justify an answer be found from a question and presented as a sequence of connected statements? This paper models a context as a graph of logical facts and takes as given which expressions represent each fact.
items.ai_summary: Semantic Chains is a logical modeling framework that constructs connected sequences of facts from a question to find and justify correct answers.

items.title: Personalized Affective Perception via Continual Learning in Human-Agent Negotiation
items.description: Self-interested intelligent agents that negotiate with humans should interpret nonverbal expressions and adapt their behavior accordingly. However, generic facial-affect models degrade across individuals and contexts, creating a generalization gap.
items.ai_summary: Affect-adaptive negotiation strategy that uses continual learning for facial expression recognition to personalize valence-arousal perception in real-time human-agent interactions.

items.title: SinkState: On-the-Fly SVD of Recurrent States for Efficient Hybrid LLM Serving
items.description: Hybrid models combine softmax attention with linear attention, which compresses history into fixed-size recurrent states to balance model quality and inference efficiency.
items.ai_summary: SinkState is an efficient hybrid LLM serving system that stores recurrent states in an adaptive low-rank form using on-the-fly SVD to reduce memory traffic and speed up decoding.

items.title: An AI Assistant for Automating Anti-Corruption Expertise of Draft Legislation Based on the TRACE Framework
items.description: We present an AI assistant for automating anti-corruption expertise of draft legislation based on the TRACE architecture, designed to screen bills for corruption risks: pinpoint provisions an expert would criticise and name the regulatory defect in each.
items.ai_summary: An AI assistant uses a deterministic parsing core and language models to screen draft legislation for corruption risks and regulatory defects.

items.title: Dyship: Leveraging Acoustic Features For Speaker Relationship Classification From Dyadic Conversations
items.description: We introduce DyShip, a framework for classifying speaker familiarity and kinship from dyadic conversations in the Seamless Interaction corpus.
items.ai_summary: Dyship is a framework for classifying speaker familiarity and kinship from dyadic conversations using conventional acoustic features.

items.title: On Federated Averaging with Partial Participation under a General Variance Condition
items.description: In this paper, we study the convergence of Federated Averaging (FedAvg) with partial participation under a general variance condition. In each communication round, the server samples $S$ of the $n$ clients uniformly at random without replacement.
items.ai_summary: Federated Averaging with partial participation is analyzed under a general variance condition, establishing a finite-time stationarity bound without requiring bounded gradient dissimilarity.

items.title: StaRSE: Compact Russian Sentence Embeddings with a Sign-Coded Static Encoder
items.description: Transformer sentence encoders provide strong retrieval quality, but their inference cost becomes a bottleneck when embeddings must be produced on CPUs or refreshed frequently.
items.ai_summary: StaRSE is a compact Russian static sentence encoder that eliminates Transformer inference at deployment time by storing token directions as sign bits and norms separately.

items.title: Stagewise and interpretable emergence of inside-outside computation in Transformer-based language models
items.description: Variability in syntactic structure and parsing ambiguity are fundamental aspects of natural language which modern LLMs have to learn to deal with proficiently.
items.ai_summary: A synthetic context-free grammar study reveals that Transformers develop inside-outside parsing in interpretable, stagewise learning curves that transition from local to abstract representations.

items.title: SHARP: Semantic Hierarchical Agentic Reasoning for Next POI Prediction with Dynamic Memory
items.description: Next point-of-interest (POI) prediction supports personalized location services by anticipating users' next destinations. Recent methods leverage large language models (LLMs) for semantic reasoning and graphs for collective mobility modeling, improving POI prediction.
items.ai_summary: SHARP is an agentic hierarchical framework that combines category-level reasoning, dynamic trajectory memory, and time-aware transition graphs to predict next points of interest.

items.title: ViGA-FLAME: Aligning Latent Visual and Geometric Representations for Robust 3D Head Expression Estimation
items.description: Estimating 3D head expression from a single image requires mapping visual appearance to underlying facial geometry. We propose ViGA-FLAME, a two-stage framework that aligns semantic visual features with a structured geometric latent space.
items.ai_summary: ViGA-FLAME is a two-stage framework that aligns semantic visual features with a structured geometric latent space to enable robust 3D head expression estimation.

items.title: Verifiable Agentic Traffic Class: A Policed Quality-of-Service Mechanism for Agentic AI Traffic, Evaluated from Simulation to Real-Kernel Adversarial Testing
items.description: Software agents built on large language models generate traffic unlike human web traffic, yet routers have no class for it and cannot verify a sender's claim to be an agent.
items.ai_summary: Verifiable Agentic Traffic Class is a policed quality-of-service mechanism that uses reserved DSCP values, router-side classification, and rate-limiting to manage software agent network traffic.

items.title: Tree-Ising: Repairing Language Models with Bit-Level Ising Edits
items.description: Tree-Ising repairs reasoning loops in LLM weights by solving sparse Ising/QUBO problems over BF16 parameters, improving math benchmark accuracy with fewer weight edits and no gradient or LLM-token cost.

items.title: Breakdown of Autoregressive Multi-Step Reasoning Under Concentrated vs. Diffuse Attention Head Dropout
items.description: During extended wakefulness, mammalian neocortical networks experience localized periods of transient neuronal silence termed off-states.
items.ai_summary: Concentrated bursts of attention head masking cause significantly worse reasoning degradation in autoregressive language models compared to diffuse, budget-matched dropout.

items.title: DailyWildfireCAN: A Dataset and Benchmark for Next-Day Wildfire Spread Prediction in Canada
items.description: Wildfires represent a critical ecological and socio-economic challenge in Canada, where vast boreal forests and a warming climate have amplified the frequency and severity of extreme fire seasons.
items.ai_summary: DailyWildfireCAN is a multi-modal dataset and benchmark tracking continuous fire progression across Canada to support next-day wildfire spread prediction.

items.title: Joint Quantization and Dynamic Partitioning for Context-Aware Edge Vision Transformers
items.description: Deploying vision transformer models across connected and automated vehicles (CAVs) requires joint management of computation and Vehicle-to-Vehicle (V2V) communication.
items.ai_summary: Edge orchestration framework that jointly optimizes model partition points, quantization bitwidths, and execution placement to reduce communication energy and latency in vehicular vision transformer systems.

items.title: An Augmented Lagrangian Approach to Lifted Bellman Linear Programming
items.description: Temporal-difference critics regress onto a bootstrapped target and usually need a target network. Lifted Bellman Linear Programming (LBLP) instead expresses the in-sample optimal values of offline RL as the solution to a linear program over the dataset.
items.ai_summary: Temporal-difference critic solver using the method of multipliers to solve lifted bellman linear programming without a target network, achieving high success rates on offline reinforcement learning tasks.

items.title: SpecValley: Aggregation as Spectral Valley in Dense Heterophilic Graphs
items.description: Node classification in heterophilic graphs remains an open problem: aggregating over neighbourhoods can damp precisely the part of the signal that carries the labels.
items.ai_summary: Node classification framework that learns aggregation position, sharpness, and flank gains prior to spectral filtering, improving performance on dense heterophilic graphs.

items.title: Aircad – Professional drafting and 3D modeling in the browser
items.description: Aircad is a professional CAD system running in the browser with deep AI integration. It includes professional grade drafting and documentation tools, NURBS-based solid modeling, and a lot more. You can make professional quality design documents with it.
items.ai_summary: Browser-based professional CAD system featuring NURBS solid modeling, multiplayer editing, and deep AI integration.

items.title: Cross-Border Fulfillment Center Selection via Doubly Robust Estimation and Linear Programming
items.description: We introduce the cross-border (XB) fulfillment center (FC) Selection Model: a multi-stage optimization framework combining forecasting, doubly robust estimation, and linear programming to select optimal source FCs.
items.ai_summary: Cross-border fulfillment center selection framework combining forecasting, doubly robust estimation, and linear programming to minimize delivery time and shipping costs while maximizing profit.

items.title: BARS: Budget-Aware Sequential Sampling with Refusal for Majority Identification under Unknown Distributions
items.description: Repeated sampling with majority selection is an effective means of enforcing self-consistency in large language models. Recently, a variant has also been introduced that terminates early to save costs when the output distribution is favorable.
items.ai_summary: Sequential sampling rule with budgeting and refusal mechanisms that certifies error rates and improves accuracy for majority identification in large language models.

items.title: Representational Atoms in Neural Networks
items.description: Understanding the internal representations of neural networks and characterizing their relationship with human conceptual structure are two critical questions for elucidating model mechanisms.
items.ai_summary: Threshold-activated sparse autoencoders framework that identifies fundamental representational units with high fidelity and stability to analyze neural network internal representations and human conceptual structure.

items.title: Nonadaptive One-Sided Testing of Binary Rank
items.description: The binary rank of a binary matrix is the minimum number of disjoint all-one rectangles that partition its one-entries. We study entry-query testing of binary rank at most $d$, with one-sided error and nonadaptive queries.
items.ai_summary: Nonadaptive entry-query tester for binary matrices that uses a specified number of queries independent of dimensions to test binary rank with one-sided error.

items.title: Unipolar Neuron Networks Trained by Recirculation for Reward-Based Continual Learning
items.description: Unipolar neurons are the predominant type of nerve cell in the octopus and in most other invertebrates. A single neurite (a fiber extending from the cell body) branches into a tree that carries both input and output synapses.
items.ai_summary: Unipolar neuron network model utilizing a recirculation learning rule and task-specific inhibition mechanisms to achieve reward-based continual learning with low catastrophic forgetting.

items.title: From Search to Decision: How Post-Training Shapes Information-Seeking Capabilities in Large Language Models
items.description: Information seeking in large language model (LLM) systems increasingly involves decisions about when to acquire information, where to search, and how to evaluate and use evidence.
items.ai_summary: Survey paper that organizes research around six information-seeking capabilities in large language models, examining learning signals, optimization methods, and evaluation practices.

items.title: GARD: Gradient-Guided Adversarial Representation Defense against Backdoors in Multimodal Contrastive Learning Models
items.description: Multimodal contrastive learning models such as CLIP are vulnerable to backdoor attacks with diverse trigger structures, ranging from localized patches to globally distributed perturbations, with recent attacks increasingly optimizing these triggers in the representation space.
items.ai_summary: Gradient-guided adversarial representation defense framework that uses global and local adversarial probes to eliminate backdoor vulnerabilities in multimodal contrastive learning models without extra inference cost.

items.title: Deviation-Aware Pretraining for Cardiovascular Disease Detection from Electrocardiograms
items.description: Electrocardiogram (ECG) signals are critical for cardiovascular disease (CVD) detection. Most current deep learning models rely on supervised, task-specific training, which limits their ability to generalize across diseases, patient populations, and acquisition settings.
items.ai_summary: Self-supervised framework that analyzes electrocardiogram signals using deviation localization and association reconstruction to improve cardiovascular disease detection without requiring labeled data.

items.title: HaiRuo: Forecasting Ocean Eddies as Fields and Objects with a Satellite-Altimetry Foundation Model
items.description: Mesoscale eddies carry most of the ocean's kinetic energy and move heat, salt and nutrients across basins, yet where an eddy will be two weeks ahead is still read off ocean models with post-hoc tracking heuristics.
items.ai_summary: Open-weight foundation model paired with an object decoder that forecasts ocean eddies as both spatial fields and moving objects from satellite altimetry data.

items.title: Sim(3)-TurboReg: Robust and Efficient Scale-Aware Registration via Tri-Scale Consistency
items.description: Feed-forward 3D foundation models recover geometry at high fidelity, yet inference memory constraints keep them from processing long sequences natively.
items.ai_summary: Sim(3) registration solver that uses a tri-scale consistency criterion to eliminate mismatching outliers and enable efficient, kilometer-scale 3D reconstruction for streaming systems.

items.title: Right for the Wrong Reasons? Evaluating Plausibility and Behavioral Change in Explanation-Guided Learning
items.description: Explanation-Guided Learning (EGL) promises models that are not only accurate but also rely on task-relevant evidence. However, whether improved agreement between model explanations and human-provided rationales also implies a changed decision strategy remains unclear.
items.ai_summary: Benchmark framework that evaluates how different explanation-guided learning objectives affect model plausibility, behavioral change, and robustness against synthetic shortcuts.

items.title: Continuous 3D Spatial Transcriptomics Reconstruction via Histology-Informed Implicit Neural Representations
items.description: Three-dimensional spatial transcriptomics (3D ST) enables the analysis of gene-expression patterns across tissue depths. However, 3D ST measurements are acquired from discrete 2D tissue sections, which are often sparsely sampled due to high acquisition costs.
items.ai_summary: Implicit neural representation model that reconstructs continuous 3D gene-expression patterns from sparse spatial transcriptomics data by leveraging auxiliary histological images.

items.title: Hierarchical Graph Representation Learning with Pooling-Induced Substructures
items.description: Hierarchical graph-level tasks that require reasoning over substructures that extend beyond local neighborhoods are posing challenges for standard Graph Neural Networks (GNNs).
items.ai_summary: Graph neural network approach that explicitly preserves pooling-induced substructures to improve hierarchical graph representation learning and reasoning.

items.title: CroCoMAE: Cross-modal self-supervised collaborative representation learning for SAR-optical remote sensing data
items.description: Remote sensing increasingly captures the Earth's surface through complementary sensors such as SAR and optical, yet ground-truth annotations remain scarce, limiting supervised approaches.
items.ai_summary: Cross-modal self-supervised learning framework that combines contrastive learning and masked image modeling at image and patch levels to improve SAR-optical remote sensing analysis.

items.title: Hx2Dx: From Anamnesis to Diagnosis - A Multimodal Arena for Conversational Clinical Reasoning in LLMs
items.description: Large language models (LLMs) achieve expert-level diagnostic accuracy in static evaluations, where the model receives a curated vignette or case report that already condenses the diagnostically relevant findings.
items.ai_summary: Interactive benchmark based on clinical cases from the New England Journal of Medicine that evaluates how large language models perform iterative, conversational clinical reasoning and diagnosis.

items.title: TAMEing the Open-World Personalization: Towards Open-Set Personalized MLLM Assistant
items.description: Personalizing Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) as intelligent assistants has recently emerged as an active research topic, where an MLLM is expected to go beyond generic, one-size-fits-all replies, and instead generate responses grounded in user-specific objects,…
items.ai_summary: Long-context open-set personalized multimodal large language model assistant that uses a training-free concept reconciliation skill to automatically incorporate novel user-specific concepts during interactions.

items.title: Visual Similarity in Adult Word Extension and Artificial Word Learning
items.description: Visual similarity measured by a self-supervised visual encoder partially explains word generalization in adults and artificial learners, while the composition of teaching examples contributes additional structure beyond that distance.
items.ai_summary: Study using a self-supervised visual encoder to analyze how visual similarity and example composition influence adult word extension and artificial word learning.

items.title: Looking One Step Ahead: An Anticipation-guided Agent for Object State Readout in Videos
items.description: Understanding the progress of an activity requires tracking how the objects involved change over time. Object state readout provides this information by describing a target object's states and transitions across video frames.
items.ai_summary: Look-ahead state readout is an anticipation-guided agent for video object state readout that uses expected next-step changes to inspect current frames and refine state records.

items.title: Model-Free Runtime Measurement of Task-Relevant Information
items.description: Autonomous systems increasingly monitor physical kinematics, environmental states and task completion outcomes.
items.ai_summary: Acquisition-State Telemetry is a model-free architecture for autonomous systems that emits real-time signals to quantify prospective task progress and informational friction from ongoing observations.

items.title: ProofCoder: Continuous Reasoning for Automated Software Verification
items.description: Formal verification using proof assistants provides strong correctness guarantees for software, but constructing proofs remains labor-intensive and requires significant expertise.
items.ai_summary: ProofCoder is an agentic proof-synthesis system for Rocq that uses continuous reasoning and proof-assistant feedback to iteratively construct, repair, and refine software verification proofs.

items.title: Sckwoky at SHROOM-Visions: Character-Level Hallucination-Span Detection in Image-Conditioned VLMs via Dual-Prompted LoRA Decoders
items.description: We present our system for the SHROOM-visions 2026 shared task on character-level hallucination span detection in image-conditioned vision-language model (VLM) responses, evaluated across English, French, Italian, and Chinese.
items.ai_summary: Sven and colleagues present a character-level hallucination span detection system for image-conditioned vision-language models that uses a Gemma backbone, LoRA adapters, and a repeated-answer prompt strategy.

items.title: Opportunity-Cost Option-Critic: Adaptive Switching Costs for Robust Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning
items.description: Deliberation costs are commonly used in hierarchical reinforcement learning (HRL) to prevent options from collapsing to primitive actions. Existing approaches rely on fixed penalties or duration-based adaptations, both of which are indirect proxies for an option's utility.
items.ai_summary: Opportunity-Cost Option-Critic is a hierarchical reinforcement learning framework that uses state-dependent deliberation costs based on value gaps to improve option persistence and adaptation in non-stationary environments.

items.title: CUVE: Making Supervised Classification more Accessible through Visualization
items.description: We present CUVE, an interface that enables people to build classifiers by generating visualizations that are interpretable by both humans and learning algorithms (the Visualization as Intermediate Representation approach).
items.ai_summary: CUVE is an interface that allows users to build supervised classifiers by generating human- and algorithm-interpretable visualizations as an intermediate representation.

items.title: BODYinTRANSIT-Lab: A Multimodal Dataset for Investigating Sensory-Driven Transformations in Body Perception and Affective Experiences
items.description: Multimodal datasets that combine synchronised behavioural and physiological signals with subjective affective and body perception measures are still rare.
items.ai_summary: BODYinTRANSIT-Lab is a multimodal dataset capturing synchronised behavioural, physiological, affective, and body perception responses to manipulated walking feedback, accompanied by a deep learning classification benchmark.

items.title: Sable: A Small-Field Sumcheck Argument for Bit-Exact Inference of Large Language Models
items.description: We present Sable, an argument system and single-GPU prover for the statement that a committed, integer-quantized transformer produced a given token sequence from a given prompt, bit for bit.
items.ai_summary: Sable is an argument system and single-GPU prover that generates bit-exact, integer-quantized transformer inference proofs for large language models using Reed-Solomon codes and multilinear commitments.

items.title: From Bias to Positionality: A critical grammar for Large Language Models
items.description: Bias has become a default lens for understanding what machine learning systems do and how we should relate to them.
items.ai_summary: This paper proposes positionality as an analytical grammar for large language models to describe the located, multi-layered perspective from which a model speaks across its corpus, tuning, and prompts.

items.title: ZoomGain: Mining Global-to-Zoom Perception Gaps for Fine-Grained Visual Supervision
items.description: Fine-grained visual perception requires Vision-Language Models (VLMs) to locate and interpret subtle evidence within complex scenes.
items.ai_summary: ZoomGain is a data construction pipeline that exploits global-to-zoom perception gaps in vision-language models to automatically generate fine-grained visual supervision questions and benchmarks.

items.title: Obscured Wildfire Flame Detection by Spatio-temporal Analysis of Smoke Patterns Using Frame-wise Transformers
items.description: In this paper, we propose a new paradigm in wildfire management for detecting both visible and obscured fire using Deep Learning (DL).
items.ai_summary: Deep learning model that uses a frame-wise transformer architecture on RGB video to detect visible and obscured wildfire flames for aerial drone monitoring.

items.title: What a CAGE 4 Score Measures: An Audit of a Learned Cyber-Defense Benchmark, Its Reference Defenders, and the Tables Built on Them
items.description: CAGE Challenge 4 is the benchmark on which learned multi-agent cyber defenders are compared. We reproduce its two reference defenders, KEEP and H-MARL Expert, in a pinned container and show that three things read from it measure less than they are taken to measure.
items.ai_summary: Study of the CAGE Challenge 4 cyber-defense benchmark that identifies how simulator behaviors and evaluation setups distort the performance measurements of learned multi-agent defenders.

items.title: Generalizing Causal Decision-Making: Markov Equivalence, Transportability and Counterfactuals
items.description: Structural causal bandits use causal knowledge to guide exploration when reward mechanisms are unknown. This paper extends the approach to partially known causal structure, information from other environments, and realizable counterfactual actions.
items.ai_summary: Framework of structural causal bandits that uses partial causal structures, environment information, and counterfactual actions to guide exploration and improve decision-making.

items.title: Where Do Vision-Language Models Get Left and Right? Position-Code Counterfactuals in Qwen2.5-VL, Qwen3-VL and InternVL3
items.description: A vision-language model may take left-right direction from the orientation of image content within patches, its vision transformer's (ViT) position code, or token positions and order in its language model (LLM).
items.ai_summary: Analysis of vision-language models demonstrating that vision transformer position codes are both necessary and largely sufficient for determining left-right spatial orientation.

items.title: HandsOnAid: Building and Evaluating an Offline First-Aid Assistant for Emergency Response Scenarios
items.description: Emergencies can occur where there is no phone signal and no ambulance nearby. A small language model on a phone can be helpful in such situations, but its advice needs to be safe and accurate.
items.ai_summary: HandsOnAid is an offline first-aid assistant built on a fine-tuned 4-bit Gemma 2B model that provides safe and accurate emergency medical guidance without internet connectivity.

items.title: CURRENT: A Recurrent Neural Network for Concurrent Spatial and Temporal Super-Resolution of 4D Flow MRI
items.description: Objective: To improve the spatial and temporal resolution of aortic 4D flow MRI through a unified deep learning framework for post-acquisition super-resolution (SR) of reconstructed velocity vector fields.
items.ai_summary: CURRENT is a recurrent neural network that performs simultaneous spatial and temporal super-resolution on 4D flow MRI velocity vector fields to improve aortic blood flow analysis.

items.title: Can KV Cache Be Reused Across Model Updates? A DeepSeek-V4-Flash Case Study
items.description: Reusing key--value (KV) caches across language model updates could avoid repeated computation of shared context, but changes in model weights raise a fundamental question about what these caches preserve.
items.ai_summary: Study on cross-version key-value cache reuse in language models showing that caches can retain task utility and speed up inference despite underlying weight updates.

items.title: Ontology-Guided Knowledge Graph Construction and Robust Evidence Retrieval for Indian Knowledge Systems
items.description: Retrieving evidence from Indian Knowledge Systems is complicated by transliteration variants, ambiguous names, and relations distributed across passages.

items.title: Structured Confidence Perturbation via Fisher Geometry for Adversarial Training
items.description: A hybrid adversarial training approach combining cross-entropy and KL divergence with geometry-aware perturbations on the confidence manifold improves robustness and transferability by targeting confidence structure deformation.

items.title: Thermodynamics of words

items.title: A Stage-Wise Explainable Pipeline for Arteriolar-to-Venular Ratio Estimation and Retinopathy Screening
