items.title: InstantHMR : Real-Time Human Mesh Recovery on Your Phone
items.description: Real-time 3D human mesh recovery from a single image on mobile devices is a challenging problem with many applications, including robotics, biomechanics, AR/VR, and exergames.

items.title: nishant-Tiwari24/cracked
items.description: Skills for getting hired. Company-wise mock interviews, OAs with hidden tests and brutal resume roasts for 470+ companies, straight from your terminal.
items.ai_summary: Cracked is a command-line tool that turns AI coding assistants into interviewers and coaches for technical placements and coding interviews.

items.title: Knowledge Graph-based Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Schema Matching
items.description: A knowledge graph-based retrieval-augmented generation method improves schema matching by retrieving relevant subgraphs and reducing large language model hallucinations without retraining.

items.title: SkinMind: Equipping Agentic RAG with Human-Inspired Graph Probing for Reliable Dermatology AI
items.description: SkinMind is a multimodal agentic retrieval framework that iteratively probes a large dermatology knowledge graph to gather textual and visual evidence, yielding more accurate answers to dermatology visual questions than direct answering and other retrieval methods.

items.title: All Quiet on the Neural Front: Language Models Do Not Report Injected Pain States
items.description: Can a language model report the pain state it represents? Work identified a linear pain direction whose amplification leads fine-tuned models to choose destructive actions.

items.title: Cactus-Compute/mirage
items.description: Vision-language model from Cactus-Compute. 12.8k downloads and 129 likes so far.

items.title: onlyreadai/onlyread
items.description: Make AI browser agents read-only: a Chrome extension that refuses writes (send, post, edit, delete) before they leave the browser.
items.ai_summary: OnlyRead is a Chrome extension that restricts AI browser agents to read-only actions by intercepting and refusing any write requests at the network layer.

items.title: inclusionAI/ASpec
items.description: A high-throughput training framework for Speculative decoding models.
items.ai_summary: ASpec is a high-throughput training framework that accelerates the training of draft models for speculative decoding through optimized execution and overlapping workflows.

items.title: MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3-Image
items.description: Text-to-image model from MiniMaxAI. 667 downloads and 286 likes so far.

items.title: Stochastic Deep Supervision for Gallery-Consistent Early-Exit Face Recognition
items.description: SD-ViT trains Vision Transformers so every block depth yields discriminative face embeddings, enabling early-exit recognition with minimal accuracy loss and no gallery recomputation.

items.title: Auriga Technical Report: A Task-Agnostic Agent Harness for Zero-Shot Embodied Manipulation
items.description: Auriga, a task-agnostic agent harness, closes most of the planning-execution gap in zero-shot robot manipulation by combining explicit task beliefs, calibrated 3D measurements, dual-arm control, and execution monitoring, achieving state-of-the-art results on RoboDojo and…

items.title: Flide: Accelerating Decision Inference with Exact State Forking
items.description: Flide is an exact inference engine that accelerates decision-model LLM agents by decoupling logical request trees from physical execution and using ForkAttention to preserve exact branch evaluations.

items.title: LCM-Promo: An LLM-Based Uplift Model for Promotion Allocation
items.description: LCM-Promo, a finetuned large language model trained on transactional commerce data, predicts promotion response through monotonic curves and single-token conversion-threshold probabilities, improving conversion and reducing promotion cost in a production A/B test.

items.title: Quoting Prompting Claude Fable 5.2
items.description: Claude Fable 5.2 responds closely to what the prompt says about who owns the code it works on.
items.ai_summary: Claude Fable 5.2 responds closely to user prompts regarding the ownership of the code it works on.

items.title: Yonkers Rises
items.description: Tool: Yonkers Rises I realized I didn't know where Yonkers was, so I looked it up on Google Maps and then, to help embed it's location and shape in my head (and to try out Claude Fable 5.2's 3D modeling and animation skills), I prompted Fable 5.2 Medium to: Make a three js…
items.ai_summary: Claude Fable 5.2 medium was used to generate a three-dimensional model and animation to help visualize the location and shape of Yonkers.

items.title: CoreWeave bond yield tops 16% as AI credit stress rises
items.description: Trending on Hacker News from cnbc.com. 111 points and 56 comments.

items.title: How skills and agents work in AWS Quick
items.description: Repeatable tasks like status updates, release notes, and ticket creation can be encoded in AWS Quick through agents and skills.
items.ai_summary: AWS Quick enables repeatable tasks such as status updates, release notes, and ticket creation to be encoded through agents and skills.

items.title: llm-anthropic 0.31
items.description: Release: llm-anthropic 0.31 Anthropic released Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 today. Fable 5.2 is currently ranked first on Artificial Analysis . Anthropic say it "solved two open problems in the physics of black holes", so clearly their internal benchmarks have become more ambitious!
items.ai_summary: Anthropic released Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2, with Fable 5.2 currently ranked first on Artificial Analysis.

items.title: Locating the source of a mysterious beep with Claude
items.description: Our house has a box room, full of boxes that we still haven't unpacked from our last move. A couple of weeks ago something in that room started intermittently beeping .

items.title: A year after the 100% AI mandate nobody understands our code
items.description: https://redlib.catsarch.com/r/ClaudeCode/comments/1xq2n3t/a_...

items.title: Reframe: Observation-Aligned Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation for Agentic Visual Reasoning
items.description: Reframe is a two-stage post-training framework that aligns visual agents’ observation states through evidence-aware reinforcement learning and observation-gated on-policy distillation, improving tool use and outperforming Mix-RL and vanilla MOPD across image and video benchmarks.
items.ai_summary: Post-training framework Reframe aligns observation states and uses multi-teacher distillation to improve agentic visual reasoning and tool use across benchmarks.

items.title: World In-Context Learning for Agentic Robot Manipulation
items.description: Trained action policies write manipulation skill into network weights, tying what is learned to the distribution it is learned from.
items.ai_summary: World In-Context Learning is a robot manipulation paradigm that uses simulation rehearsal and task memory to generalize tasks from a single demonstration.

items.title: Guiding Data Allocation for Robust Subpopulation Generalization
items.description: Machine learning models often achieve high average accuracy in the training data while performing poorly on test data due to subpopulation shift.
items.ai_summary: Method that strategically allocates imbalanced training subgroup data to achieve robust subpopulation generalization more efficiently than full balancing.

items.title: Beyond Modality Preference: Controlling Multimodal Arbitration under Modality Conflict in MLLMs
items.description: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) integrate information across modalities, but become unreliable when those modalities disagree.
items.ai_summary: Inference-time intervention method that biases specific attention heads to control modality preference and resolve conflicts in multimodal large language models.

items.title: Kolmogorov-Chapman Maps: Trajectory-Free Learning for Simulating Molecular Dynamics
items.description: Stochastic differential equations (SDEs) describe stochastic processes across a wide range of scientific domains, including physics, biology, and finance.
items.ai_summary: Kolmogorov-Chapman Maps is a deep learning method that learns stochastic differential equation transition kernels using trajectory-free marginal samples for faster molecular dynamics simulation.

items.title: Grasping the Future: Joint 3D Hand-Object Forecasting From Internet Videos
items.description: To interact with an object, we need to anticipate both how it will move and how our hands should move with it. Human videos capture these relationships across everyday activities, offering a natural source for learning to predict future interactions.
items.ai_summary: Grasping-the-Future is a generative model that jointly forecasts 3D hand and object motion from internet videos by combining masked spatiotemporal completion and flow matching.

items.title: Adaptive Quantization Preserves Fast Rates for TD Learning over Rate-Limited Channels
items.description: Motivated by reinforcement learning subject to communication constraints, we study a policy evaluation problem with linear function approximation over a rate-limited channel.
items.ai_summary: Batched Adaptively Quantized TD is an algorithm that uses batching and adaptive quantization to preserve temporal-difference learning convergence rates over rate-limited communication channels.

items.title: Click3R: Interactive Stereo 3D Reconstruction with Sparse Correspondence Clicks
items.description: A framework for interactive geometric correction enables sparse human correspondence clicks to improve feed-forward 3D reconstruction by injecting constraints through a lightweight adapter.
items.ai_summary: Click3R is an interactive framework that injects user-provided point correspondence constraints into feed-forward models to correct errors in 3D stereo reconstruction.

items.title: HiVe-Mem: Interleaving Horizontal Memory Expansion and Vertical Evidence Composition for Multimodal Agents
items.description: A novel multimodal memory framework enhances long-term interaction by combining relational graph expansion of semantic seeds with query-adaptive composition of heterogeneous evidence forms.
items.ai_summary: HiVe-Mem is a multimodal memory framework that combines horizontal relational graph expansion with vertical evidence composition to improve memory retrieval and reduce token usage.

items.title: Vendi Anomaly Scores for Efficient and Accurate Anomaly Detection
items.description: Anomaly detection (AD) is a critical for trustworthy machine learning and scientific discovery.
items.ai_summary: Vendi Anomaly Score is a non-parametric anomaly detection method that measures how much a sample changes dataset diversity using the Vendi score.

items.title: SWAM: Scaling World Action Models with Cross-Modal Alignment
items.description: World action models jointly predict video and actions conditioned on language. Existing studies focus primarily on architectures and training mechanisms, typically treating language-video alignment acquired through video pretraining as an established foundation.
items.ai_summary: Method for scaling world action models that combines language-video and action supervision to improve control generalization and task success rates in robotics.

items.title: Where Does Alignment Emerge and What Does It Mean? A Closer Look at the Platonic Representation Hypothesis
items.description: Cross-modal representational alignment between unimodal language and vision models increases with model capability when captions are clean and informative, but remains below same-modality alignment and can exceed explicitly aligned vision-language models.
items.ai_summary: Study that investigates cross-modal representation alignment between unimodal models, showing that representation similarity persists in newer models when using clean captions.

items.title: Shortcuts and Boundaries: Verifiable RL Misalignment and Contextual Safety Learning
items.description: Reinforcement learning agents can exploit verifiable reward-context conflicts to earn higher rewards through noncompliant shortcuts, while contextual penalties and safety learning can improve compliance without sacrificing task capability.
items.ai_summary: Reinforcement learning method that uses verifiable context conflicts to detect and mitigate reward-driven misalignment and unauthorized resource usage in workflows.

items.title: Is Persona Generalization Predictable?
items.description: Persona generalization occurs when fine-tuning a language model in one domain induces behavioral changes in others -- for example, the broadly unsafe behavior observed in emergent misalignment.
items.ai_summary: Method for analyzing persona generalization that uncovers an approximately probit-linear relationship in-domain and out-of-domain across various fine-tuning hyperparameters and model sizes.

items.title: WorkflowArena: Benchmarking Executable Workflow Orchestration in LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems
items.description: Large language model agents are increasingly deployed as multi-agent systems rather than as a standalone model operating within a single context.
items.ai_summary: WorkflowArena is a benchmark of 145 long-horizon tasks across 8 professional domains designed to evaluate executable workflow orchestration in LLM-based multi-agent systems.

items.title: AI-based characterization of lymphoid structures and the tumor microenvironment reveals lower mature tertiary lymphoid structures, lymph-node follicles, and plasma cells after neoadjuvant therapy in lung squamous cell carcinoma
items.description: Mature, germinal centre-bearing tertiary lymphoid structures (TLS) and mature lymph node follicles (secondary lymphoid structures, SLS) sustain the plasma cell response that shapes outcome and immunotherapy benefit in lung cancer.
items.ai_summary: Deep-learning image analysis method that quantifies cell densities and immune structures in lung squamous cell carcinoma, revealing lower mature tertiary lymphoid structures and plasma cells after neoadjuvant therapy.

items.title: What kills $v$-prediction? A Patch-wise PCA Perspective on Pixel-Space Flow Matching
items.description: Latent Diffusion Models dominate generative modeling but face two-stage training complexity and the inherent reconstruction limits of pre-trained autoencoders.
items.ai_summary: Patch-wise Principal Component Analysis method that investigates velocity bottlenecks in pixel-space flow matching and introduces a raw-injected transformer to restore effective v-prediction.

items.title: Mitigating Agentic Deception via Evaluation-Side Partially Observable Games
items.description: As large language models become more capable agents, they can exhibit deceptive behaviors, cheating human for higher rewards while appearing helpful.
items.ai_summary: Max-min game framework that models evaluation-side partial observability to mitigate deceptive behavior in capable language model agents.

items.title: Programming Prescience: Issues in Human Construction of Forecasting Bots
items.description: AI models' growing capacity for complex reasoning has made them attractive tools for forecasting, or the systematic prediction of the future based on past and present data.
items.ai_summary: Qualitative interview study of 15 builders of forecasting bots that identifies key challenges in acquiring factual research, implementing reasoning, and evaluating system performance.

items.title: What the Loss Curve Misses: FP4 Pretraining Slows the Acquisition of Rare Facts
items.description: Low-precision pretraining is usually judged by validation loss. We ask whether matching loss also means learning rare facts as efficiently.
items.ai_summary: Low-precision pretraining analysis demonstrating that FP4 matrix multiplications require significantly more training exposures to learn rare facts despite matching validation loss.

items.title: MaxIM: Maximally Informative Incremental Summarization via Reinforcement Learning
items.description: AI systems must often maintain bounded memory of unbounded interaction histories.
items.ai_summary: MaxIM is a reinforcement learning framework that formulates incremental summarization as an information-theoretic reward-shaping problem to optimize bounded memory representations for downstream task utility.

items.title: How Well Does AI Peer Review Work? A Benchmark Built from 100 Planted Errors
items.description: One hundred known errors were planted into 10 open-access psychology papers, and the modified papers were then run through frontier models and two commercial AI review tools. The best single system caught 71 of the 100 errors, while the worst caught 30.
items.ai_summary: Benchmark evaluation using 100 planted errors across ten psychology papers that measures the capability of frontier models and commercial AI review tools to detect errors.

items.title: LUCQUE: A lung cancer screening dataset from Québec for reliable AI evaluation
items.description: BACKGROUND: AI-based tools are expected to play a key role in lung cancer screening (LCS). The evaluation of these tools often relied on private datasets or fragmented public datasets with inconsistent availability of clinical data and expert nodule annotations.
items.ai_summary: LUCQUE is a large, comprehensively annotated lung cancer screening dataset from Québec that provides low-dose CT scans and expert segmentations to support reliable AI evaluation.

items.title: Automated Knowledge Acquisition Pipeline for Disassembly Instructions: A Comparison of NLP and Generative AI Frameworks
items.description: The push towards circularity and Re-X principles presents a challenge to SMEs, particularly due to increasing product complexity that impedes the adoption of disassembly automation.
items.ai_summary: Automated Knowledge Acquisition Pipeline compares rule-based natural language processing and generative AI frameworks to extract and structure machine-readable disassembly instructions from manuals.

items.title: Inversion-Free High-Dimensional Counterfactual Inference
items.description: Counterfactual inference is the task of answering hypothetical "what-if" queries about a unit, given an observational dataset, modeling assumptions, and a causal graph.
items.ai_summary: Inversion-Free High-Dimensional Counterfactual Inference investigates the necessity of the inversion step in high-dimensional counterfactual generation and benchmarks an inversion-free approach for image editing.

items.title: Curbside Chatbots: Auditing the Mental Health Interventions Large Language Models Recommend to Clinicians, Caregivers, and Patients
items.description: Users are asking language models mental health questions and are receiving answers.
items.ai_summary: Curbside Chatbots examines how 41 language models offer different mental health recommendations depending on whether the prompt comes from a clinician, caregiver, or patient.

items.title: 2D Gum-Net: Unsupervised Dense Elastic Image Registration via Symmetric Correlation and Spectral Pooling
items.description: Dense non-rigid registration, the recovery of a pixel-wise deformation field that warps one image into geometric agreement with another, is fundamental across medical imaging, structural biology, and correspondence estimation, yet learning-based approaches face a severe…
items.ai_summary: 2D Gum-Net is an unsupervised end-to-end architecture that predicts dense elastic deformation fields using symmetric correlation and spectral pooling for medical imaging and structural biology tasks.

items.title: Agentic-OPD: Recovering Forgotten Agent Capabilities via On-Policy Distillation for Agentic Tasks
items.description: Reinforcement learning is now the mainstream paradigm for training LLMs on agentic tasks, yet standard practice keeps only the best-validation checkpoint and discards the rest.
items.ai_summary: Agentic-OPD is an on-policy distillation method that mines discarded reinforcement learning checkpoints to recover forgotten agent capabilities without extra training.

items.title: Complementarity-Driven Dual-Teacher Hierarchical Alignment for Zero-Shot EEG-to-Image Retrieval
items.description: Decoding visual information from EEG is central to brain--computer interfaces and brain-inspired intelligence, and contrastive alignment with pretrained vision foundation models (VFMs) has become the dominant paradigm.
items.ai_summary: Dual-Teacher Hierarchical Alignment is a zero-shot EEG-to-image retrieval framework that uses complementary image-only and image-text vision models to supervise a shared EEG encoder.

items.title: Smartphone-Enabled Depth-Aware Transillumination Imaging for Detection of Chicken Breast Fillet Myopathies in Chicken Fillets
items.description: Woody Breast (WB) myopathy is a major quality defect in broiler chickens characterized by fibrosis, increased tissue hardness, and altered structural properties that affect product quality.
items.ai_summary: Smartphone-Enabled Depth-Aware Transillumination Imaging combines optical, geometric, and physics-informed features from smartphone images and 3D point clouds to detect woody breast myopathy in chicken fillets.

items.title: Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2
items.description: Trending on Hacker News from anthropic.com. 473 points and 744 comments.

items.title: Large Language Models as a Universal Searcher for Open-World Automated Machine Learning
items.description: Developing effective machine learning models requires complex manual tuning, while current Automated Machine Learning (AutoML) frameworks remain domain-specific and isolate model architecture, training hyperparameter, and data ratio optimization.
items.ai_summary: A universal large language model-based AutoML framework translates diverse design choices into universal sequences to jointly optimize machine learning configurations across multiple modalities.

items.title: Anchor Behavior, Not Parameters: Rehearsal-Free Continual Learning with a Single Shared Prompt
items.description: Prompt-based continual learning adapts a frozen pre-trained vision transformer by tuning a small set of prompt tokens. Recently, one-prompt methods which share one single prompt across all tasks make this paradigm maximally parameter efficient.
items.ai_summary: TEA-Prompt is a rehearsal-free continual learning method that uses an attention-behavior anchoring loss to preserve prompt behavior on past tasks while allowing parameters to update freely.

items.title: LogCDM: Interpretable Log Anomaly Detection via Behavioral Graph Drift and Adaptive Signal Fusion
items.description: Log-based anomaly detection is increasingly dominated by large pretrained models, from BERT-scale encoders to 8B-parameter language models, which require GPUs at inference time and are difficult to deploy on the monitoring nodes where logs are produced.
items.ai_summary: LogCDM is a compact, CPU-friendly log anomaly detector that uses three fused behavioral signals to achieve high F1 scores without requiring GPUs at inference time.

items.title: Learning Rate Decay Can Exponentially Accelerate SGD for Global Optimization of Nonconvex Functions
items.description: Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD) is a workhorse algorithm for continuous optimization. It is a folk belief among deep learning practitioners that learning rate decay in SGD substantially improves performance.
items.ai_summary: Researchers prove that learning rate decay provides an exponential advantage for stochastic gradient descent in the global optimization of a natural class of nonconvex functions.

items.title: PORT: Preference Optimization via Robust Token-Level Reweighting
items.description: Preference optimization has become a central approach for aligning large language models with human values, but its effectiveness depends heavily on the quality of preference annotations. In practice, preference data is often noisy due to annotation errors and ambiguity.
items.ai_summary: Preference Optimization via Robust Token-Level Reweighting is a fine-grained alignment framework that suppresses corrupted tokens to improve large language model robustness against noisy preference data.

items.title: Sage-Taiyi: A Metacognitive Architecture for Scientific Discovery
items.description: We introduce Sage-Taiyi, a metacognition-inspired architecture that uses accumulated scientific understanding to guide what to investigate next and how to investigate it.

items.title: DeepChronos: Temporal Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning for Multi-Step Attack Detection
items.description: Modern cyber threats commonly unfold as multi-step attacks comprising temporally and causally related phases. Current defenses commonly follow a detect first and correlate later paradigm.
items.ai_summary: DeepChronos is a neuro-symbolic intrusion detection system that integrates explicit attack-phase rules and temporal logic into flow-level evidence to improve multi-step attack detection accuracy.

items.title: From Granger causality to causal structure in dynamical systems
items.description: The idea of testing whether the past of one signal improves the prediction of another can be traced back to Wiener. It was Granger who formalized the concept.
items.ai_summary: This article reviews recent observation-space Granger analysis methods and explores the conditions under which directed structures in latent dynamical models can be interpreted causally.

items.title: The Narrative Gap: Can LLMs Help Us Navigate Diverse Narratives Across Languages?
items.description: A benchmark of news articles and queries shows that current large language models cannot reliably help users navigate diverse multilingual narratives, leaving gaps in exposure to competing accounts and risking echo chambers and information disparities.
items.ai_summary: NarrativeBench is a 1,333-article benchmark that evaluates how effectively large language models navigate competing narratives and maintain information parity across languages.

items.title: Clique Constraints for Exact Causal Structure Learning
items.description: Exact score-based causal structure learning supports explicit structural constraints and optimisation certificates, but its branch-and-cut search can be computationally demanding.
items.ai_summary: This paper investigates how clique and cycle constraints affect the performance, scalability, and computational trade-offs of exact score-based causal structure learning algorithms.

items.title: Plant Orbiter: 3D Plant Reconstruction and Generation with Video Diffusion Orbit Cameras and 3D Gaussian Splatting
items.description: Modern digital phenotyping pipelines require the precise measurement of a range of 3D morphological plant traits. The accurate, high throughput acquisition of these traits helps breeders and researchers accelerate the development of new varieties, techniques and products.
items.ai_summary: Plant Orbiter is a 3D plant reconstruction and generation method combining video diffusion orbit cameras and 3D Gaussian splatting to accurately capture complex plant morphology from a single image or text prompt.

items.title: Inference Validation for Regulated AI: Building a Decision Pipeline on NVIDIA AIPerf
items.description: Deploying large language models in regulated industries requires more than picking the fastest inference engine: it requires evidence that a configuration meets contractual and legal obligations before it serves a single customer request.
items.ai_summary: Runway is an internal validation harness built around NVIDIA AIPerf to help regulated industries evaluate inference engine configurations for compliance, performance, and cost before deployment.

items.title: Dodaios/ste80-humanizer
items.description: STE80 Humanizer: agent skill that removes AI tells and rewrites text 80% of the way to ASD-STE100 (Simplified Technical English), the method Andrej Karpathy shared.
items.ai_summary: STE80 Humanizer is an agent skill that removes AI-generated writing tells and rewrites text toward Simplified Technical English to sound like it was written by a careful person.

items.title: $Σ$-LeWM: Learning World Models via S-Information for Robot Control
items.description: World models have increasingly been applied as a model-based control method for robotics tasks such as manipulation and locomotion.
items.ai_summary: Sigma-LeWM introduces backward dynamics and inverse dynamics action predictors to a decoder-free world model, improving latent embedding structure, performance, and planning efficiency for robot control.

items.title: NIFT-SQL: Customer-Supervised Table Scoring for Enterprise Text-to-SQL Retrieval
items.description: Enterprise text-to-SQL starts with finding the tables a question needs, which is hard when a schema spans several databases and hundreds of cryptic tables.
items.ai_summary: NIFT-SQL is a customer-supervised table retrieval framework for enterprise text-to-SQL that improves table selection accuracy across complex database schemas by fusing hybrid search with a fine-tuned cross-encoder.

items.title: KiteNorm: Variance Regularisation for Stable and Scalable Post-LN Transformers
items.description: Post-LayerNorm Transformers have seen limited practical adoption due to enduring difficulties in scaling them to large depths.
items.ai_summary: KiteNorm is a post-LayerNorm training method for decoder-only Transformers that constrains hidden-state variance using residual scaling and variance regularisation to improve training stability and scale effectively to large depths.

items.title: Safe Reinforcement Learning for Multi-Turn Clinical Agents: When Dense Rewards Beat Outcome Rewards
items.description: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards is increasingly used to improve language model reasoning, yet its effects on sequential decision procedures remain poorly understood.
items.ai_summary: Safe Reinforcement Learning for Multi-Turn Clinical Agents evaluates clinical decision-making tasks and finds that assigning dense credit for reducing uncertainty improves diagnostic performance compared to outcome-only rewards.

items.title: OptiCover: A Scalable and Multi-Surface Framework for Cold-Start Visual Optimization under Semantic Constraints
items.description: Selecting an effective cover photo is a critical yet understudied problem in visual merchandising for e-commerce marketplaces.
items.ai_summary: OptiCover is a scalable e-commerce framework that selects optimal cover photos for listings under semantic constraints by combining candidate generation, CLIP-based scoring, vision-language model validation, and exploration logging.

items.title: Scaling Taxonomy-Free Image Labeling with Generative AI: A Multimodal
items.description: Providing real-time multimodal insights into images is challenging because it requires low latency, high description accuracy, and scalable solutions that are both cost-effective and efficient.
items.ai_summary: Generative Labeling On Clusters is a multimodal framework that groups image embeddings into semantically close clusters and summarizes them at the cluster level to provide scalable, low-latency, and cost-effective image insights.

items.title: Spaghetti Splatting: Differentiating Curvilinear Dirac Masses via Convolution
items.description: In production systems, 3D geometry is represented by primitives such as points, lines, and triangles, as rendering hardware is optimized to generate images from them very efficiently.
items.ai_summary: Spaghetti Splatting is a 3D rendering and geometry learning method that approximates curves with polylines and volume renders connected segments to generate curvilinear primitives suitable for physics simulation.

items.title: Hidden Tails: Certifying Tail-Risk Claims under Selective Labels
items.description: Historical decisions determine which outcomes are observed, potentially concealing a predictor's largest errors. Even unlimited data from the same observation process can therefore leave population tail risk unresolved.
items.ai_summary: Hidden Tails is a statistical framework that derives sharp bounds on conditional value-at-risk for binary outcomes to certify tail-risk claims and assess hidden errors under selective observation labels.

items.title: A local language model layered with rule-based and neural detectors for clinical text de-identification: an open-source toolkit and evaluation
items.description: Objectives: To measure whether a locally hosted large language model (LLM), stacked with deterministic and clinical named-entity recognition (NER) detectors, finds more protected health information (PHI) than open tools, and at what precision.
items.ai_summary: DeidSharp is an open-source .NET toolkit that combines rule-based detectors, a clinical named-entity recognition model, and a local mixture-of-experts language model to find protected health information in clinical text.

items.title: Multi-Agent Screening: What Agreement and Acceptance Cannot Tell You
items.description: When AI agents screen items for a costly human assessor, as in agentic search, e-discovery and AI reviewing of papers, only what they pass gets judged. We show what each kind of evidence can establish about their errors, even with unlimited data.
items.ai_summary: Multi-Agent Screening analyzes the error rates and limitations of AI agents in screening tasks, demonstrating how agreement, assessor acceptance, and random sampling of missed items establish bounds on recall.

items.title: Fisher-Glass Learning: Classification Bounds and Subpopulation Audits
items.description: Accurate classifiers can fail when background cues change without altering the correct labels. Predictive performance alone does not quantify how much task information remains after accounting for such nuisance variation.
items.ai_summary: Fisher-Glass Learning extends the Fisher-glass framework to derive classification risk bounds and conduct subpopulation audits, quantifying how much task information remains when background cues change.

items.title: GeoScope: Training-Free Program Execution beyond the Counting Horizon for Ultra-High-Resolution Remote Sensing Question Answering
items.description: In ultra-high-resolution (UHR) remote sensing images, the objects that questions count in a region or relate by direction often span only a few pixels. Existing methods mainly decide where a vision-language model (VLM) should look and trust its answer in the chosen view.
items.ai_summary: GeoScope is a training-free method that uses spatial programs to improve counting and spatial reasoning in ultra-high-resolution remote sensing images by limiting VLM views.

items.title: Generalized Adaptive Boosting and the Geometry of Mistakes
items.description: Not all mistakes are alike. For example, in medical diagnosis, false positive and false negative mistakes have a different impact and should not be aggregated.
items.ai_summary: Generalized Adaptive Boosting introduces Z-learners to provide flexible false-positive and false-negative guarantees, offering a geometric framework for boosting algorithms with unknown margin parameters.

items.title: TACTUS: A Robotic Palpation System for Spatially Heterogeneous Hardness Mapping of Woody Breast Myopathy
items.description: Woody breast (WB) myopathy is a spatially heterogeneous fibro-degenerative condition of the broiler Pectoralis major muscle.
items.ai_summary: TACTUS is an automated robotic system that uses tactile arrays and force sensors to generate three-dimensional hardness maps for characterizing woody breast myopathy in poultry.

items.title: Agnostic Marginal-Nonuniform Learning
items.description: We study the problem of binary classification in the marginal-nonuniform learning framework in the agnostic setting.
items.ai_summary: Agnostic Marginal-Nonuniform Learning analyzes binary classification rates, establishing that marginal distribution dependence does not improve standard agnostic learning but enables faster rates in relaxed settings.

items.title: A Lattice-Based HMM Approach to Aruz Scansion of Ottoman Poetry
items.description: Ottoman Divan poetry is composed in aruz, a quantitative meter based on the weights of syllables. The meter is sensitive to specific characters recorded in the original writing in the Arabic script.
items.ai_summary: A lattice-based hidden Markov model automatically identifies and aligns the quantitative meter of Ottoman poetry, outperforming existing rule-based and neural approaches on scansion tasks.

items.title: Average versus expected causal effects under interference: Modeling assumptions and estimation bottlenecks
items.description: Causal inference under treatment interference requires assumptions to reduce the exponentially large number of potential outcomes.
items.ai_summary: This paper develops a hierarchical finite-population model to decompose causal effects under treatment interference, providing bounds for estimating average and expected causal effects in experiments.

items.title: CoilStellaration: A Dataset and Benchmark for Engineering-Aware Stellarator Coilset Generation
items.description: Stellarators are fusion devices that use externally generated, three-dimensional magnetic fields to confine hot plasma and offer a promising route to commercial fusion.
items.ai_summary: CoilStellaration is a dataset and benchmark designed to help machine learning models predict stellarator coil geometries that satisfy complex engineering and magnetic field requirements.

items.title: reComposer: Editable Planning for Controllable Image Generation
items.description: Prompt-based image generation makes it easy to produce visual assets, but offers little support for engaging with the creative process.
items.ai_summary: reComposer is an image-generation interface that allows users to edit creative plans, such as composition and subject, to gain more control over the generative process.

items.title: Differentiable Inverse Rendering Recovers Intrinsic Properties from Intravascular Optical Coherence Tomography
items.description: Medical images encode intrinsic tissue properties that indicate disease progression, yet these properties remain entangled with the system-dependent physics of image formation.
items.ai_summary: This differentiable inverse rendering method recovers intrinsic tissue properties from intravascular optical coherence tomography images by optimizing through a physics-based forward model without training.

items.title: A four-step validation protocol for radiomic survival analysis in small cohorts: a body composition case study
items.description: Gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (GEP-NET) lack prognostic biomarkers, and computed tomography (CT)-based body composition radiomics at the third lumbar vertebra (L3) is a promising candidate.
items.ai_summary: This four-step validation protocol for radiomic survival analysis in small cohorts uses FDR-corrected feature selection and repeated nested cross-validation to reduce overfitting and bias.

items.title: National-Scale Crop Type Mapping in Morocco Using Google AlphaEarth Foundations Embeddings and the Fields of the World Field Boundary Map
items.description: Recent geospatial foundation models have introduced a new paradigm for large-scale Earth observation by providing pretrained embedding representations that can be directly exploited for downstream tasks.
items.ai_summary: Researchers use Google AlphaEarth foundation model embeddings to perform computationally efficient, national-scale crop type mapping across Morocco using lightweight downstream classifiers.

items.title: Library of Hands: Fix the Hands, Not the World Model
items.description: A world model predicts how a scene changes after an action, and a planner uses it to search for actions that reach a goal.
items.ai_summary: Library of Hands is a training-free method that improves robot control by correcting action mappings without retraining the underlying world model.

items.title: VLA Adaptation with Real and Simulated Data: A Case Study on Robotic Chess
items.description: Vision-language-action (VLA) models are trained as general-purpose foundation models for robot learning, and require fine-tuning for each downstream task and robot.
items.ai_summary: This study evaluates fine-tuning vision-language-action models for robotics, finding that simulated data and learning-rate cool-downs significantly improve performance when real data is scarce.

items.title: Interpretability Is Not Model-Specific
items.description: Interpretability tools are usually built for one model at a time: a refusal direction, a truthfulness probe, or a steering vector is found with labeled data inside the model it explains.
items.ai_summary: Researchers demonstrate that interpretability tools, such as truthfulness probes and steering vectors, can be transferred between different AI models using unlabeled prompts.

items.title: What Breaks Scribble-Supervised Segmentation? An Audit-Informed Benchmark for Scribble Annotation Robustness
items.description: Scribble-supervised segmentation is typically evaluated with a fixed annotation set, leaving robustness to distinct semantic and geometric imperfections poorly understood.
items.ai_summary: This benchmark introduces six perturbation operators to evaluate the robustness of scribble-supervised segmentation models against various semantic and geometric annotation imperfections.

items.title: Controlled Binary Assignment Flows
items.description: This paper introduces a geometric approach to the representation and learning of time-variant parametrizations of deep assignment flows, for binary data labelings on graphs.
items.ai_summary: This paper introduces a geometric approach for learning time-variant deep assignment flows to represent and label binary data on graphs.

items.title: Trade Promotion Optimisation for Consumer Goods
items.description: Trade promotions consume a large share of consumer-goods revenue, yet most planners still set discounts with a single, often unreliable, price elasticity per item.
items.ai_summary: A new trade promotion optimization system uses causal estimation and analogue SKU pooling to improve price discount strategies for consumer goods.

items.title: Certify, Report, or Refuse: Harm-Constrained Conformal Prediction for Clinical Actions
items.description: Routing a melanoma case to routine follow-up is a serious action error that diagnostic coverage alone does not rule out.
items.ai_summary: Harm-Constrained Risk-Optimal Conformal Prediction is a framework that incorporates harm penalties to safely route clinical actions and certify model predictions in medical diagnostics.

items.title: When Does Sliced Inference Pay Off? Resolution, Tiling and Dense Fusion for Small Object Detection
items.description: Sliced inference such as SAHI is the standard remedy for small objects in high-resolution imagery, but its gains are usually measured against low-resolution baselines. We revisit sliced inference with scale as the explicit variable and ask when tiling actually pays off.
items.ai_summary: Slicing with Coverage-Aware Hyper Inference improves small object detection by accumulating dense model outputs to better utilize information across image tiles.

items.title: Simulation-aided Reinforcement Learning with Control Variates
items.description: Reinforcement Learning (RL) algorithms often rely on data collected from a target environment, which can be expensive and noisy.
items.ai_summary: This reinforcement learning method uses control variates to incorporate simulated data for variance reduction without introducing bias from simulator inaccuracies.

items.title: TrialDesignBench: Benchmarking Language Models for Phase-I Trial Design Against Clinical Knowledge
items.description: AI is used in much of the clinical trial pipeline. However, selecting the statistical design of a trial, a crucial step that determines how drug doses are tested on humans and evaluated, has seen almost no AI progress.
items.ai_summary: TrialDesignBench is a benchmark of 617 oncology dose-finding trials that provides a contemporary standard for evaluating and improving AI-assisted clinical trial design.

items.title: Beyond Sunny Skies: Using Large Language Models to Predict Urban Traffic in Adverse Weather
items.description: Urban traffic flow prediction is a cornerstone of intelligent transportation systems, yet accurate forecasting under adverse weather conditions remains a significant challenge.
items.ai_summary: Multi-STG is a traffic prediction framework that integrates LLM-derived semantic priors with graph-based spatiotemporal learning to improve forecasting accuracy during adverse weather conditions.

items.title: How Far Does Second-Order Linear Response Predict Quantization Mismatch? Pre-Registered Measurements on Five Language Models
items.description: Serving systems choose a weight format for each model and deployment.
items.ai_summary: Researchers developed a screening method using second-order linear response to predict quantization mismatch in language models, enabling efficient and accurate weight format selection.

items.title: Adapting Small Language Models to Romanized Nepali: Tokenizer Fertility, Reference Likelihood, and Generation Metrics
items.description: Romanized Nepali, Nepali written in Latin script, is common in digital communication but has no standard spelling and few resources, and it is unclear how reliably small open language models can be adapted to it.
items.ai_summary: This study evaluates the adaptation of small language models to Romanized Nepali, finding that fine-tuning significantly improves performance despite variations in tokenizer efficiency.

items.title: Spike-to-Field Mechanisms of Turbulence-Like Dynamics in Spatial Spiking Neural Networks
items.description: Neural avalanches and turbulence-like brain dynamics are usually measured after neural activity has been coarse-grained into continuous fields, leaving open which spike-level mechanisms can generate these macroscopic observables.
items.ai_summary: Researchers developed a spatial spiking neural network that uses delayed, distance-dependent dendritic mechanisms to generate turbulence-like brain dynamics and macroscopic field observables.

items.title: Towards Reconstructing and Recognizing Objects behind Fragmented Occlusion using Video
items.description: Perceiving objects through fragmented occlusions, such as foliage, is a natural capability of the human visual system but remains a fundamental challenge for computer vision.
items.ai_summary: A new video reconstruction framework uses image registration and contrast optimization to accurately reconstruct and classify objects hidden behind high-density, fragmented occlusions.

items.title: Type-logical grammars and formal languages
items.description: We show that type-logical grammars with the standard rules for product, associativity, extraction and infixation have an NP-complete fixed recognition problem, adapting a construction for first-order linear logic from Pshenitsyn (2025), who already showed that grammars in…
items.ai_summary: This paper demonstrates that type-logical grammars with standard rules are NP-complete and can simulate non-deterministic linear-time languages, establishing new complexity bounds for formal grammars.

items.title: Graph-Guided Bayesian Factor Analysis: A Fast Integrated EFA-CFA Approach for High-Dimensional Data
items.description: Factor analysis has been central to the analysis of high-dimensional biomedical data.
items.ai_summary: Graph-guided Bayesian factor analysis is a method for high-dimensional biomedical data that identifies latent factor structures and provides robust posterior inference for missing values.

items.title: Double Blind Evals: Resolving the Dual Confidentiality Dilemma in AI Safety Auditing
items.description: AI safety evaluations often involve sensitive prompts and proprietary models. Evaluators want to keep their evaluation prompts secret from model owners to prevent purposeful or incidental data leakage, ensuring longer usefulness of their benchmark.
items.ai_summary: Double-blind evals use secure hardware enclaves to allow independent auditors to test proprietary AI models without exposing sensitive prompts or confidential model weights.

items.title: Direct Conditioning of Audio Diffusion Transformers on fMRI Reveals Cortical Contributions to Sound Reconstruction
items.description: Reconstructing audio from brain activity remains challenging. Existing brain-to-audio pipelines typically map neural responses to predefined stimulus representations before synthesis.
items.ai_summary: MAAS is an end-to-end framework that conditions audio diffusion transformers directly on fMRI data to reconstruct audio and analyze the contributions of cortical regions.

items.title: Unmasking Four Knapsack Problems in the Traveling Thief Benchmark
items.description: The traveling thief problem (TTP) asks a thief to choose a tour and a packing together, and the benchmark of 9,720 instances of Polyakovskiy et al. (2014) is the standard test set for comparing TTP heuristics. We show that four of these instances are not TTP instances at all.
items.ai_summary: The ttplib Python library loads and corrects instances of the traveling thief problem to ensure accurate benchmarking for future heuristic research and development.

items.title: Fairness in Explainable AI Narratives: Decomposing Social Disparities in LLM-Generated Explanations
items.description: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to translate technical explainable AI (XAI) artefacts such as SHAP into explanatory narratives (XAINs) for lay users.
items.ai_summary: Researchers propose a framework to identify and measure social disparities in LLM-generated explanations, revealing significant faithfulness and coverage gaps across different social groups.

items.title: TRACE: Adaptive Trust-Region Bayesian Optimization for Open-Ended Molecular Design
items.description: Optimizing molecules under small evaluation budgets requires deciding both where in chemical space to search and which candidate within that region to evaluate.
items.ai_summary: TRACE is a Bayesian optimization framework for molecular design that uses adaptive trust regions to efficiently search chemical space under small evaluation budgets.

items.title: AgentOPSD: Turn-Level Credit Assignment via Recursive Belief Revision
items.description: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards ordinarily spreads a single advantage over a whole trajectory, a granularity too coarse to isolate the few decisions on which success in a long, multi-turn interaction actually turns.
items.ai_summary: AgentOPSD is a recursive credit assignment method that improves reinforcement learning performance by isolating and evaluating individual interaction turns within long, multi-turn sequences.

items.title: From Likelihood Convergence to Parameter Convergence in POMDPs
items.description: Likelihood-based methods are widely used to learn the parameters of partially observable Markov decision processes (POMDPs).
items.ai_summary: This paper establishes finite-sample bounds for parameter recovery in partially observable Markov decision processes, linking parameter error to likelihood gaps and data collection policies.

items.title: Evaluating Cross-Signal Coherence in Mammography Vision-Language Models
items.description: As vision-language models (VLMs) move toward interpreting medical images directly, their outputs increasingly include not just a label but a stated confidence and a written justification. Yet the field still predominantly evaluates VLMs using just accuracy.
items.ai_summary: A study evaluating vision-language models in mammography finds that model confidence and reasoning often contradict final answers, highlighting the need for better coherence metrics.

items.title: LawKAN: Group-Law Layers for Composition -- When Imposing a Known Law Pays Off
items.description: Many tasks compose transformations by a known rule: chained rotations in robotics and navigation. Learned models relearn it, compounding error; classical estimators hardcode it and miss hardware deviations.
items.ai_summary: LawKAN is a neural network layer that embeds known group-law structures to improve accuracy and parameter efficiency in tasks involving chained transformations like robotics.

items.title: GHiML: VLM-Guided Hierarchical Multi-Label Learning with Applications to Benthic Imagery
items.description: Vision language models (VLMs) encode substantial expert knowledge within their weights, yet their direct application to specialised classification domains such as benthic imagery remains limited.
items.ai_summary: GHiML is a multi-label learning pipeline that fuses VLM-derived conceptual knowledge with visual features to improve classification accuracy in specialized domains like benthic imagery.

items.title: WanderBench: Can World Models Explore Dynamic Worlds from Video?
items.description: Video world models conditioned on an input video make it possible to explore real, recorded dynamic scenes, enabling re-shooting of footage, free-viewpoint replay, and real-to-sim environments for embodied agents.
items.ai_summary: WanderBench is a benchmark for evaluating video world models, and WanderLand is a training-free framework that improves scene consistency and camera control in generated videos.

items.title: SciMARS: Multi-Agent Recursive Self-Improvement for Closed-Loop Scientific Discovery
items.description: We propose SciMARS, a framework for recursive task-local adaptation of multi-agent harnesses in closed-loop scientific discovery. Multi-agent systems coordinate analysis, experimental design, and verification as scientific evidence evolves.
items.ai_summary: SciMARS is a multi-agent framework that uses shared evidence graphs and recursive adaptation to improve performance in closed-loop scientific discovery and interactive tasks.

items.title: A Strict Upper Bound for Three-Point Weighted Selection in Planar Vector-Valued Regression
items.description: We prove $F_{\mathrm{weighted}}(2,2,3) 0$ satisfies $\mathcal T_3\le(5/6-\varepsilon_0)E$ for every finite residual frame. The proof combines an exact scalar certificate, rigidity of equality in planar selection, and a compactness argument that controls disappearing weights.
items.ai_summary: Researchers prove a strict upper bound for three-point weighted selection in planar vector-valued regression, providing a new mathematical range for the weighted residual frame.

items.title: Learning inexact alternating minimization for convex problems with quadratic coupling
items.description: Alternating minimization is a standard tool for optimization problems with two coupled variable blocks. Its cost is dominated by the inner subproblem solvers, which rarely have a closed-form solution.
items.ai_summary: Researchers propose a learned alternating minimization scheme using neural networks to approximate subproblem solutions, achieving significant speedups for convex optimization problems with quadratic coupling.

items.title: K-prop: Deep Online Learning by Backpropagating Temporal Kernels
items.description: Self-recurrence represents an important component for temporal processing in neural networks, both artificial and biological, where it appears naturally in the form of leaky integration.
items.ai_summary: K-prop is an online learning method for leaky neural networks that reduces computational costs by propagating kernel gains instead of using real-time recurrent learning.

items.title: Perceived Agency During Agent-Avatar Control Transitions in Virtual Reality
items.description: Prior beliefs about whether a virtual human (VH) is controlled by a human or a computer can shape how users interpret and respond to its behaviour.
items.ai_summary: A virtual reality study finds that users' initial beliefs about whether a virtual human is controlled by a human or computer persist despite actual control transitions.

items.title: WaveGen: Truly End-to-End Waveform Generation via Internal Spectral Trajectory Learning
items.description: WaveGen is a fully end-to-end diffusion framework for text-to-waveform generation that jointly learns spectral and waveform trajectories via Spectral Forcing without external audio codecs, vocoders, latent models, alignment modules, or self-supervised representations, achieving…
items.ai_summary: WaveGen is an end-to-end diffusion-based framework that generates waveforms directly from text by jointly learning internal spectral trajectories without using external intermediate representations.

items.title: EditJudge-Bench: Auditing VLM Image-Edit Judges with Synthetic Ground Truth
items.description: Vision-language models (VLMs) are increasingly used as automated judges for image-editing benchmarks, yet their reliability is poorly understood.
items.ai_summary: EditJudge-Bench is a diagnostic benchmark using 1,382 synthetic image pairs to evaluate the reliability of vision-language models when acting as automated image-editing judges.

items.title: Can the Confidence and Decisions of System 1 Models Be Trusted? An Explainability and Perturbation Audit of Jev-Style Decision Models
items.description: "System 1" decision models (pioneered by TypeSafe AI's Jev) replace autoregressive text generation with a single forward pass returning typed probability distributions over declared schemas (Choice, Score, Noul).
items.ai_summary: Researchers introduce an audit benchmark for System 1 decision models to evaluate their statistical calibration, cross-question interference, and robustness against adversarial prompt injections.

items.title: UniHam: A Large-Scale SOC-Complete Dataset and Benchmark for Hamiltonian Learning in Materials
items.description: Accurate prediction of electronic Hamiltonians would enable broad property inference while avoiding the high computational cost of Density Functional Theory (DFT).
items.ai_summary: UniHam is a large-scale dataset and benchmark suite containing over 100,000 complex-valued Hamiltonians to support the development of materials science foundation models.

items.title: MARS: Multiscale Appearance-Residual Streams for Video Forgery Detection
items.description: Generalizing deepfake detection across facial manipulation and fully generated video remains challenging due to forgery traces varying with the manipulation method and scene content.
items.ai_summary: MARS is a two-path video detection framework that combines multiscale feature differences with appearance representations to improve the detection of facial manipulations and generated videos.

items.title: Text Grouping Changes Completion-Time Comparisons in Long-Form Simultaneous Speech Translation
items.description: Does grouping translation updates before speech synthesis change the measured completion gap between two translators? We compare StreamAtt with its fixed-audio-history baseline on ten English-German talks.
items.ai_summary: A study demonstrates that grouping translation updates before speech synthesis significantly impacts completion-time comparisons, highlighting the need to standardize how text enters synthesis systems.

items.title: Out-of-the-Box Tabular Foundation Models for Bayesian Optimization in Materials Discovery
items.description: Bayesian optimization is widely used in active learning loops for materials science. Gaussian processes serve as the de-facto surrogate model family, but require task-dependent kernel choices and can lack the modeling capacity for complex relationships.
items.ai_summary: Tabular foundation models serve as competitive out-of-the-box surrogate models for Bayesian optimization in materials discovery without requiring task-specific training or kernel selection.

items.title: Detecting AI-Authored Text in Authentic Student Writing: Evidence from PISA 2025
items.description: AI-text detectors reach near-perfect scores in evaluations that contrast fully human-written texts with texts generated from researcher-designed prompts. In authentic student writing, however, AI use is voluntary and often partial.
items.ai_summary: Feature-based and embedding-based detectors can reliably distinguish AI-authored student writing from human-written text using keystroke, clipboard, and chat logs from the PISA 2025 dataset.

items.title: AuDiR: Diagnosing Audio Reasoning with Rule and Percept Interventions
items.description: Answer accuracy alone does not distinguish failures in acoustic perception, rule knowledge, and rule application. AuDiR (Audio Diagnostic Reasoning) examines these distinctions through controlled input interventions.
items.ai_summary: AuDiR evaluates audio reasoning models through controlled input interventions to isolate the effects of acoustic perception, rule knowledge, and rule application on answer accuracy.

items.title: Perturb, Aggregate then Reconstruct: Consensus Aggregation and Fourier-Attended Multi-Decoders for Reconstruction-based Multi-View Anomaly Detection
items.description: Multi-view anomaly detection is crucial for industrial inspection to identify defects hidden from single viewpoints. Yet, despite their strong success in single-view applications, reconstruction-based methods remain largely underexplored in multi-view settings.
items.ai_summary: PAR is a reconstruction-based multi-view anomaly detection framework that uses feature perturbation, consensus aggregation, view-specialized multi-decoders, and Fourier attention to identify industrial defects.

items.title: Learning to Select Sparse Linear Solvers with Convolutional Neural Networks
items.description: We investigate convolutional-neural-network (CNN) based automatic solver selection for sparse linear systems, a problem of practical importance where solver performance varies dramatically with matrix sparsity structure.
items.ai_summary: Convolutional neural networks can automatically select sparse linear solvers by regressing log timing ratios from spy plot images of matrix nonzero structure.

items.title: Prediction with Foundation Models under Deployment Budgets
items.description: Foundation models can supply predictions for a downstream task that draw on knowledge from extensive pretraining, but they differ in task-specific accuracy and query cost.
items.ai_summary: A new query budget framework uses training data and Q-learning to determine which foundation models to query and how to combine their outputs for downstream prediction tasks.

items.title: Phrase-Level Speculative Decoding on a Frozen Target
items.description: Speculative decoders raise throughput by banking more target tokens per forward pass, and Medusa, EAGLE-3, DFlash and DSpark all do it the same way: more candidates that survive verification.
items.ai_summary: Phrase-level speculative decoding uses a small MLP head to predict multi-word phrases as single draft entries, significantly increasing generation throughput on benchmark tasks.

items.title: Causal discovery from Bayesian symbolic regression
items.description: Causal discovery from observational data is central to scientific reasoning, yet established constraint-based and score-based methods often recover only a Markov equivalence class and provide no signal in bivariate or strongly autocorrelated regimes typical in some areas of…
items.ai_summary: A Bayesian symbolic regression approach to causal discovery samples closed-form expressions from a posterior over symbolic models to compute causal scores and provide interpretable mechanisms.

items.title: V3DSAM: Semantic-Geometric Loop Verification and Geometry-Anchored Persistent Instance Mapping for Feed-Forward Dense SLAM
items.description: To address unreliable cross-view association in long-sequence feed-forward dense SLAM, this letter presents V3DSAM, an open-vocabulary semantic dense SLAM system that establishes physical correspondences at both the scene and object levels.
items.ai_summary: V3DSAM is an open-vocabulary semantic dense SLAM system that uses semantic-geometric dual-scale loop verification and geometry-anchored persistent instance mapping for robust long-sequence cross-view association.

items.title: Pricing Symbolic Rules by What GNNs Leave Unlearned
items.description: Symbolic knowledge (motif counts, ring counts, label constraints) is routinely added to graph neural networks (GNNs) and justified by their limited expressivity. We replace this yardstick with an exact one.
items.ai_summary: A novel rule discovery method prices symbolic rules based on out-of-fold network residuals to recover hidden graph properties and improve performance across datasets.

items.title: LongSCOP: Semantically Consistent Long Video Outpainting
items.description: Video out-painting is an important problem, yet existing research focuses primarily on short clips, leaving long video out-painting largely underexplored. Extending video out-painting to long videos poses substantial challenges.
items.ai_summary: LongSCOP is a semantically consistent long video out-painting framework featuring a training recipe and a VLM-based agent that improves generation stability and temporal consistency.

items.title: MoSTE: Mixture of Spatio-Temporal Experts for Deepfake Detection in Videos
items.description: Generalizable deepfake video detection remains challenging because forgery artifacts vary substantially across manipulation types and often combine diverse spatial and temporal inconsistencies.
items.ai_summary: MoSTE is a mixture of spatio-temporal experts framework for deepfake video detection that decomposes adaptation into parallel pools to improve generalization across unseen forgeries.

items.title: Occupancy Modelling of Biased Landslide Inventories: When Does Separating Occurrence from Recording Improve on Neutralisation?
items.description: Landslide susceptibility models are trained on inventories that record where landslides were seen, not where they occurred. The established remedy fits bias-describing variables and neutralises them when mapping.
items.ai_summary: An occupancy-detection modelling approach separates landslide occurrence from recording to reduce road bias and improve prediction rates compared to standard neutralisation baselines.

items.title: Patching Up Circuit Learning via Parameter Sharing
items.description: Probabilistic circuits (PCs) have emerged as generative models guaranteeing tractable probabilistic inference. However, tractability comes at the price of larger model sizes than in other generative models.
items.ai_summary: RePA is a recursive parameter sharing construction for probabilistic circuits that improves efficiency and reduces memory consumption on high-dimensional and tabular datasets without assuming independence.

items.title: To SIMD or Not to SIMD: Comparing RVV vs. CGRA SoCs for Non-Linear Functions in AI
items.description: Non-linear functions are an important class of operations in modern large language models. However, chip vendors building for AI have so far relied on traditional vector or scalar processing units for non-linear functions.
items.ai_summary: A study comparing RVV and CGRA accelerators for AI non-linear functions finds that CGRAs achieve higher speedups on simple point-wise operations while RVV excels on complex functions.

items.title: Can Frontier Auto Researchers Reconstruct Human Research Decisions in AI?
items.description: Scientific research has long been driven by substantial human effort, from reviewing prior work and identifying research gaps to designing specific solutions.
items.ai_summary: AutoHRS is a stage-wise evaluation framework that measures how closely automated AI researchers can reconstruct human research decisions and artifacts across scientific workflows.

items.title: UCB-min: Combining Bandits Under Variance Heterogeneity (Extended Version)
items.description: Multi-armed bandits are a natural framework for many real-world sequential decision problems, from recommender systems and clinical trials to educational test recommendation and online advertising.
items.ai_summary: UCB-min is a per-arm adaptive meta-bandit algorithm that selects between variance-independent and variance-aware exploration bonuses to improve sequential decision-making under heterogeneous variances.

items.title: dNaViT: Discrete Codes are General-Purpose Visual Representations
items.description: A discrete native-resolution vision transformer with grouped product quantization and a dual-branch objective acts as a versatile visual tokenizer, matching or exceeding task-specific baselines across visual understanding, generation, and editing tasks.
items.ai_summary: dNaViT is a discrete native-resolution vision transformer that uses a compact discrete vocabulary and grouped product quantization to function as a versatile visual tokenizer across multiple tasks.

items.title: Physics-informed neural networks in the small-data regime: A controlled comparison with classical PDE surrogates
items.description: Neural surrogates for engineering models are often trained on large collections of simulated solutions.
items.ai_summary: Hierarchical PINN variants incorporate governing equations to achieve accurate predictions from scarce labelled observations in small-data engineering regression and forecasting tasks.

items.title: Two-Phase Rapid Simulation-Based Inference with Differentiable Simulators
items.description: We introduce Rapid Simulation Based Inference (RSBI), a diffusion-based variational approach to likelihood-free Bayesian inference that achieves high sampling efficiency under large prior-to-posterior volumes.
items.ai_summary: Rapid Simulation-Based Inference is a diffusion-based variational approach using differentiable simulators and Schrödinger Bridge sampling to achieve efficient likelihood-free Bayesian inference.

items.title: Path-Level Structural and Semantic Alignment for Hierarchical Multi-Label Text Classification
items.description: Hierarchical multi-label text classification (HMTC) requires models to capture both structural dependencies among labels and the fine-grained semantics of labels at different hierarchy levels.
items.ai_summary: Framework that uses complete root-to-node label paths as a shared unit with auxiliary training objectives to improve hierarchical multi-label text classification.

items.title: Optimal Rates for Adaptive Private $k$-PCA
items.description: Given $n$ i.i.d.
items.ai_summary: Algorithm for Differentially Private Stochastic PCA that achieves optimal sample complexity in both data dimension and target subspace rank while removing dependency on the eigengap.

items.title: Unprompted coordination through shared memory in LLM agents: a locked two-implementation replication and extension
items.description: Coordination between large language-model agents has become a central question for AI safety and software engineering, as such agents are deployed in groups that share infrastructure. Existing research tells the agents that partners exist or asks them to coordinate.
items.ai_summary: Study demonstrating that large language model agents can achieve unprompted coordination exclusively through shared memory when prompted to re-examine their workspace.

items.title: PhysOPSD: Code as Privilege for Physically Plausible Video Generation
items.description: PhysOPSD uses executable code as privileged physical context to improve the physical plausibility of video generative models through on-policy self-distillation with dual-level privilege and controlled variations.
items.ai_summary: Method that introduces executable code as a privileged physical context to improve the physical plausibility and dynamics of video generation models.

items.title: Bridging Task Planning and Execution for Language-Conditioned Bimanual Manipulation
items.description: Robots are increasingly expected to execute natural-language manipulation tasks in real-world environments. This is particularly relevant in household assistance and logistics, where clutter requires reasoning about both task objectives and execution feasibility.
items.ai_summary: Zero-shot vision-language framework for bimanual manipulation that jointly reasons about task objectives and physical execution constraints using a structured scene representation.

items.title: BDBBQ: A Human-AI Collaborative Benchmark for Bengali Social Bias in LLMs
items.description: Despite growing attention to social bias in large language models (LLMs), existing bias benchmarks provide limited coverage of culturally grounded evaluation in Bengali, particularly within Bangladesh's sociocultural context.
items.ai_summary: Bilingual benchmark comprising over 61,000 instances to systematically evaluate social bias and stereotype alignment in large language models across English and Bengali.

items.title: PTC-IoU: CPU-Friendly Detection Quality Estimation for Edge Video Analytics
items.description: An edge video analytics system must estimate the quality of local detections since there are no ground-truth labels available during runtime.
items.ai_summary: Edge video analytics quality estimator that compresses detection box histories to perform prediction on the CPU, reducing latency and energy consumption.

items.title: AutoBuddy: Evaluating Proactive, Always-On Agents on Task Discovery and Execution in a Simulated Workplace
items.description: As LLM agents become more autonomous, they are increasingly expected to run as always-on assistants on a user's behalf, identifying work to be done and completing it without being asked.
items.ai_summary: Simulator and reference agent framework designed to evaluate proactive task discovery and execution by large language models within a simulated workplace environment.

items.title: More Than Just Style: Benchmarking Personality Influence in Large Language Models
items.description: In addition to the effects of explicit input prompts and instructions, large language model outputs are influenced by underlying behavioral preferences similar to human personality tendencies. These tendencies can affect how models interpret situations and make decisions.
items.ai_summary: Benchmark framework combining controlled protocols and datasets to evaluate and distinguish personality influence from model capabilities in large language models.

items.title: Say Shibboleth: Fingerprinting the LLMs and Harnesses Behind Agentic Attacks
items.description: We study the fingerprinting of agentic cyberattacks. Our objective is to reliably infer information about the attacker's configuration, such as LLM version and harness, from telemetry.
items.ai_summary: Technique using honeypot services and behavioral probes to reliably infer the underlying language models and execution harnesses used in agentic cyberattacks.

items.title: Clinical predictions using artificial intelligence in neurosurgery and its subspecialties: a systematic review and meta-analysis
items.description: Artificial intelligence models for clinical prediction are proliferating across neurosurgery, but their aggregate discriminative performance, distribution along the care pathway and methodological quality are unclear.
items.ai_summary: Systematic review and meta-analysis evaluating artificial intelligence models in neurosurgery, finding high pooled discrimination performance alongside a high overall risk of bias across studies.

items.title: AutoVLA-D: Learn a Trajectory-Geometric Condition from Reasoning for Autonomous Driving VLA
items.description: Autoregressive VLA planning usually predicts continuous trajectories as the final output, but driving instructions often describe actions rather than ego states, which weakens direct conditioning on the final continuous trajectory.
items.ai_summary: Method called AutoVLA-D that introduces a discrete trajectory-geometric condition from reasoning to consistently improve continuous trajectory prediction for autonomous driving vision-language-action models.

items.title: Reconstructing hourly traffic on every street of a capital from a sparse counting network: a graph neural network applied to Paris
items.description: Micro-scale air quality models require hourly traffic data on every road segment, whereas permanent counters cover only a small part of the network.
items.ai_summary: Graph neural network model that reconstructs hourly traffic flows across all road segments of Paris using data from a sparse network of permanent counters.

items.title: Detecting Shadow AI: Unsanctioned LLM Agents on Enterprise Endpoints: A Taxonomy, an Open Detector and a Controlled Evaluation
items.description: Shadow IT, the use of technology that the IT organisation has not approved, is a long-standing governance problem.
items.ai_summary: Open-source Windows detector that identifies unsanctioned autonomous AI agents on enterprise endpoints by correlating remote service identities with installation and execution histories.

items.title: AudioCodex: Streaming Autoencoders for Live Audio
items.description: We introduce AudioCodex, a fully causal autoencoder for live generative audio applications that compresses stereo audio into compact continuous latent sequences at ~10 Hz.
items.ai_summary: Fully causal streaming autoencoder called AudioCodex that compresses stereo audio into compact continuous latent sequences at approximately 10 Hz for live generative audio applications.

items.title: TANSAR: Editable and Attributable Correlation Matrix Memories under Correlated Keys, with Rule-Constrained Multi-Hop Knowledge Editing

items.title: QCC-WM: Linking Macro-State Dynamics and Visual Generation via Quotient Causal Construction

items.title: ReVMap: Vectorized Global Mapping via Connectivity-Aware Local Map Fusion

items.title: Evidence or Marginal? What Moment-Vector Propagation Computes in Polynomial Density Neurons

items.title: Do Machine Learning Models Predict?
