items.title: CPU-ARC: Agentic Reasoning Caching for on-CPU Reasoning Reuse
items.description: Reasoning caches built from LLM traces can efficiently apply previously derived solutions to new problem instances with robustness and much lower invocation cost than source models.
items.ai_summary: Agentic reasoning caching is a method that constructs CPU-executable reasoning caches from LLM reasoning traces, enabling efficient solution reuse for mathematical and scientific tasks at a fraction of the source model's cost.

items.title: On the (non-)closedness of the set of ReLU networks
items.description: We prove that the set $\mathcal{N}_N$ of ReLU networks with one hidden layer and at most $N\in\mathbb N$ neurons is weakly closed in $W^{1,p}(Ω)$, for a bounded connected open set $Ω\subset\mathbb R^d$.
items.ai_summary: A mathematical proof demonstrates that the set of one-hidden-layer ReLU networks with a bounded number of neurons is weakly closed in a specific Sobolev space, while the two-hidden-layer case is not.

items.title: FlowMoP: Stochastic Multi-Person Motion Prediction
items.description: Predicting the future motion of multiple people is inherently stochastic: the same observed history admits many plausible continuations depending on intent, coordination, and social context.
items.ai_summary: FlowMoP is a conditional flow matching framework that jointly generates diverse future motions for multiple agents using a B-spline reparameterization and a dual-stream transformer for interaction-aware forecasting.

items.title: ZeoBench: A Benchmark for Self-Supervised Learning on 3D Zeolite Representations
items.description: Zeolites are an important class of porous crystalline materials with broad applications in gas storage, separations, and catalysis.
items.ai_summary: ZeoBench is a benchmark for self-supervised learning on 3D zeolite representations, used to evaluate features on downstream adsorption-property prediction tasks and improve materials discovery in low-data regimes.

items.title: Graded convolutional networks: scale invariance without the scale and robustness to unknown blur
items.description: The Gaussian jet of an image is a graded vector space: a dilation by $λ$ multiplies derivatives of order $k$ by $λ^{-k}$.
items.ai_summary: Graded convolutional networks utilize local graded convolutions and retractions to achieve scale invariance and robustness to unknown Gaussian blur without explicit scale parameters.

items.title: On the Reliability of Majority-Vote Pseudo-Labels in Test-Time Reinforcement Learning
items.description: Test-time reinforcement learning (TTRL) adapts pretrained language models to unlabeled target-domain data using self-generated pseudo-labels, whose reliability remains poorly understood.
items.ai_summary: Prompt-Conditional Distributionally Robust DPO is a test-time reinforcement learning method that conditions robust reweighting on vote reliability to reduce errors from sampling-sensitive prompts.

items.title: CodeQuant2: Enhanced Outlier Mitigation and Adaptive Clustering for Low-Precision LRMs
items.description: Large reasoning models (LRMs) improve task performance by generating longer intermediate reasoning traces, but this substantially increases inference costs and makes low-precision quantization increasingly important.
items.ai_summary: CodeQuant2 is a clustering-based lookup table quantization framework for low-precision large reasoning models that uses rotation, scaling, and improved calibration to enhance reasoning accuracy and inference speed.

items.title: GRAC: Graph-Based Retrieval-Augmented Captioning for Surgical Scene Description
items.description: Purpose: Surgical operative reports support procedural documentation, surgical training, performance assessment, and workflow review. However, extracting meaningful information often requires extensive manual review and clinical expertise.
items.ai_summary: Graph-Based Retrieval-Augmented Captioning is a framework that represents surgical scenes as graphs to retrieve relevant examples and improve the language quality and factual accuracy of automated surgical captions.

items.title: Grasp-TAGS: Task-Aware Grasp Selection via Critic Distillation for Prehensile Loco-Manipulation
items.description: Loco-manipulation, which requires mobile manipulators to coordinate locomotion and manipulation over long horizons, is a key capability for large-object rearrangement in applications such as service robotics and warehouse automation.
items.ai_summary: Grasp-TAGS is a task-aware grasp selection framework for goal-conditioned large-object rearrangement that distills a reinforcement learning critic into a lightweight network to rank candidate grasps by downstream utility.

items.title: Flow-Guided Target-Space Alignment via Path Consistency
items.description: Many multimodal alignment problems require mapping a source modality into a fixed space defined by a target modality, where the target space is not merely an intermediate embedding but is used directly for downstream analysis.
items.ai_summary: FlowAlign is a flow-guided target-space alignment method that uses conditional flow matching to guide source representations into a fixed target space while preserving paired correspondence and global structure.

items.title: Super-resolved digital terrain models for GEDI geolocation correction: agreement with airborne LiDAR DTM-based corrections at the beam level, not the footprint level
items.description: The Global Ecosystem Dynamics Investigation (GEDI) mission measures three-dimensional forest structure with a LiDAR aboard the International Space Station.
items.ai_summary: Study on super-resolved digital terrain models finds that super-resolving a 10-meter DTM to 1-meter yields beam-level GEDI geolocation corrections that match airborne LiDAR DTM corrections, though footprint-level corrections do not match.

items.title: Health-System-Wide Mapping of Demographic Information in Routine Clinical Histopathology
items.description: The extent to which demographic-associated information is detectable across organs and disease states in routine clinical histopathology remains unclear.
items.ai_summary: Study using 1.3 million clinical histopathology images demonstrates that patient demographic attributes such as sex, age group, and race are broadly recoverable across multiple organs using pathology foundation models.

items.title: How far does a hash-only sender go? A pre-registered map of sender memory versus bits for short text messages
items.description: Can a sender that only computes hashes, with a language model only at the receiver, transmit short human text more cheaply than a classical sender trained on the same domain? We answer with one pre-registered run on 1,000 English user utterances from Taskmaster-1.
items.ai_summary: Study mapping sender memory versus bits for short text messages finds that a hash-only sender can transmit text cheaply compared to classical senders, though failures incur additional airtime and acknowledgement costs.

items.title: Computer-Use Agents Are Embodied Generalists
items.description: In many areas of AI, general-purpose models have increasingly replaced handcrafted methods and specialized architectures. We argue that embodied AI is poised for a similar shift. Our key claim is that embodied tasks can be formulated as interaction with digital software.
items.ai_summary: Study argues that computer-use agents can serve as embodied generalists by performing embodied tasks through screen rendering and software controls without task-specific agent tuning.

items.title: Ensemble Methodology for Reference-Free Confidence Estimation in LLM-based Code Summarization
items.description: This paper describes an approach and use case to estimate the correctness of LLM-generated COBOL summaries without access to human-authored references.
items.ai_summary: Reference-free confidence estimation approach for LLM-based COBOL summarization uses diverse model generation, an LLM evaluator for pairwise assessments, and a calibrated aggregation rule to estimate summary correctness without human references.

items.title: AdaptivePnP: Fast Auto-Tuned Plug-and-Play for Deconvolution
items.description: Plug-and-play (PnP) methods reconstruct images by alternating a data-fitting step with an image denoiser. Their performance depends on two parameters: the step size $γ$ and the measurement noise level $σ$.
items.ai_summary: AdaptivePnP proposes an auto-tuned plug-and-play framework for image deconvolution that jointly estimates measurement noise and step size from data-fitting residuals without requiring parameter tuning.

items.title: Fifty-Two Shades of Pig: What the UCR Archive Really Asks Classifiers to Do
items.description: The pigs were bleeding. That was the point of the experiment: could airway pressure reveal hemorrhage before it became critical?
items.ai_summary: An audit of the UCR Time Series Classification Archive reveals that many benchmark datasets are repurposed from original tasks, use flawed test splits, or rely on toy setups, urging more careful interpretation of archive scores.

items.title: Can Agentic Systems Close the Gap in Radiology with Production AI Tools?
items.description: Radiology AI has developed along two paths: specialized models that perform well on narrow tasks but cover few clinical findings, and generalist models that address a broader range of tasks but remain prone to hallucination and inaccurate measurements.
items.ai_summary: A radiology agentic framework combines specialized and generalist AI tools through an orchestrator to automate structured report generation and evaluate finding recovery from FDA-cleared devices.

items.title: Designing Effective Monitor-Based Interventions for Mitigating Reward Hacking During RL
items.description: Reinforcement learning (RL) rewards are notoriously difficult to design and control, often leading to the model learning unintended behaviors such as reward hacking.
items.ai_summary: Three realistic reinforcement learning environments are introduced to study and mitigate reward hacking, demonstrating that monitors leaking more learning signal can suppress hacking but increase evasive behavior.

items.title: BitDecoding-FP4: Native FP4 KV Cache Decoding via Algorithm-System Co-Design
items.description: The key-value (KV) cache dominates memory capacity and bandwidth in long-context LLM serving.
items.ai_summary: BitDecoding-FP4 introduces an algorithm-system co-design for native FP4 KV cache decoding that eliminates quantization errors and softmax bottlenecks to deliver higher peak serving throughput in large language models.

items.title: Discovering formally verified quantum programs with AI
items.description: The timeline by which quantum computers can solve breakthrough problems in science depends on improved quantum algorithms as much as on better hardware. Such algorithmic advances are typically achieved through many years of expert human collaboration.
items.ai_summary: Large language model agents collaborating within a formal proof assistant discover and verify quantum programs, achieving order-of-magnitude improvements across several scientific applications.

items.title: Generative Latent Priors for Interpreting and Steering Protein Language Models
items.description: Dominant methods for interpreting large models impose strong structural assumptions. Generative Latent Priors (GLP) are a complementary approach: a diffusion model that learns the distribution of a frozen model's activations directly, imposing no assumptions.
items.ai_summary: Generative Latent Priors apply diffusion models directly to protein language model activations without structural assumptions to serve as a lens for protein representations and an editing prior for steering properties.

items.title: Machine learning for lattice QCD
items.description: Machine learning (ML) methods have been explored as a means of optimizing lattice field theory calculations, with increasing interest in recent years.
items.ai_summary: This book chapter provides an introduction and summary of machine learning methods used to optimize lattice field theory calculations without introducing uncontrolled approximations.

items.title: BEV3SR: Evidence-Aware 3D Spatial Reasoning from Video
items.description: 3D spatial reasoning from video remains challenging for VLMs because videos provide sequential, view-local observations rather than persistent metric scene records.
items.ai_summary: BEV3SR is a training-free framework that converts RGB-D videos into metric bird's-eye-view scene memory to improve 3D spatial reasoning and query-based question answering across vision-language models.

items.title: The Cost of Coverage: Conformalising Native Forecast Uncertainty for GB Wind Power
items.description: Uncertainty bands on wind forecasts help inform reserve sizing and commitments, but often fail to deliver their stated coverage.
items.ai_summary: Applying conformal prediction to native wind forecast uncertainty bands repairs marginal coverage and cuts out-of-band volume in high winds by over forty percent when calibrated by forecast wind regime.

items.title: Compaction, decay and reinforcement in a two-tier conversational memory: a paired evaluation against retrieval-augmented generation
items.description: A conversational agent that remembers has to decide what to keep. Retrieval-augmented generation keeps the transcript and searches it; the alternative is to compact each turn into atomic facts and search those.
items.ai_summary: Conversational memory method that compacts turns into atomic facts outperforms retrieval-augmented generation on value-based questions while using fewer tokens.

items.title: Scaling Graph Similarity Learning with Graph Neural Networks
items.description: Graph similarity computation is an important task in graph mining with many real-world applications, such as chemical compound analysis, program dependence comparison, and social network analysis.
items.ai_summary: FiLSim is a scalable graph neural network framework that computes graph similarity for large graphs with over 150,000 nodes within seconds.

items.title: When Instruction Files Go Stale: Documentation Debt and Hidden Cost in Coding Agents
items.description: LLM-based coding agents such as Claude Code are guided by repository instruction files (also called context files or agent configuration files) like AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md, which are read in every agent session.
items.ai_summary: Coding agents frequently follow stale repository instruction files when relevant to their tasks, increasing tool call usage and introducing documentation debt.

items.title: Maya a1: Do the Options Read the Model, or Does Their Position? Order Sensitivity in a Non-Autoregressive Decision Model
items.description: Laya answers typed multiple-choice questions in one forward pass by scoring a hidden state at one [MASK] marker per option.
items.ai_summary: Option order sensitivity study on a non-autoregressive model reveals that answer choices fluctuate based on their listed position, which is mitigated by fine-tuning with shuffling.

items.title: Test-Time Compute Scales Better with Parallel Agent Teams
items.description: Test-time scaling improves the performance of a fixed model by spending more computation at inference. There are two common ways to spend it on agents when a verifier can score every attempt.
items.ai_summary: Parallel agent teams sample many small collaborating groups in the same setup to scale test-time compute, outperforming single agents and large teams.

items.title: AR-Edit: Training-Free Autoregressive Video Editing without Inversion
items.description: Editing a video stream in real time, without access to future frames, is essential for interactive applications.
items.ai_summary: AR-Edit is a training-free and inversion-free video editing method that caches and reuses source values for real-time streaming video generation.

items.title: Seeing What Matters: Benchmarking Task-Conditioned Actionable Spatial Belief for Manipulation
items.description: When should a robot look at the cup, and when at the portafilter? Spatial-reasoning benchmarks evaluate whether a model can describe a scene, but manipulation needs something more specific: the ability to acquire the particular evidence that makes the current command executable.
items.ai_summary: Seeing What Matters is a new simulated benchmark designed to evaluate whether vision-language models and policies select the correct camera views for manipulation tasks.

items.title: Knowing When to Intervene: Causal Evaluation of AI Agents
items.description: Current evaluations of agentic AI systems primarily rely on benchmarks. However, the static nature of benchmarks makes them uninformative about the value of auditing interventions at deployment time.
items.ai_summary: A new causal inference framework estimates the dynamic effects of randomized interventions within AI agent trajectories to prioritize audits and improve safety.

items.title: Assessing the Impact of Retrieval-Augmented Generation on Algorithmic Problem-Solving
items.description: Competitive programming problems pose distinctive challenges for Large Language Models, as they demand not only proficient code generation but also advanced algorithmic reasoning.
items.ai_summary: Retrieval-augmented generation approach integrating embedding-based retrieval and similarity search helps large language models solve competitive programming problems.

items.title: Are These Programmers Ripe Enough to Eat? Evaluating How LLMs Handle Lexical Knowledge Conflicts in Translation
items.description: External lexical resources can help large language models (LLMs) translate texts in low-resource languages and specialized domains, but these resources may conflict with models' prior lexical knowledge.
items.ai_summary: Controlled study on Mandarin-to-English translation investigates how large language models handle conflicts between external lexical resources and their prior knowledge.

items.title: Quasipolynomial-Time Planning for Decodable POMDPs
items.description: We study planning for finite-horizon partially observable Markov decision processes (POMDPs) with finite state, action, and observation spaces.
items.ai_summary: Approximation algorithms based on decodability provide quasipolynomial-time planning for finite-horizon POMDPs under weaker assumptions than prior methods.

items.title: ROSE: Risk-Aware Orthogonal Subspace Navigation for Lifelong Knowledge Editing in Multimodal Large Language Models
items.description: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) require continuous factual updates to stay current, yet lifelong knowledge editing remains a daunting challenge.
items.ai_summary: Risk-Aware Orthogonal Subspace Navigation is a framework for multimodal large language models that prevents catastrophic forgetting and locality erosion during lifelong knowledge editing.

items.title: AnimWeb-Bench: Benchmarking Animated Webpage Code Generation from Videos
items.description: Animation is pervasive on the Web, the CSS animation property alone appears on over three-quarters of webpages.
items.ai_summary: AnimWeb-Bench is a new benchmark for evaluating multimodal large language models and coding agents on generating animated webpage code from reference videos.

items.title: Language as Trait, Politeness as Strategy: Controlled Tests of Linguistic Effects in LLM Social-Deduction Agents
items.description: Large language model (LLM) agents coordinate through conversation, and the same message can be phrased in simpler or more complex language, bluntly or politely.
items.ai_summary: Controlled tests using the LURK Werewolf framework show that varying linguistic range and politeness in LLM social-dedction agents does not significantly affect trust or voting behavior.

items.title: From PAC bounds on the generalization error to PAC bounds on the parameter estimation error
items.description: Probably Approximately Correct (PAC) bounds on the generalization error (the difference between the empirical prediction error computed on the training data and its expectation) are an established tool in statistical machine learning, and there have been several extensions of…
items.ai_summary: Oracle bounds derived from classical PAC bounds are used to establish finite-sample parameter-estimation error bounds for regularized loss minimization in dynamical systems.

items.title: A Tight Hierarchy for Chain of Thought
items.description: Chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning has emerged as a powerful paradigm for extending the computational capabilities of transformer-based models.
items.ai_summary: A new hierarchy theorem proves that increasing chain-of-thought reasoning steps provably increases the computational power of transformer-based models.

items.title: Diffusion-free Score Matching for Exact Conditional Sampling
items.description: The success of modern score-based generative models is largely driven by diffusion-based training, which learns a collection of time-indexed score fields corresponding to progressively noisier versions of the data distribution.
items.ai_summary: Diffusion-free score matching estimates a single score of a perturbed data distribution to enable exact conditional sampling without time-dependent diffusion fields.

items.title: A lightweight convolutional neural network for target detection in an edge environment
items.description: This paper proposes a novel, lightweight convolutional neural network (CNN) designed for edge device deployment. The CNN is developed to recognize and classify threats or targets of interest.
items.ai_summary: A lightweight convolutional neural network is designed for edge deployment to perform real-time threat detection and object classification using thermal sensors.

items.title: Continuous wavelet-based feature extraction for laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy classification of human plasma samples
items.description: Extracting discriminative features from laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy (LIBS) spectra is important for the classification of complex biological samples.
items.ai_summary: Continuous wavelet transform-based spectral peak extraction coupled with a support vector machine classifies human plasma samples using laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy data.

items.title: Multiscale Closing Index (MCI) for measuring structural similarity between 2D point sets
items.description: We introduce Multi-scale Closing Index (MCI), a new dissimilarity measure for evaluating the alignment of two 2D point sets. MCI is bounded between 0 and 1 and is based on multiscale mathematical morphology operations, with smaller values indicating greater structural agreement.
items.ai_summary: Multi-scale Closing Index is a multiscale morphological dissimilarity measure for evaluating structural alignment and registration quality between two-dimensional point sets.

items.title: Zero-Shot Benchmarking of Unified Multimodal Models for Shallow-Water UAV Image Distortion Assessment and Restoration
items.description: Shallow-water UAV imagery provides centimeter-scale observations of benthic environments, but water-induced distortions complicate interpretation.
items.ai_summary: Zero-shot benchmark that evaluates five unified multimodal large language models on their ability to assess and restore shallow-water UAV imagery without reference images.

items.title: Safety Is $Π_1$, Provability Is $Σ_1$: One Framework for the Hugging Face Breach and OpenAI's Mathematical Proofs
items.description: OpenAI's agents breached Hugging Face in July 2026, and the same company released more than seven hundred AI-generated manuscripts of mathematical proofs in October 2026. The first event is read as a failure in security, while the second is read as a success in mathematics.
items.ai_summary: Hybrid framework that models program safety and mathematical provability through a single deductive mechanism based on Turing's Undecidability Theorem.

items.title: What to Delegate, What to Preserve: Human Preferences for Agentic AI Across Everyday Life and Work
items.description: AI agents can execute multi-step tasks on users' behalf, yet the boundaries of acceptable delegation remain unclear. We report a scenario-based survey of 289 U.S. adults with prior AI experience covering 45 use cases across nine life domains.
items.ai_summary: Scenario-based survey that identifies user preferences for human-AI collaboration, showing that trust and desired leadership drive automation choices across everyday and work tasks.

items.title: One Run Is Not Enough: A Monte Carlo Protocol for Evaluating LLM Reliability on Data Science Tasks
items.description: Large language models (LLMs) have shown promise for automating data science workflows. Benchmarks such as DataSciBench (2026) and StatQA (2024) have advanced the evaluation of their capabilities across data science and statistical tasks.
items.ai_summary: Monte Carlo protocol and benchmark dataset designed to evaluate the consistency and reliability of large language models on data science and statistics tasks.

items.title: SAGE-PAIR: Source-Pretrained Routed Residual Adaptation for Sparse-Feedback Recommendation
items.description: Recommendation systems often enter a new serving window before enough outcomes are available to retrain the deployed model.
items.ai_summary: Staged adapter framework that uses source-pretrained residual corrections to improve recommendation ranking quality under extremely sparse feedback conditions.

items.title: TriNetra: Thermal-Reliability-Guided RGB-Thermal Fusion and Tracking for Surveillance
items.description: Visible cameras fail at night and thermal sensors fail under saturation, blur or loss of contrast, yet most RGB-thermal (RGB-T) detectors mix the two streams with fixed weights and cannot tell when one modality has become unreliable.
items.ai_summary: Reliability-aware surveillance framework that uses a thermal reliability coefficient to gate and fuse RGB-thermal video streams for robust object detection and tracking.

items.title: Evaluating Anterior Cruciate Ligament Risk of Injury Using a Graph Convolutional Autoencoder
items.description: Current solutions for assessing the risk of anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injury typically rely on expensive motion-capture labs that require substantial resource investment or subjective evaluations of specific athletic stress tests by experts.
items.ai_summary: Smartphone-based unsupervised learning model that uses graph convolutional networks and pose estimation data to screen athletes for anterior cruciate ligament injury risk.

items.title: Fixed-point acceleration on Neural Wasserstein manifolds
items.description: We propose a fixed-point acceleration method for optimization over probability measures, applicable to a variety of machine learning problems.
items.ai_summary: Fixed-point acceleration method that applies Riemannian Anderson mixing to optimize probability measures over neural Wasserstein manifolds more efficiently.

items.title: FOSCAR: Accelerating Decode Attention over 2- and 4-Bit KV Caches through Affine Folding
items.description: Large-language-model decode attention streams the key-value (KV) cache for every generated token. Packing that cache into 2-bit or 4-bit quantized integers reduces memory traffic but does not automatically translate into latency saving.
items.ai_summary: Affine folding method that accelerates large-language-model decode attention over 2-bit and 4-bit quantized key-value caches by drastically reducing scale-and-offset operations.

items.title: MemoryDojo: Benchmarking Poisoning Through LLM Agent Memory
items.description: LLM agents benefit from using memory systems to improve performance on long-horizon, multi-session tasks. However, memory introduces a critical attack surface.
items.ai_summary: Benchmark suite for evaluating how malicious instructions propagate through and poison different large language model agent memory systems across multi-session tasks.

items.title: Direct Regression and Geometric Recovery for Event-based Spacecraft Pose Estimation
items.description: Event cameras offer high temporal resolution and dynamic range for uncooperative spacecraft pose estimation, but models trained on synthetic event streams must generalize to the noise, background activity, and contrast variation of physical sensors.
items.ai_summary: Comparative study of two synthetic-to-real event-based spacecraft pose estimation systems finds that direct regression reduces orientation error while a modular pipeline reduces relative translation error.

items.title: Intent-Aware Caching for Efficient LLM Serving
items.description: Modern LLM serving systems use prefix caching to accelerate multi-turn conversational workloads.
items.ai_summary: Intent-Aware Caching classifies conversation requests by user intent and learns lightweight reuse statistics to improve cache hit rates and reduce LLM serving latency.

items.title: Beyond Segmentation: Enriching ImageCAS with Coronary Ostia Landmarks, Rooted Centerline Graphs, and Open-Weight Localization Models
items.description: Coronary ostia and centerlines are key reference points for automated analysis of coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA), from surgical planning to intraoperative vessel tracking.
items.ai_summary: Enriched ImageCAS dataset adds coronary ostium annotations and rooted centerlines to 1,000 patient scans, enabling improved 3D ostium localization and vessel analysis.

items.title: ICare-DT: a digital twin for continuous forecasting of intensive care patients
items.description: Digital twins of intensive care patients should update forecasts from new data and predict treatment responses, but few studies test whether routine records support either.
items.ai_summary: ICare-DT is a Transformer-based digital twin that continuously updates intensive care patient states hourly from new measurements to forecast vital signs and treatment responses.

items.title: RidgeFill: Training-Free Late-Layer Cache Fill for Faster Prefill
items.description: RidgeFill shortens prefill by not computing most of a model's upper layers for the prompt. The lower layers run exactly up to a split; from the split layer's state a per-layer map predicts every later layer's input, and each late layer writes its cache from that prediction.
items.ai_summary: RidgeFill uses closed-form ridge regression maps to predict upper-layer inputs from lower-layer states, accelerating LLM prefill time without requiring model retraining.

items.title: Empirical Assessment of Post-Quantum Cryptography Adoption Status in TLS
items.description: Anticipating Q-day security concerns, major CDNs and cloud providers are migrating to post-quantum cryptography (PQC). While existing literature benchmarks PQC performance, empirical research evaluating real-world adoption data remains scarce.
items.ai_summary: Empirical assessment of post-quantum cryptography adoption across seven critical protocols reveals that origin-server support reaches 9.1% for HTTPS but remains below 1% for other protocols.

items.title: Empirical Study of Post-Quantum Cryptography Adoption Status in SSH Infrastructure
items.description: With the anticipated arrival of Q-day, quantum computers threaten current cryptographic schemes for encryption and digital signatures. In response, major content delivery networks and cloud service providers are already adopting Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC).
items.ai_summary: Large-scale analysis of SSH infrastructure shows that post-quantum cryptography adoption is highly polarized, with 45.2% of hosts supporting PQC while 54.8% remain classical-only.

items.title: Where Should Learning Live? Regret Analysis for Text, Parameter, and Joint Adaptation
items.description: Language-model systems can select prompts and parameter adapters repeatedly during deployment, using feedback to guide later choices. Earlier choices may change the context or environment inherited by later configurations.
items.ai_summary: Analysis of language-model adaptation compares prompt and parameter selection, showing that limiting configuration switches can reduce within-family regret depending on inherited histories.

items.title: Attend at the Right Resolution: Head-Adaptive Sparse Attention via Query-Key Interaction Structure
items.description: Attention is a major scalability bottleneck in large language models (LLMs), with its computational cost and key-value (KV) memory traffic becoming increasingly prohibitive as context length grows.
items.ai_summary: Head-Adaptive Sparse Attention is a training-free framework that adapts selection resolution along feature and sequence dimensions using query-key interaction structures to reduce attention bottlenecks.

items.title: Verifier Noise Is a Temperature: Testing Tilt Predictions in Finite-Budget LLM-Guided Search
items.description: LLM-guided search loops propose a modified candidate, score it, and keep it if it scores better.
items.ai_summary: Empirical tests on LLM-guided program search evaluate stationary law tilt predictions, finding that search performance varies with minibatch size and parent-child quality correlations.

items.title: A Generalized Bayesian Approach to Clustering with Dimension Reduction
items.description: Generalized Bayes product partition models provide a probabilistic counterpart to loss-based clustering.
items.ai_summary: Generalized Bayes product partition models are extended by jointly learning an autoencoder and a partition, allowing the clustering loss to adaptively shape the latent space for high-dimensional data.

items.title: PoseRieFlow: Riemannian Flow Matching for Whole-Body Text-to-Pose Generation
items.description: We present PoseRieFlow, a compact flow-matching framework for text-conditioned generation of whole-body 3D human poses. Prior text-to-pose methods either neglect articulated hands or model rotations in Euclidean space despite their non-Euclidean geometry.
items.ai_summary: PoseRieFlow is a compact Riemannian flow-matching framework for text-to-pose generation that models joint rotations on a product manifold to achieve high kinematic fidelity for whole-body 3D human poses with articulated hands.

items.title: SURE:Spatiotemporal Uncertainty Representation for Efficient Vision-Language-Action Learning
items.description: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies have become a promising paradigm for end-to-end robot control, but their effectiveness still depends heavily on large volumes of demonstration data.
items.ai_summary: SURE is a data-efficient vision-language-action training framework that models spatial and temporal uncertainty using a probabilistic action decoder and Soft-DTW alignment to improve robotic manipulation performance.

items.title: The Multiscale Single-Index Model: An MSE Analysis of Online SGD Dynamics
items.description: We consider the Multiscale Single-Index Model (MSIM), first introduced by Oymak and Soltanolkotabi (2021), as a stylized model for hierarchical feature learning with scale separation.
items.ai_summary: This work analyzes joint online spherical SGD under MSE loss for the Multiscale Single-Index Model, proving that it achieves weak and strong recovery in hierarchical feature learning settings.

items.title: SPARSEUP: Towards Better Recipes for Training Modern Learned Sparse Retrievers
items.description: Learned sparse embeddings are a powerful alternative to dense retrieval, yet they have fallen behind single-vector and late interaction models.
items.ai_summary: SPARSEUP is a training recipe for Splade-like sparse encoders that uses logit distribution control, per-position fan-out capping, and vocabulary merging to improve efficiency and retrieval effectiveness.

items.title: Autonomous Particle Image Velocimetry Using Zero-Shot Sim-to-Real Reinforcement Learning
items.description: Particle image velocimetry (PIV) reconstructs a flow field from the motion of tracer particles but the reconstruction quality is bounded by how well the flow structure of interest is resolved in the images.
items.ai_summary: Autonomous Particle Image Velocimetry uses a zero-shot sim-to-real reinforcement learning agent to control a camera-equipped manipulator for locating and resolving hydrofoil wakes in water tunnels.

items.title: Goodhart in the Planner: Sampling-Based Control Exploits Rewards Learned from Human Preferences
items.description: Robots increasingly choose actions by searching against a reward model learned from human preferences, in model-predictive control or best-of-$N$ selection; we measure what this does to the true objective.
items.ai_summary: Sampling-based control algorithms using human-preference reward models can degrade true objective performance through reward hacking, which is mitigated by a proposed calibrated regularization rule.

items.title: Online Causal Configuration for Networked Systems via Doubly Robust Steady-State Learning
items.description: Measurement exploration reveals how interacting local controllers behave but can alter the steady-state regime a network operator seeks to optimize.
items.ai_summary: CAUSAL-UCB is an online causal configuration algorithm that uses an interference-aware clipped doubly robust evaluator to balance measurement exploration and target optimization in networked systems.

items.title: Dual Architecture Fusion Vehicle Lidar 3D Target Detection
items.description: In this paper, a 3D backbone network (SpconvTransformer) based on the fusion of convolutional architecture branch and Transformer architecture branch is proposed.
items.ai_summary: SpconvTransformer is a 3D target detection network that combines a sparse convolutional branch for local features with a Transformer branch for global context to improve vehicle lidar detection accuracy.

items.title: How Much Conversation History Does an AI Agent Need?
items.description: How does using less conversational history change reader-token use and benchmark scores? We examine this question on 1,100 BEAM questions.
items.ai_summary: An empirical analysis of conversation history length on AI agent performance shows how varying passage budgets and message retention impact token usage, benchmark scores, and task accuracy.

items.title: Video2Asset: Online Construction of Persistent 3D Street-Scene Assets
items.description: Online 3D street-scene asset construction turns multi-view video into a continually updated scene of independently editable objects.
items.ai_summary: Video2Asset is an online framework that converts multi-view videos into continually updated 3D street-scene assets with improved temporal identity consistency and reduced fragmentation.

items.title: Differentially Private GraphRAG: Protecting Relation Connectivity and Semantics
items.description: Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation (GraphRAG) connects information across documents through entity relationships to support relational reasoning.
items.ai_summary: RelGuard is a differentially private GraphRAG framework that protects relation connectivity and semantic meaning through relation removal to defend against reconstruction attacks.

items.title: Decoupled Mode Connectivity for Base-to-Novel Generalization in Vision-Language Models
items.description: Prompt learning adapts vision-language models such as CLIP by optimizing a short learnable prompt.
items.ai_summary: Decoupled Mode Connectivity is a prompt learning method that uses separate specialization and generalization prompts to improve base-to-novel generalization in vision-language models.

items.title: Breaking the Privacy Promise: Gradient Inversion Attacks on Federated Low-Rank Adapted Vision Transformers
items.description: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) has been increasingly adopted to fine-tune pretrained models with low computational cost and is therefore also preferred in the federated learning paradigm to reduce computational and communication overhead.
items.ai_summary: Spatially anchored generative inversion is a framework that uses server-prescribed trainable positional embeddings to improve gradient inversion reconstructions for LoRA-adapted Vision Transformers.

items.title: TensorMutation: Learning Weight-Space Mutations of Deep Learning Models on Neural Graphs
items.description: Mutation testing for deep learning (DL) faces a cost-realism trade-off.
items.ai_summary: TensorMutation is a method that represents trained models as neural graphs and uses a graph neural network to predict parameter changes for generating executable deep learning mutants without retraining.

items.title: NAVE: A Normalized, Adaptive Conformer for Antarctic Whale Vocalization Detection
items.description: Antarctic whale vocalization detection requires temporally localizing call boundaries in long underwater recordings and classifying them into predefined call types.
items.ai_summary: NAVE is a Conformer-based detector that combines per-bin complex mean subtraction, per-channel energy normalization, and a frequency-dynamic stem to accurately detect Antarctic whale vocalizations in noisy recordings.

items.title: Steerable Multi-Objective Group-Relative Preference Optimization with Jointly Trained Low-Rank Adapters
items.description: Language model deployment often requires different trade-offs between competing objectives as user preferences change, yet standard post-training methods typically produce a single policy for a fixed objective weighting.
items.ai_summary: LambdaMix is a parameter-efficient method that jointly trains low-rank adapters to create a preference-conditioned family of policies for multi-objective language model adaptation.

items.title: Encoding Memory in World Models with Test-Time Model-Based Reinforcement Learning
items.description: Model-based reinforcement learning (MBRL) approaches have demonstrated strong performance across diverse domains in recent years, learning accurate world models from agent trajectories.
items.ai_summary: Test-Time Model-Based Reinforcement Learning is an approach that uses gradient descent at test time to encode episode observations into world model parameters, improving long-term memory and planning.

items.title: BiLoGo: Reducing the smoothing of localised responses in Transformer-based neural operators for sheet forming
items.description: Trial-and-error FE simulation of sheet forming could be computationally expensive, neural-network-based learned simulators are used to accelerate design.
items.ai_summary: BiLoGo is a bipartite local-global learned simulator that combines node-element message passing with Transformer-based operators to reduce the smoothing of localized responses in sheet forming simulations.

items.title: CRTrack-Cap: A New Benchmark for Cross-View Dense Video Object Captioning
items.description: Dense video object captioning (DVOC) localizes, tracks, and describes object trajectories within a video. Existing methods process each camera view independently, producing separate camera-local tracklets and captions for the same person across cameras.
items.ai_summary: CRTrack-Cap is a benchmark and reference framework for cross-view dense video object captioning that associates tracklets into scene-level global trajectories and generates unified descriptions.

items.title: Contextual Search and Bilateral Trade with a Trace-Square-Root Potential
items.description: We present a unified potential method for contextual search and bilateral trade with one-bit feedback and obtain order-tight algorithms for both problems.
items.ai_summary: Algorithms for contextual search and bilateral trade achieve order-tight regret bounds using a unified trace-square-root potential method.

items.title: Know What You Need: Efficient Activation Checkpointing
items.description: Large Language Model training is increasingly constrained by memory capacity.
items.ai_summary: An approximate activation checkpointing method selectively recomputes important transformer layer components to reduce memory usage during large language model training.

items.title: Kernel-Based Learning of Analytic Operators and Parametric PDEs
items.description: We study kernel-based learning of analytic operators from finite samples, with a focus on how the regularity of the target should determine the choice of the kernel.
items.ai_summary: Kernel-based learning methods establish finite-sample error bounds and convergence rates for analytic operators and parametric partial differential equations.

items.title: Not Your Diary, Just Your Topic: Grading the Wrong-User Control
items.description: A common test of personalization replaces a user's history with someone else's and measures the drop in accuracy. But this swap also changes the topics in the history, so the drop may reflect topic mismatch.
items.ai_summary: Evaluations of language model personalization reveal that topic matching and evaluation on unseen users are critical for accurate benchmarking.

items.title: ReplayAudit: Auditing Outsourced LLM Fine-Tuning via Sealed Records and Selective Replay
items.description: Auditing outsourced LLM fine-tuning requires checking an untrusted provider's training while controlling verification cost. Uniform sampling ignores training-time signals, while checking a suspicious record can require replaying several preceding steps.
items.ai_summary: ReplayAudit uses telemetry-guided sampling and sealed training records to audit outsourced large language model fine-tuning with reduced verification costs.

items.title: Coresets for Capacitated Clustering via Dual Concentration
items.description: We study coresets for clustering problems, focusing on the classical $k$-median and $k$-means objectives. A coreset is a small weighted summary of the input data that approximately preserves the clustering cost for every choice of centers.
items.ai_summary: Coresets for capacitated clustering problems achieve optimal sizes and near-linear dependence on cluster counts by using dual concentration bounds.

items.title: Dual-Region Slice Aggregation for CT-Based Renal Tumor Classification
items.description: Clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) is the most common kidney cancer in adults. We present a region-aware architecture for CT-based ccRCC classification. Tumor and 0--10 mm peritumoral context are pooled separately from shared frozen DINOv3 feature maps.
items.ai_summary: A region-aware architecture pools tumor and peritumoral CT features with slice aggregation to improve clear cell renal cell carcinoma classification.

items.title: Transformer-FSQ: Discrete Latents for Extreme KV-Cache Compression
items.description: Private, personalised language models must run on local consumer devices, where large, frontier models cannot fit, and retaining long contexts is non-trivial.
items.ai_summary: Transformer-FSQ replaces standard key and value projections with a finite scalar quantization bottleneck to achieve extreme key-value cache compression.

items.title: RuACT: Recovering Inactive Rubrics as Adaptive Critics and Teachers
items.description: Rubric-based reinforcement learning (RL) extends RL with verifiable rewards to open-ended tasks by scoring each response against query-specific rubrics.
items.ai_summary: RuACT repurposes inactive rubrics as adaptive critics and teachers through reward-gated self-distillation and child rubric decomposition to improve reinforcement learning.

items.title: Coordinatewise Epsilon for Adam under Heavy-Tailed Noise
items.description: Adam estimates second moments coordinatewise, but typically adds the same scalar $\varepsilon$ to every denominator. We study how this shared $\varepsilon$ affects convergence when noise and curvature vary across coordinates.
items.ai_summary: Coordinatewise epsilon tuning for the Adam optimizer attains optimal convergence rates for smooth nonconvex stochastic optimization under heavy-tailed noise.

items.title: MSR-ABC: Complementary Feature Fusion for Clear Cell Renal Cell Carcinoma Classification
items.description: Clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) classification from computed tomography (CT) may benefit from representations that capture different aspects of tumour phenotype.
items.ai_summary: MSR-ABC is a global-local multi-source framework that integrates MedVAE, MedSigLIP, and radiomics for classifying clear cell renal cell carcinoma from CT scans.

items.title: Locally Adaptive Conformal Prediction for Polynomial Chaos Expansions
items.description: This work develops a locally adaptive jackknife+ conformal prediction framework for polynomial chaos expansions.
items.ai_summary: This paper proposes a locally adaptive conformal prediction framework for polynomial chaos expansions that achieves target coverage while adapting to local prediction uncertainty.

items.title: Half-precision inference of AI weather prediction models: negligible loss of skill at a fraction of the cost
items.description: AI weather prediction models are released with 32-bit (fp32) weights and run in fp32 by default, although current GPUs compute much faster in 16-bit formats.
items.ai_summary: Running AI weather prediction models in half-precision (fp16) on a single GPU speeds up 10-day forecasts significantly while maintaining negligible loss of skill.

items.title: Video Stitching from Multiple Moving Cameras
items.description: We address geometric video alignment for the same scene captured by multiple freely moving cameras.
items.ai_summary: MViS is a lightweight test-time optimization framework for joint multi-view video alignment that uses spatial-transformer-inspired networks to predict per-view homographies with temporal consistency.

items.title: Alignment by Confident Debate: Preference Learning from Multi-Agent Debate
items.description: Post-training language models for reasoning typically rely on gold answers, task-specific verifiers, or learned reward models, limiting scalability when such signals are scarce.
items.ai_summary: Alignment by Confident Debate converts multi-agent debate traces into preference data without gold answer labels to improve language model post-training for reasoning.

items.title: TurtLES: A Large-Scale Benchmark for Turbulent 3D Neural PDE Surrogates
items.description: Machine-learning surrogates are increasingly used to accelerate computational fluid dynamics, yet progress is limited by the lack of benchmarks capturing realistic, time-dependent turbulent flows.
items.ai_summary: TurtLES is a 14 terabyte benchmark dataset of 3D turbulent cylinder wakes designed for evaluating neural surrogate models in computational fluid dynamics.

items.title: Solver-Free Decision-Focused Learning via Neural Optimization Layers for Edge Selection
items.description: Decision-focused learning trains prediction models to improve downstream decisions, but many methods require costly solver calls or optimal-solution labels.
items.ai_summary: This paper proposes a solver-free decision-focused learning framework using neural optimization layers to produce fast, high-quality decisions for NP-hard edge-selection problems.

items.title: Optimal Regret for Profit Maximization in Bilateral Trade
items.description: Learning to profit from trade requires learning both sides of a market: what a seller is willing to accept and what a buyer is willing to pay.
items.ai_summary: This paper designs an algorithm for repeated bilateral trade that achieves optimal regret by learning seller acceptance and buyer payment prices from trade outcomes.

items.title: Query-Guided RoPE Modulation for Lost-in-the-Middle Mitigation in Long-Context LLMs
items.description: Long-context language models often neglect information in the middle of the input, a phenomenon known as "lost-in-the-middle". Part of this gap may stem from the long-range decay of rotary position embedding (RoPE), which weakens the positional signal between distant tokens.
items.ai_summary: QGPM is a training-free method that uses query relevance to reshape rotary position embeddings, mitigating the lost-in-the-middle phenomenon in long-context language models.

items.title: CoMoFlow: Controllable Protein Conformational Ensemble Generation via Explicit Collective-Mode Modeling
items.description: Protein conformational ensemble generation aims to efficiently characterize the structural variations accessible to a protein beyond a single static structure.
items.ai_summary: CoMoFlow is a controllable framework that generates protein backbone conformational ensembles by explicitly modeling collective variation to guide SE(3) flow matching.

items.title: Marginal-Nonuniform Multiclass Learning
items.description: We study the problem of multiclass classification within the framework of marginal-nonuniform learning, where the constants in the learning rate may depend on the unknown marginal distribution generating the unlabeled data, but not on the target concept.
items.ai_summary: Marginal-nonuniform learning framework for multiclass classification characterizes optimal learning rates into exponential, linear, and arbitrarily slow rates using a new uncentered DS-eluder dimension.

items.title: CID: Measuring Cognitive Work Through Semantic State Change
items.description: Traditional information theory provides powerful tools for analyzing statistical properties of information but offers limited insight into meaning and semantic transformation. It has never been possible to quantify the meaning of an arbitrary piece of information.
items.ai_summary: Contextual Information Differential metric measures semantic displacement and cognitive work in large language models by treating meaning as a geometric property within high-dimensional semantic spaces.

items.title: Multimodal Training with Knowledge Traction for Video Anomaly Detection
items.description: The task of weakly supervised video anomaly detection is challenging. Existing approaches mainly model video frame features and determine whether anomalies are present based on their magnitudes.
items.ai_summary: Multimodal training method for video anomaly detection integrates textual prompts, large language models, and dictionary learning to improve model performance, robustness, and generalization.

items.title: Graph representations of dislocation networks
items.description: The mechanical response of a crystal is governed by the evolving network of dislocations it contains, yet quantitatively linking the `state of that network' to its yield stress remains challenging.
items.ai_summary: Random forest model predicts crystal yield stress from graph topologies of dislocation networks, successfully linking microstructural states to mechanical responses.

items.title: PreForceVision: Physics-Guided Optical Estimation of Bolt Preload from Bolt-Head Deformation
items.description: Bolt preload is a decisive functional quantity in bolted joints because it determines whether external loads are transmitted primarily through frictional clamping or directly through the bolt.
items.ai_summary: PreForceVision is a physics-guided optical framework that estimates bolt preload by analyzing surface deformations on the bolt-head front face from reference-loaded image pairs.

items.title: StockASkill: A Local-First AgentSkill for Intelligent Stock Selection
items.description: Quantitative equity selection and portfolio construction in emerging and cross-border markets frequently suffer from computational bottlenecks, remote API fragility, survivorship bias, and rigid execution constraints such as discrete board lots and investor-mandated drawdown…
items.ai_summary: StockASkill is a local-first agent skill and quantitative co-processor that uses a DuckDB engine and a convex optimizer to accelerate equity screening and portfolio construction for AI agents.

items.title: ExQuery: Explicit Structured Query Priors for Temporal 3D Object Detection
items.description: Sparse query-based 3D detectors commonly encode heterogeneous semantic, geometric, and motion information into unified latent queries, including when explicit 3D anchors are used. We introduce ExQuery, an explicit structured query framework for temporal 3D object detection.
items.ai_summary: ExQuery is an explicit structured query framework for temporal 3D object detection that organizes queries into semantic and physical-state slices to improve detection performance.

items.title: RadarDINO: Distilling a Visual Foundation Model into mmWave Radar for Human Mesh Reconstruction
items.description: Millimeter-wave (mmWave) radar offers a privacy-preserving and illumination-robust alternative for human mesh reconstruction (HMR). However, high-fidelity radar HMR remains challenging.
items.ai_summary: RadarDINO is a human mesh reconstruction framework that distills visual semantics from a DINOv3 teacher into 3D millimeter-wave radar representations to improve reconstruction accuracy.

items.title: Atik: A Shared-Mesh Transformer Accelerator for RISC-V
items.description: Transformer inference repeatedly invokes dense matrix multiplication and attention, including its data-dependent softmax normalization.
items.ai_summary: Atik is an open-source accelerator for RISC-V that speeds up transformer inference by executing matrix multiplication and dense attention through a shared fixed-point MAC mesh.

items.title: Embedding Predictive Adaptation and Refinement for Multi-Modal Industrial Anomaly Detection
items.description: Industrial Anomaly Detection (IAD) has evolved from 2D image-based approaches to multi-modal methods that leverage the complementary nature of RGB images and 3D point clouds.
items.ai_summary: EPAR is a multi-modal industrial anomaly detection method that adapts pretrained encoders by predicting masked region embeddings and refines coarse anomaly maps using a noise suppression network.

items.title: Active Learning of Robust Models
items.description: In many domains from species identification to cancer diagnosis, labelling data to train predictive models remains costly.
items.ai_summary: Active learning strategy that efficiently trains classifiers to generalize under subpopulation shifts by leveraging metadata as a proxy for underlying subgroups.

items.title: Benchmarking Speaker Embedders in the Sub-Second Regime for Real-Time Voice AI Agents
items.description: Real-time Voice AI agents must separate the active user from intelligible background speech that survives conventional noise suppression. Background sources include television audio, family members, and colleagues.
items.ai_summary: Evaluation of open-source speaker embedders under sub-second latency budgets to provide deployment guidance for real-time voice AI agents filtering background speech.

items.title: A Physics-Informed Learning Framework for Linking Microscopic Surface Degradation to Bolted Joint Functional Behavior
items.description: Returned products in circular engineering often have heterogeneous degradation histories, making remaining function difficult to assess. For bolted joints, corrosion alters surface morphology, contact, friction, preload retention, and mechanical response.
items.ai_summary: Physics-informed multimodal framework that links microscopic and camera-based corrosion observations to functional indicators of degraded bolted joints.

items.title: V-STORM: A Structure-Aware Grounded Chain of Thought Dataset for Faithful and Fine-Grained Spatio-Temporal Video Reasoning
items.description: While MLLMs can often identify what happens in a video, they still struggle with fine-grained spatio-temporal reasoning, which requires precise grounding when and where the supporting evidence appears and composing such evidence into a coherent reasoning chain.
items.ai_summary: Structure-aware framework that transforms videos into scene graphs and derives a grounded chain of thought dataset for faithful spatio-temporal video reasoning.

items.title: On the Effectiveness and Limitations of Open-Weight LLMs for Low-Resource Offensive Language Detection in Danish
items.description: We study the effectiveness and robustness of open-weight large language models (LLMs) for Danish offensive language detection, an underexplored low-resource task.
items.ai_summary: Study evaluating open-weight large language models and prompt strategies for low-resource Danish offensive language detection.

items.title: BEiTScore++: Reference-free Image Captioning Evaluation with BEiT-3 and Conformalized Quantile Regression
items.description: Reliable uncertainty estimation is important for deploying evaluation metrics in real-world settings, where both input ambiguity and domain shifts are common.
items.ai_summary: Uncertainty-aware image captioning metric that uses conformalized quantile regression to produce confidence intervals alongside alignment scores.

items.title: TimeOmni-Live: Continuous & Live Time Series Understanding with Long-Term Memory
items.description: Existing time series language models predominantly follow an offline, one-shot paradigm: they process fixed-length inputs independently and do not retain past states.
items.ai_summary: Live time series understanding model equipped with hybrid encoding and persistent memory for continuous streaming tasks.

items.title: e-means: outperforming k-means (in one-tenth the epochs)
items.description: Lloyd's k-means algorithm is a long-running standard for clustering, with applications in data analysis, retrieval, quantization and data curation.
items.ai_summary: Exponential moving average optimization procedure for k-means clustering that achieves faster convergence and lower losses on large embedding datasets.

items.title: Mosaic:montage-agnostic self-distilled graph learning for subject-independent ieeg seizure detection
items.description: Intracranial EEG provides high signal-to-noise ratio and spatial resolution for detecting epileptic activity, but patient-specific electrode placement leads to substantial variation in channel count and montage across subjects.
items.ai_summary: Lightweight graph-learning framework that enables subject-independent iEEG seizure detection across varying electrode placements and channel counts.

items.title: FusionCLIP: Multimodal Contrastive Pretraining for Fusion Plasma Diagnostics
items.description: Visible-light videos and multivariate diagnostic signals provide complementary observations of tokamak discharges.
items.ai_summary: Multimodal contrastive pretraining framework that aligns visible-light videos with asynchronous diagnostic signals to improve fusion plasma property predictions.

items.title: An Effective Spoken Language Understanding Approach Leveraging Query-Adaptive Intent Detection
items.description: Large language models enable fine-tuning-free spoken language understanding (SLU) through in-context learning, but direct query-based retrieval may select semantically similar yet intent irrelevant demonstrations.
items.ai_summary: Query-Adaptive Intent Detection via Prototype Extraction (APEX) is a two-stage retrieval framework that improves spoken language understanding accuracy by selecting intent-level prototypes before retrieving contextual exemplars.

items.title: LEMMO: A Large Electromagnetic Model leveraging Pretrained LLMs for Million-Sample Signal Understanding
items.description: Large language models have expanded beyond text to vision, audio, and other modalities, but understanding raw electromagnetic (EM) signals remains challenging.
items.ai_summary: LEMMO is a large electromagnetic model combining a linear-attention encoder and pretrained language models to process long raw IQ recordings for instruction-driven signal recognition and description.

items.title: ENGRAM: From Agent Experience to Weights through Verified Consolidation
items.description: Language-model agents use experience through external retrieval and parameter learning. Consolidating stored experience into model weights requires deciding both which experience to train on and when its external records can leave retrieval.
items.ai_summary: ENGRAM is a framework that separates training admission from memory release to consolidate language-model agent experience into model weights through verified consolidation.

items.title: Consensus-Constrained Dual-Federated Optimization with Client-Side Dynamic Weighting for Distributed Android Device Threat Defense
items.description: Smartphones, smart-home hubs, and wearables are increasingly exposed to sophisticated Android malware, while centralized threat-detection pipelines raise privacy and scalability concerns.
items.ai_summary: DW-FedADMM is a federated optimization framework combining primal-dual coordination and performance-dependent client-side weighting to improve distributed Android malware detection.

items.title: Left-Right-Consistent Iterative Stereo Matching via Cross-Injection
items.description: State-of-the-art stereo matching models predominantly predict the disparity of only the left (reference) view. However, applications such as per-eye AR/VR rendering, novel view synthesis, or two-view depth fusion require disparity for both views, and need those two maps to agree.
items.ai_summary: Cross-injection is a lightweight extension for iterative stereo matching models that injects signed left-right inconsistency to reduce disparity disagreement between views.

items.title: Definitions, Label Names, or Demonstrations? Auditing What Governs LLM Annotation
items.description: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to annotate social-science texts, but high accuracy does not establish that they apply researcher-supplied category definitions: predictions may instead reflect prior associations with category labels or labeled demonstrations.
items.ai_summary: Counterfactual auditing reveals that large language models used for text annotation largely rely on category labels and training examples rather than researcher-supplied definitions.

items.title: Overview of the ImageCLEFmedical 2026 GANs task: Exploring fingerprint detection, privacy leakage, and synthetic medical image generation
items.description: The 2026 ImageCLEFmedical GANs Task Exploring Fingerprint Detection, Privacy Leakage, and Synthetic Medical Image Generation continues to investigate privacy and security concerns around using patient data to generate synthetic medical images, now in its fourth edition.
items.ai_summary: The 2026 ImageCLEFmedical GANs task provides datasets and evaluation subtasks for exploring fingerprint detection, latent vector reversibility, and privacy-preserving medical image generation.

items.title: From LoRA to Language: Recovering Skill Documents from Adapters
items.description: Agent skills are short documents that teach a language model how to handle a class of tasks.
items.ai_summary: The Executing Writer is a small writer model trained on top of an adapted model to recover readable skill documents and instructions from low-rank adapters.

items.title: Not All Entropy Is Equal: Reward-Conditioned Entropy Allocation in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards
items.description: Policy entropy is widely used to diagnose exploration and collapse in reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR), yet its magnitude does not consistently track reasoning performance across optimization objectives.
items.ai_summary: Reward-Conditioned Entropy Allocation (RCEA) is a hierarchical diagnostic framework that separates and conditions reinforcement learning uncertainty on verifier outcomes and process validity.

items.title: Logit Laundering: Evading Data-Use Auditing in Large Language Models
items.description: Data-use auditing in Large Language Models (LLMs) aims to determine whether the given data has been used for training, thereby supporting data ownership safeguards.
items.ai_summary: Logit Laundering is an evasion framework that manipulates model outputs in the logit space at inference time to suppress watermarking signals and evade data-use auditing.

items.title: The Role Of Recurrent Refinement In Medical Image Segmentation
items.description: While feed-forward segmentation networks perform well on large cohorts, they degrade in constrained clinical settings with few training samples and imaging artifacts.
items.ai_summary: Lightweight recurrent refinement blocks added to segmentation backbones improve performance on clean data and under noise in medical image segmentation.

items.title: DexDICE: Reconciling Safety and Performance via Dual-Expert Offline Imitation Learning
items.description: Ensuring high returns while providing strong safety guarantees in offline imitation learning (IL) is a fundamental challenge: existing approaches either rely on explicitly specified cost functions, which are difficult to design for complex real-world safety constraints, or…
items.ai_summary: DexDICE combines offline learning with safe support constraints to balance high returns and safety in dual-expert offline imitation learning.

items.title: MINE: Entropy-coded Memory-efficient Inference for Large Language Models
items.description: We present MINE (Memory-efficient INference Engine), a lossless entropy coding approach that accelerates single-stream inference of Large Language Models (LLMs), where existing lossless compression methods yield speedups only for specific data types such as \texttt{BF16} and…
items.ai_summary: MINE is a lossless entropy coding engine that accelerates single-stream large language model inference by optimizing weight compression and decoding latency.

items.title: Agentic AI for Healthcare Claim Denial Analysis: A Policy-Grounded Framework for Privacy Preservation
items.description: In the healthcare sector, claim denials impose significant financial and administrative burdens, emphasizing the need for automated and trustworthy decision-support systems.
items.ai_summary: An agentic AI framework integrates predictive analytics, graph-based learning, and policy-grounded retrieval to automate healthcare claim denial analysis while preserving privacy.

items.title: Future-Informed Actor-Critic
items.description: Actor-critic methods optimize a parametrized policy using a critic to estimate their policy gradient. Recent work has shown that conditioning the critic on features of future states, actions, or rewards can improve sample efficiency and even final return.
items.ai_summary: The future-informed actor-critic algorithm conditions value functions on both exogenous and endogenous future features to improve sample efficiency in reinforcement learning.

items.title: Typed-Centrality Grounding for Agentic GraphRAG: A Symbolic Approach for Agentic Reasoning
items.description: Knowledge Graphs (KGs) and Large Language Models (LLMs) represent two approaches for knowledge representation and reasoning over heterogeneous data.
items.ai_summary: A typed-centrality grounding approach combines symbolic knowledge graph reasoning with large language models to improve consistency in GraphRAG systems.

items.title: SmartBloch-Agent: An Agentic Framework for Automated MRI Sequence Design and Optimization
items.description: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) pulse sequences organize radiofrequency excitation, gradient encoding, and signal acquisition, determining magnetization evolution and image formation.
items.ai_summary: SmartBloch-Agent is an AI-driven framework that automates the design, simulation, and optimization of magnetic resonance imaging pulse sequences from natural language objectives.

items.title: MIRA: Mitigating Pole Geometry Bias in Recurrent Language Models
items.description: We show that the Transformer's recurrent successors --- such as selective state-space models (SSMs), Receptance Weighted Key Value (RWKV), and Retentive Network (RetNet) --- can be characterized as infinite-impulse-response (IIR) systems.
items.ai_summary: Mira is a linear-time recurrent architecture that uses a lattice-ladder structure to eliminate pole geometry bias in recurrent language models.

items.title: DataHelix: A CPU-GPU Co-Scheduling Data Plane for Multimodal Model Training
items.description: Multimodal model training breaks the loose coupling between data loading and model execution assumed by conventional training pipelines.
items.ai_summary: DataHelix is a CPU-GPU co-scheduling data plane that coordinates data preprocessing and execution across ranks to reduce pipeline stalls in multimodal model training.

items.title: ROAM: Retrieval-Augmented Optimization for Feasible Multi-Day Itinerary Planning
items.description: Large language models (LLMs) can draft plausible travel itineraries, but the plans they produce are frequently infeasible: attractions are grouped into days without regard for geography, opening hours are ignored, and a single generation pass cannot reliably organize a…
items.ai_summary: ROAM couples semantic preference retrieval with spatiotemporal optimization to generate feasible, map-ready multi-day travel itineraries using large language models.

items.title: A Spiking Neural Model of the Mental Lexicon: Representations, Similarity Structure, and Associative Retrieval in Perception and Production
items.description: A neural account of lexical access requires an explicit distinction between the structure of lexical representations, the associations linking representational levels, and the activity generated during retrieval.
items.ai_summary: A spiking neural implementation of the mental lexicon uses the Semantic Pointer Architecture to simulate perception and production pathways across 613 lexical entries.

items.title: PhyCAD: Physics-Aware Text-to-CAD Generation via Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning
items.description: Language-driven computer-aided design (CAD) generation enables the creation of editable parametric models from text, yet geometric correctness alone does not ensure physical feasibility.
items.ai_summary: PhyCAD proposes a physics-aware framework using hierarchical reinforcement learning to train language models to generate executable CAD programs meeting geometric and physical constraints.

items.title: Causal graph fusion across incomplete cohorts and causal steering of tabular foundation models
items.description: Clinical data are split across incomplete cohorts with partially overlapping variables. Causal discovery under missing data and multi-source integration have developed separately, and tabular foundation models cannot take a causal graph without retraining.
items.ai_summary: Causal graph fusion integrates incomplete cohorts and causal attention steering improves the discrimination of frozen tabular foundation models under distribution shift.

items.title: Frontier3DBench: Benchmarking Coding Agents for 3D Creation across Objects, Scenes, and Interactive Open Worlds
items.description: A unified 145-task benchmark evaluates coding agents across object, scene, and interactive 3D creation, revealing reference fidelity and coordinated activity completion as central bottlenecks.

items.title: OmniLatent: Unified Latent for 3D Part Modeling
items.description: OmniLatent jointly models geometry, deformation, appearance, and part identities in a shared latent space to generate and interactively edit part-aware 3D assets from images or point prompts.

items.title: Exploring Weight-Space Programming: Capabilities, Generalization, and Limitations
items.description: Weight-Space Programming can produce large localized accuracy gains and uneven cross-task transfer, but reliable editing remains inconsistent.

items.title: The Last Mile to the Real World: Agent-Native Primitives as Reusable Building Blocks for Solving Real-World Tasks
items.description: A harness engineering framework composes reusable LLM-equipped primitives into task-specific graphs, verifies and revises them, and improves agent success on real-world tasks while reducing time and cost.

items.title: Beneath the Surface: What We Overlook When We Talk About Agent Evolution
items.description: Agent harness evolution can improve benchmark performance without weight updates, but gains are unreliable, costly, and transfer inconsistently, motivating preservation-aware evaluation and EvoAudit revisions.

items.title: ryph-hq/ryph
items.description: 🤖 Self-hosted coding agents for your team: on call for your incidents, in your chat, on your forge.
items.ai_summary: Self-hosted agent orchestrator that deploys sandbox environments for automated incident response, debugging, and hotfix pull requests.

items.title: Confucius4-R2T2: A Stable-Prefix Streaming ASR Model for Real Real-Time Transcription
items.description: A full-context speech recognizer is adapted to emit immutable streaming transcripts with near full-context accuracy and low latency by learning longest stable prefix labels.

items.title: AI is destroying my CS degree
items.description: My comment on AI is destroying my CS degree — Hacker News. I don't envy educators right now. AI clearly means you need to change how you teach and evaluate students.

items.title: Sketchpad: certified exact arithmetic with a small vision-language model
items.description: A language model with a low-rank adapter and bounded external memory can be certified exact for arbitrary-length arithmetic by checking finitely many views, and it performs multiple exact arithmetic procedures on a laptop browser.

items.title: OneTrans-GSR: A Generative Slate Ranking Paradigm Unifying Reranking and Mix-Ranking with One Autoregressive Transformer
