items.title: User Embeddings are Superpositions of Interpretable Behavioral Modes
items.description: User embeddings are central components of modern recommendation, personalization, and behavioral modeling systems. Though these embeddings can compactly encode rich behavioral information, they are inherently dense and opaque, limiting interpretability.
items.ai_summary: Research paper proposing a post-hoc, model-agnostic framework using sparse autoencoders to recover interpretable behavioral modes from opaque user embeddings for recommendation systems.

items.title: Do You Miss the Nights We Spent Crafting Figures? Rethinking Teaser and Framework Figures in the Age of Generative AI
items.description: Scientific figures give research ideas a visual form through choices of abstraction, composition, and emphasis. Generative AI offers new ways to realize these choices, raising questions about explanatory clarity and purposeful visual expression.
items.ai_summary: Research paper examining 371 scientific figures to find that generative AI revisions can increase clarity ratings while decreasing aesthetic coherence.

items.title: Where and Why is Grounded Reasoning Useful?
items.description: Grounded reasoning, where a model outputs text coordinates of relevant locations in chain-of-thought reasoning, is a common strategy for solving complex visual reasoning problems. However, the benefits and limitations of grounded reasoning are understudied.
items.ai_summary: Method that studies where and why grounded reasoning is useful, finding it improves counting and helps when tasks require undescribable visual references.

items.title: SwarmEvolve: Latent Agent Swarms for Evolutionary Discovery and Optimization
items.description: LLM-guided evolutionary search uses AI agents to improve programs for mathematical and computational problems by iteratively refining solutions and combining high-scoring methods.
items.ai_summary: Framework called SwarmEvolve that uses latent agent swarms to perform fast and low-cost program search for mathematical discovery and scientific computing.

items.title: Scientist World: Grow a Research World for AI-Scientists
items.description: AI-Scientists arrived, but a world for them to grow in did not. Human scientists take theirs for granted $-$ centuries of open problems and shared ideas, waiting in the scientific literature.
items.ai_summary: Evaluation environment called Scientist World where every research paper becomes an executable environment to assess and train autonomous AI-scientists.

items.title: EgoGeneralist: Unifying Egocentric Action-Video Tasks through Video-Native Modeling
items.description: Modern video models possess strong visual priors, yet do not natively represent human action in metric 3D space.
items.ai_summary: Framework called EgoGeneralist that adapts pretrained video generators to unify action-conditioned egocentric video generation, pose estimation, and joint action-video learning.

items.title: XStack: A Benchmark for ML Repo Migration
items.description: ML code should run where researchers choose, not where it was first written. Today, machine learning code mainly lives in two ecosystems, PyTorch on NVIDIA GPUs and JAX on Google TPUs. Migrating repositories between them means building and testing across frameworks and hardware.
items.ai_summary: Benchmark called XStack that evaluates coding agents on migrating machine learning repositories between PyTorch and JAX frameworks and hardware ecosystems.

items.title: Same Behavior, Different Mechanism: What Finite Experiments Can Certify About Integrated Information
items.description: Interpretability, AI auditing and assessments of machine consciousness increasingly rest on mechanism-level quantities: functionals of a system's causal transition law that describe how it computes, not what it outputs.

items.title: Towards interpreting any residual stream direction by scaling activation inversion
items.description: To interpret a direction in a language model's residual stream, we can look for text that strongly activates it. But when such text is found by scanning a corpus, it is limited to what that corpus contains.
items.ai_summary: Language models called Maximally-Activating Example Metamodels that map residual stream directions to text exemplars that strongly activate those directions.

items.title: Adversarial Training with Large Step Sizes: Implicit Bias, Optimization, and Sharpness
items.description: Adversarial Training (AT) is an important method for improving model robustness. We study the dynamics of deterministic Gradient Descent (GD) in AT. Most existing works in this direction focus on the small or vanishing step sizes regime, where GD resembles a continuous-time flow.
items.ai_summary: Study analyzing the dynamics of deterministic gradient descent with large step sizes in adversarial training to understand implicit bias, optimization, and loss sharpness.

items.title: Unpacking the Compute Efficiency of Strong-to-Weak OPD against GRPO
items.description: On-policy distillation (OPD) trains a student on its own rollouts under a frozen teacher's per-token supervision. Does this dense signal reduce the training FLOPs needed to reach a target accuracy compared with reinforcement learning?
items.ai_summary: Systematic comparison between on-policy distillation and group relative policy optimization to measure compute efficiency and accuracy across various tasks and models.

items.title: ReproBridge: Building Reproducibility into ML Research Artifacts
items.description: Reproducing machine learning experiments requires reconstructing procedures from information scattered across papers, released code, and supporting artifacts.
items.ai_summary: Agent workflow called ReproBridge that constructs standardized, reproducible machine learning artifacts to improve reproduction success rates and reduce downstream API spending.

items.title: VFlash: Fast, Accurate Visual Planning via Flash Primitive Decoding
items.description: Models for physical AI tasks, such as robotics and autonomous driving, need not reason solely in language. They can use visual plans--points, bounding boxes, and trajectories--to represent spatial goals and anticipate motion.

items.title: A Hidden Markov Preference Model for Online Prediction of Adversary Actions
items.description: A defender anticipating an attacker needs a probability distribution over the attacker's next action from information available before that action occurs.
items.ai_summary: Hidden Markov preference model for online prediction of adversary actions that uses a feasibility-masked tree of executable actions and achieves high filtering performance on cyber defense benchmarks.

items.title: Edge-Assisted Crowdsensing for Explainable Cyclist Safety Perception
items.description: Cyclist fatality rates remain high despite policy support for active travel, and autonomous vehicles add complexity to mixed traffic. Neither crash statistics nor multi-model detection pipelines scale to continuous monitoring of perceived safety along a route.
items.ai_summary: Edge-assisted crowdsensing system combining handlebar cameras, a vision-language model, and an explainable boosting machine to predict cyclist safety perception scores and attribute ratings to road infrastructure features.

items.title: Label-Wording Augmentation in a Typed-Decision Encoder: Gains on Unfamiliar Words, Not on Abbreviations or Codes
items.description: Typed-decision models score options that the caller supplies at request time, so their accuracy depends on label wording that the model's developer does not control.
items.ai_summary: Typed-decision cross-encoder model evaluation showing that label-wording augmentation improves accuracy on ordinary or borrowed words but provides no usable gain on abbreviations or opaque codes.

items.title: Understanding AI from the Inside: The State of Mechanistic Interpretability for AI Safety
items.description: Neural networks are likely to be among the most consequential artefacts in human history. As these systems become more capable and autonomous, their potential to cause societal harm also grows, making AI safety one of the defining challenges of our time.
items.ai_summary: Survey of mechanistic interpretability for AI safety that examines internal model representations, features, circuits, and training-data attribution to evaluate how understanding model mechanisms improves safety.

items.title: SM4RT: Cascaded Feed-forward Model for 4D Reconstruction
items.description: We introduce SM4RT, a multi-task cascade feed-forward model for dynamic scene reconstruction from RGB videos.
items.ai_summary: SM4RT is a cascaded feed-forward model that sequentially reconstructs 3D geometry and estimates 3D motion from RGB videos to improve dynamic scene reconstruction and motion estimation.

items.title: MedGraph: Maintaining Patient State with Graph Memory for Long-Term Medical Dialogue
items.description: LLM-based medical assistants that follow a patient across visits need a memory that keeps the patient's clinical state correct as it changes.
items.ai_summary: MedGraph is a graph memory system for long-term medical dialogue assistants that tracks changing patient states by extracting dated facts and linking medical records into chains.

items.title: The Power of Meta Access in the Software of the Future --- Demonstrated on LLM Chat UIs and Chat AI
items.description: Chat remains the default surface for many large language model (LLM) tasks, even as agentic tools such as OpenCode excel at coding and automation. Yet the model sees the current dialogue but not the workspace around it.
items.ai_summary: Meta Chat prototype that gives large language model chat interfaces a structured, permissioned view of application state to turn chat into a control layer for the entire workspace.

items.title: Failure Prediction and Classification in Vision-Language-Action Models Via Calibrated Latent Probing
items.description: Vision-Language-Action models (VLAs) enable general-purpose embodied intelligence, but their performance is brittle under distribution shift, where unanticipated failures can damage equipment or endanger people.
items.ai_summary: VLA-Tug is a lightweight probe over vision-language-action model latent layers that enables early failure detection, classification, and runtime safety monitoring on edge devices.

items.title: Data-driven discovery of intrinsic Lie point symmetries of differential equation systems
items.description: Discovering continuous symmetries directly from differential-equation data can reveal geometric structure for model reduction and scientific machine learning without symbolic determining equations or a closed-form representation of the governing system.
items.ai_summary: Data-driven framework that formulates intrinsic Lie point-symmetry discovery as an operator-theoretic problem to recover continuous symmetries directly from differential equation data.

items.title: On the limitations of molecular representations
items.description: Molecular representations such as fingerprints and learned embeddings play a central role in cheminformatics and small-molecule machine learning.
items.ai_summary: Systematic investigation of molecular representations finding that current embedding models do not capture graph structure or 3D shape better than classical fingerprints, which also suffer from non-unique representations.

items.title: Benchmarks as Software: Terminal-Bench and the Case for Continuous Benchmarks
items.description: Coding agents are among the most economically consequential deployments of LLMs to date, making reliable evaluation increasingly important. Yet even benchmarks that are carefully validated at release can become stale.
items.ai_summary: This paper introduces a continuous-validation workflow for agentic benchmarks, demonstrating its effectiveness on Terminal-Bench 2.1 to correct maintenance debt and improve evaluation accuracy.

items.title: Spectral and Subspace Dynamics of LoRA in Supervised Fine-Tuning and Reinforcement Learning
items.description: Low-rank adaptation (LoRA) is commonly used in both supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and reinforcement learning (RL), often under similar optimizer settings. Yet, how the different dynamics of the two stages manifest in the low-rank increment that LoRA optimizes remains unclear.
items.ai_summary: This paper analyzes the spectral and subspace dynamics of LoRA in supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning, showing how group-mean baseline subtraction drives differences and proposing tailored configurations for each stage.

items.title: T3R: Training-Free Two-Stage Token Refinement Towards Efficient and Robust VLA Models
items.description: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models enable end-to-end robot control, but inference is increasingly expensive.
items.ai_summary: This paper proposes T3R, a training-free two-stage token pruning and attention-biasing framework that improves the accuracy-efficiency frontier of vision-language-action models for robot control.

items.title: The Gold Rush in AI4Math, II: What are signatures of AI-assisted Proofs?
items.description: The growing use of AI in mathematics raises a question: can we detect AI involvement in proofs, separately from AI assistance with writing?
items.ai_summary: This paper introduces ProofTrace, a graph-based framework that extracts interpretable features of mathematical organization to detect AI involvement and recurring signatures in mathematical proofs.

items.title: Conformal Prediction for Time-Dependent PDEs
items.description: Uncertainty quantification is crucial in scientific machine learning, where models inform safety-critical tasks such as flood forecasting, financial risk management, and thermal control in machines.
items.ai_summary: This paper investigates conformal prediction for surrogate models of time-dependent partial differential equations, proving theoretical limitations on exact coverage and presenting a weighted conformal prediction method for finite-sample guarantees.

items.title: Social Humanoid: Socially Responsive Human-Humanoid Interaction
items.description: Humanoid robots are typically trained as solitary agents, leaving them unable to coordinate physically with human partners who naturally anticipate and adjust to one another.
items.ai_summary: This paper presents Social Humanoid, a hierarchical system that generates socially responsive whole-body motion for humanoid robots conditioned on human partner dynamics using a new interaction benchmark.

items.title: StepBack: Step-Level Error-Localized Resampling for Efficient Test-Time Reasoning
items.description: Self-consistency (SC) is a widely used decoding strategy for improving chain-of-thought reasoning, but it requires sampling many complete reasoning trajectories with a preset budget.
items.ai_summary: This paper proposes StepBack, a step-level error-localized resampling method for test-time reasoning that reduces token usage while matching the accuracy of standard self-consistency.

items.title: Synthesis of Ovarian Cancer Multi-Omics Datasets: A Biology-Informed Evaluation Framework
items.description: Paired multi-omic cancer cohorts are costly to assemble and difficult to share, motivating synthetic cohorts as a complementary resource.
items.ai_summary: This paper introduces a biology-informed and patient-disjoint evaluation framework to assess whether synthetic multi-omic cancer cohorts preserve modality-specific fidelity and cross-modality coherence.

items.title: Adaptive Low-Light Enhancement for Road Anomaly Detection: A Multi-Architecture Benchmark and Edge Deployment Study
items.description: Road anomaly detection systems on autonomous vehicles must function reliably under degraded visual conditions including darkness, rain, and Harmattan dust haze.
items.ai_summary: This paper benchmarks object detection models under degraded visual conditions and proposes a lightweight luminance-adaptive router that selects appropriate low-light enhancement strategies for road anomaly detection.

items.title: Learning a patient world model for health system simulation in intensive care
items.description: Designing healthcare strategies requires anticipating their clinical and operational consequences before implementation, a task that often relies on health system simulation. Such a simulation necessitates modeling how patient states evolve and generate care demands.
items.ai_summary: This paper proposes a neural network-based patient world model learned from longitudinal electronic health records to provide a shared clinical representation for health system simulations in intensive care.

items.title: Hybrid Machine Learning for Imbalanced Landing-Phase Safety Event Prediction from Flight Data
items.description: Landing-phase safety-event prediction requires the detection of rare abnormal approaches within strongly imbalanced multivariate flight data.
items.ai_summary: Interpretable hybrid feature-fusion framework that combines an LSTM autoencoder and a class-weighted XGBoost classifier to predict multiclass landing-phase safety events from flight data with high recall.

items.title: FedReason: Large Language Models as Weight-Space Meta-Aggregators for Heterogeneous Federated Learning
items.description: Federated learning servers combine client models with a fixed aggregation rule, and each rule in common use is designed for one kind of heterogeneity.
items.ai_summary: FedReason framework that uses a large language model on the server to select customized aggregation programs for heterogeneous federated learning without server-side training.

items.title: Module-Aware Optimization for Graph Neural Networks
items.description: GraphMuon adapts Muon's matrix orthogonalization to the covariance of graph-propagated representations, reducing graph-induced update amplification and speeding validation-loss time-to-target on graph benchmarks.
items.ai_summary: GraphMuon is a graph-aware optimizer that adapts matrix-aware updates to graph-propagated representations, accelerating validation-loss convergence on large-scale graph neural network benchmarks.

items.title: Muir: Linear Attention with Sensitivity-Allocated Gating and Matched-Filter Readout
items.description: A linear attention architecture called Muir allocates gate capacity by sensitivity, uses matched-filter readout and a stable parallel update, improving language modeling, long-context recall, and training speed over Gated DeltaNet-2 and Transformer baselines.
items.ai_summary: Muir is a linear attention model that uses sensitivity-allocated low-rank gating and matched-filter readout to improve perplexity and reasoning accuracy over existing architectures.

items.title: MOMASPLAT: Dynamic Novel-View Demonstration Augmentation for Mobile Manipulation
items.description: Visuomotor policies trained through imitation learning are highly sensitive to changes in camera viewpoint.
items.ai_summary: Momasplat is a demonstration augmentation framework for mobile manipulation that combines 3D Gaussian Splatting and foundation models to synthesize full trajectories with dynamic object interactions from unseen base poses.

items.title: NPCBench: A Clinical Apprenticeship Benchmark for Multimodal Care-Pathway Reasoning in Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma
items.description: NPCBench evaluates whether medical AI models can integrate subspecialty knowledge with multimodal evidence and maintain temporally coherent diagnostic and care decisions across longitudinal nasopharyngeal carcinoma patient pathways.

items.title: VisionSIM: Beyond Idealized Sensors - A Multi-Modal Simulator for Robot Perception
items.description: Robotic perception increasingly relies on heterogeneous sensor suites combining cameras with emerging modalities (event, SPAD, iToF/dToF, and thermal).
items.ai_summary: VisionSIM is a multi-modal robotic perception simulator that models physical measurement processes and failure modes for conventional and emerging sensors.

items.title: SHORE: Stability-Hybrid On-Policy Reinforcement Learning for Online Bin Packing
items.description: Online 3D bin packing with a processing buffer requires choosing which box to pack, its orientation, and its placement while keeping the stack stable under unknown future arrivals. A collapse ends the episode and forfeits the remaining volume.
items.ai_summary: Stability-Hybrid On-Policy Reinforcement Learning (SHORE) combines a learned stability probability with an actor-critic model to achieve faster learning and higher space utilization in online 3D bin packing.

items.title: StrataFlux: Memory-Hierarchy-Native Low-Bit LLM Inference
items.description: Quantization reduces the memory and bandwidth demands of large language model (LLM) inference but can degrade accuracy; offloading higher-precision data can instead stall generation.
items.ai_summary: StrataFlux is a memory-hierarchy-native inference framework that improves accuracy for low-bit quantized large language models by streaming precision from host RAM and solid-state drives.

items.title: SpecCTMC: Exact Speculative Simulation of Diffusion Language Model Continuous-Time Markov Chains
items.description: Masked diffusion language models offer parallel text generation, but independently sampling multiple tokens can disrupt their dependencies and change the output distribution.
items.ai_summary: SpecCTMC is a training-free speculative sampler for masked diffusion language models that uses parallel evaluation and an exact correction procedure to reduce sequential model evaluations without changing the output distribution.

items.title: OraRefer: Segmentation-Guided Multi-Photograph Fusion for Oral Cancer Screening with Guaranteed Patient-Level Sensitivity
items.description: Oral cancer and the oral potentially malignant disorders (OPMD) that can precede it are visible on the oral mucosa, which makes smartphone photographs a promising tool for screening. Deep learning models for this task classify individual photographs.
items.ai_summary: OraRefer is a patient-level screening framework that uses segmentation-guided fusion and guaranteed sensitivity thresholds to detect oral cancer and precancerous disorders from multiple smartphone photographs.

items.title: A Theoretical Analysis of a Bilevel Optimization Formulation for Combined Local-Global Optical Flow Models
items.description: This paper analyzes a bilevel formulation for learning the regularization parameter of combined local-global (CLG) optical flow models.
items.ai_summary: Theoretical analysis of a bilevel optimization formulation for combined local-global optical flow models establishes conditions for the existence and properties of optimal regularization parameters.

items.title: Unifying Central Flow, Rod Flow, and the Edge Coupling
items.description: At the edge of stability, the iterates of gradient descent oscillate along the sharp directions of the Hessian. This poses a significant challenge for continuous-time models as the usual continuous-time approximation -- the gradient flow -- admits no oscillations.
items.ai_summary: Edge coupling framework unifies central flow and rod flow models for gradient descent and momentum methods, tracking discrete iterates across all phases of neural network training.

items.title: USB Gym: A Gymnasium Testbed for Closed-Loop Ultrasound View Matching
items.description: Background and Objective: Our main goal is ultrasound guidance: moving a probe until its image matches a target view. Published methods for each part of a guide are evaluated in separate simulators. We asked whether these methods, combined into one guide, are good enough.
items.ai_summary: USB Gym is a simulation testbed for evaluating and combining modular methods for closed-loop ultrasound probe guidance toward target anatomical views.

items.title: 4D Point Splatting for mmWave Radar Micro-Doppler Differentiable Rendering
items.description: Millimeter-wave radar resolves the micrometer displacements of a moving body as micro-Doppler, enabling gait, gesture, activity, pose and vital-sign sensing.
items.ai_summary: 4D Point Splatting is a physics-based differentiable renderer that reconstructs moving 3D scenes from real millimeter-wave radar captures to improve downstream sensing models.

items.title: Enhancing Local and Global Structure in Compressed AI Agent Memory
items.description: AI agents store text as embedding vectors and compress them at scale. A compression is accepted when each item's nearest neighbors survive, but agents also consolidate, delete, and compare memories, tasks that depend on which items lie far apart.
items.ai_summary: Locality-aware quantization improves the global structure and fidelity of compressed vector embeddings in AI agent memory systems without losing retrieval performance.

items.title: Discovering Learning Rules that Shape Others
items.description: In general-sum games, self-interested learners can reach outcomes that are poor for everyone, which has motivated methods that shape the opponent's learning.
items.ai_summary: Discovered Update Rule for Opponent Shaping meta-learns update rules that enable reinforcement learning agents to successfully influence opponents in general-sum games without accessing their internal parameters.

items.title: Cultural Adaptation within Repeated Social Interactions
items.description: Much of human culture is tacit and is typically learned through situated social interaction.
items.ai_summary: Sandbox evaluation framework demonstrates that memory mechanisms enable large language models to continuously adapt their cultural norms and language use through repeated social interactions.

items.title: InstantHand: Feed-Forward 3D Gaussian Splatting for Animatable Hand Avatar Reconstruction from a Single Image
items.description: Hand avatar reconstruction typically relies on multi-view capture or per-subject optimization, limiting its scalability.
items.ai_summary: InstantHand is a feed-forward framework that rapidly constructs animatable 3D Gaussian hand avatars from a single image using specialized regularization and appearance transfer techniques.

items.title: Decision Models as Retrieval Gates Against Injection and Pollution
items.description: Retrieved web text can carry instructions aimed at the language model, or synthetic pages written to mislead.
items.ai_summary: Open-weight decision models serve as efficient retrieval gates to screen out prompt injections and polluted text from retrieved web pages before they reach language models.

items.title: Polarity Classification with Multitask Learning Syntax Augmentation
items.description: Sentiment Analysis (SA) is a fundamental NLP task concerned with the identification and categorization of subjective information in text. While lexicon-based methods offer transparency, they often struggle with linguistic phenomena such as negation and intensification.
items.ai_summary: Multitask learning strategies integrate syntactic knowledge into neural sentiment analysis models to improve polarity classification performance across multiple languages and datasets.

items.title: Learning the Task or Learning the Verifier? Rethinking Criteria Exposure in Embodied Self-Improvement
items.description: Exposing benchmark success criteria to self-improving embodied coding agents can raise measured success under those criteria without improving instructed-task completion, and the advantage weakens under slight criteria changes and transfers poorly across tasks, while…
items.ai_summary: Controlled experiments reveal that criteria exposure causes self-improving embodied agents to overfit to benchmark verifiers rather than learning transferable task skills.

items.title: Benchmarking Large Language Models on Heterogeneous Cognitive and Biomedical Knowledge Graphs: The Role of Graph Grounding in Multi-Hop Reasoning and Hallucination Mitigation
items.description: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used in biomedical and cognitive neuroscience, but their ability to reason reliably over heterogeneous knowledge graphs (KGs) remains unclear.
items.ai_summary: A benchmark evaluation across five heterogeneous knowledge graphs demonstrates that graph grounding significantly reduces hallucination rates in large language models.

items.title: Interpretable many-body interaction laws for collective motion from few trajectories
items.description: Models of collective motion usually reduce social interactions to pairwise forces, despite empirical evidence for many-body effects.
items.ai_summary: The directional atomic cluster expansion framework recovers interpretable many-body interaction laws for collective motion from limited trajectory data.

items.title: LLM-Assisted Label Noise Correction for EEG-Based Sleep Stage Classification
items.description: Automatic sleep stage classification from electroencephalography (EEG) signals is a critical task in clinical sleep medicine.
items.ai_summary: An LLM-assisted label-noise filtering pipeline identifies and removes unreliable sleep-stage annotations during training to improve automated classification accuracy.

items.title: RM-VLM: From Natural-Language Task Descriptions to Vision-Grounded Reward Machines
items.description: Reward machines (RMs) have been proposed as a reward formulation in reinforcement learning (RL) to capture non-Markovian tasks where credit assignment depends on history.
items.ai_summary: RM-VLM generates reward machines from natural-language descriptions using a large language model and grounds them with a vision-language model for reinforcement learning.

items.title: Measured Coupling for Parallel Decoding in Diffusion Language Models
items.description: Diffusion language models can write many tokens per step, but must choose which tokens are safe to commit together. Mean-field decoding penalizes pairs of positions whose predictions look alike.
items.ai_summary: A parallel decoding method for diffusion language models measures coupling probes inside the main forward pass to commit tokens faster with high accuracy.

items.title: GINGER: Spicing Up Graph-Based Vector Search
items.description: We present \textsc{Ginger}, a state-of-the-art open-source C++ library for graph-based approximate nearest neighbor search (ANNS). We developed \textsc{Ginger} at Google to push the speed and memory efficiency of graph search on large and high-dimensional embedding datasets.
items.ai_summary: Ginger is an open-source C++ library for graph-based approximate nearest neighbor search that improves query throughput and memory efficiency on large embedding datasets.

items.title: First-Token Attraction in Mamba Dynamics
items.description: We study token dynamics in deep Mamba models, with a particular focus on the attracting role of the first token.
items.ai_summary: An analytical framework based on invariant boxes proves that the first token in deep Mamba models exerts a strong attracting influence, driving token clustering.

items.title: Dynamic Optimistic Constrained OCO with Memory via Delay Equivalence
items.description: Online Convex Optimization with memory and time-varying constraints (COCO-M) is a recently-introduced framework that captures the dynamics of stateful online learning and non-stochastic control with budget constraints.
items.ai_summary: An optimistic algorithm for online convex optimization with memory and time-varying constraints incorporates untrusted predictions to bound regret and constraint violations.

items.title: Australian universities are creating AI-native graduates
items.description: Australian universities are expanding access to ChatGPT and bringing AI into teaching and learning to prepare students for an AI-enabled workforce.
items.ai_summary: Australian universities are integrating ChatGPT and AI tools into their teaching and learning programs to prepare students for an AI-enabled workforce.

items.title: Transformer-Based Trajectory Prescription for sEMG-Optimizing Robot-Mediated Rehabilitation
items.description: Robot-mediated rehabilitation has the potential to deliver high-intensity, individualized therapy, but existing systems (which have not consistently improved outcomes) typically prescribe kinematic trajectories rather than explicitly targeting the neuromotor activations thought…
items.ai_summary: Personalizable transformer-based model that maps muscle activations to prescribed contact force trajectories, enabling neuromotor-optimized robot-mediated rehabilitation.

items.title: ManimCode: Learning Visual Self-Correction for Educational Animation
items.description: Manim supports precise, programmatic video generation, but a successfully rendered educational animation can still have visual defects, missing explanations, or incorrect content.
items.ai_summary: ManimCode is a data and training framework that uses feedback-driven reinforcement learning to train models to write, review, and revise educational animation programs.

items.title: AutoCompress: Automated Hardware-Guided Model Compression
items.description: AutoCompress is a hardware-guided compression framework that uses differentiable architecture search to optimize global and per-layer structures under serving constraints, improving accuracy over Minitron and compressing a large model while retaining most benchmark performance.
items.ai_summary: AutoCompress is a hardware-guided compression framework that uses differentiable architecture search to prune large language models while meeting specific hardware and latency constraints.

items.title: Hierarchical Incremental Beta Splatting for Online Reconstruction
items.description: Online 3D Gaussian Splatting reconstructs a scene during capture: each keyframe spawns primitives once and refines them for only a few dozen iterations, leaving little chance to fix poor initialization or missing detail.
items.ai_summary: Hierarchical Incremental Beta Splatting is an online 3D reconstruction method using beta kernels to improve geometry confidence, rendering speed, and optimization efficiency.

items.title: Interactive Visual Gym: Evaluating Visual Interaction Models with Simulated Users in Interactive Worlds
items.description: Interactive Visual Gym enables closed-loop evaluation and training of visual interaction models by jointly simulating task environments and human users, exposing limitations in state-of-the-art VLMs and improving performance through closed-loop training.
items.ai_summary: Interactive Visual Gym is a closed-loop evaluation framework that simulates task environments and human users to benchmark visual interaction models.

items.title: A Generative Model of Contextual Integrity: Appropriate vs. Inappropriate Information Sharing
items.description: Contextual integrity (CI) holds that appropriate information flow depends on context-specific norms. The same disclosure may be appropriate in one context and inappropriate in another.
items.ai_summary: Generative model of contextual integrity that uses interacting large language models to study appropriate and inappropriate information sharing across different conversational scenarios.

items.title: Multimodal-SEA: Benchmarking AI Agent Security under Multimodal Social Engineering Attacks
items.description: Personal AI agents face social engineering attacks supported by forged multimodal content, but existing evaluations mainly focus on text-based dialogue, leaving their intrinsic security under such attacks insufficiently studied.
items.ai_summary: Multimodal-SEA is an interactive benchmark comprising 608 expert-designed tasks to evaluate the intrinsic security of personal AI agents against multimodal social engineering attacks.

items.title: LeanContext: Disentangling Mathematical Resources from Local Formal Context in Lean Whole-Proof Generation
items.description: Neural theorem proving increasingly uses retrieved premises and project context to support proof generation. Evaluating these resources requires measuring the advantage of target-selected declarations over comparable alternatives and how this advantage depends on training.
items.ai_summary: LeanContext is a benchmark of 129,826 Lean whole-proof generation problems designed to evaluate retrieved mathematical resources and project context in neural theorem proving.

items.title: Aligning Policy Encoders with a Shape Teacher
items.description: 3D-aware representations can improve robotic manipulation by providing geometric information that is robust to changes in viewpoint, object position, and occlusion.
items.ai_summary: Shape-teacher alignment is a training-time mechanism that uses a pretrained 3D shape representation to transfer geometric structure to image-based robot policy encoders.

items.title: Accelerating Safe Reinforcement Learning with Massive Parallelism
items.description: We investigate the problem of scaling safe reinforcement learning (safe RL) to massively parallel training regimes, where a large number of environments are exe- cuted with short rollout horizons.
items.ai_summary: Scalable safe reinforcement learning method using a phase-aggregated cost estimator and constraint tightening to support massively parallel training regimes with short rollouts.

items.title: DART: Domain-Agnostic Residual Transfer for Generalist Anomaly Detection
items.description: Generalist Anomaly Detection (GAD) aims to detect anomalies in unseen domains using only a few reference samples.
items.ai_summary: DART is a plug-in framework for generalist anomaly detection that separates residuals into anomaly-relevant and domain-specific components to improve cross-domain transfer performance.

items.title: Accepted but Wrong: Silent Failures of LLM Code Repairs after API Migrations
items.description: After a runtime or API migration, an LLM-repaired procedure can run cleanly yet return wrong results, and a release check on typical test inputs ships it. We report a preregistered study of 73 tasks covering 60 documented changes in CPython, Node.js and SQLite.
items.ai_summary: Study on LLM code repairs reveals that standard release checks and tests frequently accept incorrectly repaired programs after API migrations.

items.title: SplatAnything: Gaussian Spacing Normalization for Feed-forward 3DGS across Arbitrary Scenes
items.description: SplatAnything applies Gaussian Spacing Normalization to canonicalize scene-level Gaussian spacing, yielding more consistent supervision and improved feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting under varying scene scales and viewpoints.
items.ai_summary: SplatAnything introduces Gaussian Spacing Normalization to canonicalize a scene-level spacing statistic, improving feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting across varying scales and viewpoints.

items.title: Scaling Neural Motor Decoding via Decoupled Behavioral Pretraining
items.description: Recent neural decoding approaches achieve strong performance by training on large collections of paired neural-behavioral recordings, but such datasets are expensive, invasive, and difficult to scale.
items.ai_summary: BEEMO is a multi-session neural motor decoding framework that decouples behavioral and neural representation learning to scale training with unpaired behavioral data.

items.title: The Geometry of Simulated Perspectives: Dissociating Representation and Behaviour in a Multimodal Language Model
items.description: Multimodal language models can simulate different observers, yet it remains unclear how assigned perspectives reshape their internal representations and whether these changes govern their judgements.
items.ai_summary: Investigation into the internal representations of Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct shows that prompt framing reshapes representational geometry more strongly than assigned persona identity.

items.title: Nowcasting of Tropical Cyclone Wind Fields and Intensity from Geostationary Imagery
items.description: High-resolution tropical cyclone surface wind speeds derived from synthetic aperture radar (SAR) observations can support storm structure and intensity modelling, but remain spatially and temporally sparse and unavailable near-real-time.
items.ai_summary: Neural networks predict 2D surface wind fields and storm intensity from geostationary satellite imagery to improve tropical cyclone nowcasting.

items.title: Series-wise Cross-validation for Global Time Series Forecasting
items.description: We consider the problem of cross-validation (CV) in time series forecasting, with a focus on global forecasting models based on deep learning. The prevailing CV strategy in forecasting is to partition data across time with the last part of each series used for testing.
items.ai_summary: Series-wise cross-validation partitioning for global time series forecasting improves downstream accuracy by guiding model selection toward better generalization across series and time.

items.title: Geometric Relevance Is Not Sufficient: Evaluating Focused Post-Training Supervision in Diffusion Docking
items.description: Diffusion-based molecular docking requires learning a corrective score field across a broad corruption distribution, yet individual pose errors can differ substantially in their structural consequences.
items.ai_summary: Study on diffusion-based molecular docking evaluates focused versus broad post-training supervision strategies, finding that broad continuation achieves higher mean Top-1 success.

items.title: Value-oriented policy distillation for interpretable wind farm power control
items.description: Wind farm power control can help the system maintain balance and avoid blackouts.
items.ai_summary: Value-oriented policy distillation framework using explainable boosting machines creates interpretable wind farm power control policies that significantly reduce grid imbalance costs.

items.title: FewStepRL: Fine-tuning Few-step Diffusion Models with Reinforcement Learning
items.description: Reinforcement learning objectives for diffusion models are reformulated for few-step samplers through x-space transformation, gradient decomposition, and anchor adaptation, yielding modular few-step variants of several methods and showing reward-gradient methods excel with…
items.ai_summary: FewStepRL adapts reinforcement learning objectives for few-step diffusion models by transforming, decomposing, and adapting gradients to efficiently fine-tune generative models.

items.title: Terminal-style Mathematical Modeling Bench: The First Agentic and Verifiable Benchmark for Mathematical Modeling
items.description: TB-MathModel is a terminal benchmark that makes complete contest-style mathematical modeling problems agentic and verifiable, scoring final numeric answers against multiple human references with feasibility checks.
items.ai_summary: TB-MathModel is a terminal-style benchmark that evaluates mathematical modeling agents using verifiable contest-style problems and multi-reference scoring.

items.title: Beyond Quadratic Attention: Separable Gaussian Operators for ODE Vision Transformers
items.description: Self-attention carries a quadratic cost in token count, which limits how far Vision Transformers can scale with input resolution.
items.ai_summary: SSoG is a separable sum-of-Gaussians spatial operator that replaces dense self-attention in Vision Transformers to reduce computational costs and improve accuracy.

items.title: Signals, Evidence, and Context: User Scrutiny in Real-World LLM Conversations
items.description: Large language models (LLMs) often present synthesized answers without making their supporting evidence easy to inspect.
items.ai_summary: Study of user scrutiny in nearly 500,000 LLM conversations reveals how attribution language and uncertainty features influence whether users check or challenge assistant responses.

items.title: From Twisted Facts to Rogue Agents: Can LLMs Reliably Detect Multi-Dimensional Hallucinations?
items.description: Large language models (LLMs) are widely used for information access, content production, and agent-based task execution, but their outputs remain vulnerable to subtle, high-risk hallucinations.
items.ai_summary: HaluCheck is a large-scale bilingual benchmark comprising over 42,000 instances designed to evaluate and diagnose multi-dimensional hallucinations in text and agent trajectories.

items.title: Domain-specific information retrieval
items.description: Information Retrieval (IR) is much more than ad hoc web search: a large portion of the information seeking activities takes place in specific domains, often addressing work-related tasks.
items.ai_summary: Review of domain-specific information retrieval explores common tasks, unique challenges like long documents, and transferable methodological advances.

items.title: "Blind Compliance": Coercive Control in AI Jailbreaking
items.description: The explosion of generative AI systems and concerns surrounding their rapidly scaling capabilities has led to an adversarial cycle between increasingly narrow content restrictions ("guardrails") and increasingly sophisticated structured prompting techniques ("jailbreaks").
items.ai_summary: Study introduces a coercive control framework to analyze the relational dynamics of power and control embedded in AI training paradigms and jailbreaking techniques.

items.title: Agent-R$^2$: Scaling Agents for Realistic Productivity Work via Real-Source Data Synthesis
items.description: A real-source data synthesis framework trains a 4B agent on 4k task instances with supervised fine-tuning and rubric-based reinforcement learning, improving realistic productivity work and file-grounded reasoning over larger models.
items.ai_summary: Agent-R2 is a real-source data synthesis framework that creates realistic productivity tasks and rubrics to train high-performing language model agents.

items.title: ProQuant: Progressive Quantization-aware Training for Edge MLLMs
items.description: Multi-modal large language models (MLLMs) with impressive perception and understanding capabilities will enable a range of downstream applications.
items.ai_summary: ProQuant is a weight-activation quantization-aware training framework designed to maintain the performance of multi-modal large language models under low-bit quantization on edge devices.

items.title: Do sEMG Foundation Models Improve Cross-Subject Generalisation?
items.description: sEMG Foundation Models aim to learn general purpose representations over diverse subjects and recording conditions that boost performance on a variety of downstream tasks.
items.ai_summary: Systematic evaluation of sEMG foundation models finds that pretraining boosts performance within the same session but offers little benefit under inter-subject evaluation.

items.title: SMART: State-based Multi Agent Reasoning Traces for Verification-oriented Problem-Solving
items.description: Complex problems with limited context, such as claims, require a means to obtain additional knowledge necessary for solution reasoning.
items.ai_summary: SMART is a multi-agent framework that captures implicit entity states to curate verified premises, improving solution reasoning and validation performance on complex claims.

items.title: Multimodal Hierarchical Mixture-of-Experts for 3D Medical Vision-Language Modeling
items.description: Medical 3D scans and reports are inherently hierarchical, with diagnostic cues concentrated in specific anatomical regions across multiple levels of organization. Yet, most medical vision-language models ignore this structure and fail to focus on clinically relevant anatomy.
items.ai_summary: MedHiVE proposes a hierarchical mixture-of-experts and contrastive learning framework for 3D medical vision-language modeling, improving performance across segmentation, classification, and detection tasks.

items.title: BUMP: Brief Unexpected Mid-Interpolation Peak
items.description: We identify an intriguing phenomenon when linearly interpolating between permutation-aligned neural networks: test accuracy briefly improves near the interpolation endpoints before dropping toward the midpoint, which we term BUMP (Brief Unexpected Mid-interpolation Peak).
items.ai_summary: Weight-prediction mixed ensembling combines weight mixing and prediction-space mixing to consistently outperform standard logit ensembling in test accuracy and calibration trade-offs.

items.title: Knowing When to Teach: Learning from Teachable Prefixes in Multilingual Reasoning Distillation
items.description: TOPSD improves multilingual reasoning by using likelihood-based drift detection and verification to decide when teacher supervision should be applied during on-policy self-distillation.
items.ai_summary: Teachable On-Policy Self-Distillation uses likelihood estimation and verification to prevent teacher drift during multilingual reasoning distillation, improving mathematical reasoning across multiple languages.

items.title: BabyTheorist: A Benchmark for Learning to Theorize the World from Observation Alone
items.description: How would we know whether a machine truly understands the world? We argue that one key capability is \textit{observational theory learning}: acquiring reusable theories from pure observations and applying them to new situations.
items.ai_summary: BabyTheorist is a benchmark that generates continual streams of visual observations from hidden compositional programs to evaluate machine observational theory learning.

items.title: PCBRouteAgent: How Close Are LLM Agents to Becoming PCB Routing Engineers?
items.description: Automating printed circuit board (PCB) routing requires coordinating board-level connectivity decisions with geometric execution under strict design rules. Although recent agents can interact with native routing tools, reliable routing on complex boards remains challenging.
items.ai_summary: PCBRouteAgent is a multimodal agent that coordinates global routing plans with detailed execution to automate printed circuit board routing.

items.title: Regret Bounds for Profit Maximization in Bilateral Trade: Learning the Best Posted-Price Mechanism
items.description: Bilateral trade models the task of intermediating between two strategic agents, a seller and a buyer, willing to trade a good for which they hold private valuations. We study this problem from the perspective of a profit-maximizing broker in a regret minimization framework.
items.ai_summary: Adversarial and stochastic learning algorithms achieve near-optimal regret bounds for profit-maximizing brokers in bilateral trade by combining localized estimation with minimax and distribution properties.

items.title: RouteAlign: Aligning Task Requirements with Model Profiles for LLM Service Selection
items.description: LLM service selection requires performance evidence that reflects the demands of the current task. Aggregate scores obscure differences in capability and difficulty, while semantically related examples can involve different combinations of skills.
items.ai_summary: RouteAlign uses task requirements and performance profiles to structure LLM service selection, extending the empirical quality-cost frontier toward higher task quality.

items.title: Patch Attention Wisely: Understanding Patch Length in Attention-Based Forecasting
items.description: Attention-based time series forecasters commonly group consecutive observations into patches. Patch length is known to have a substantial impact on forecasting performance, yet its selection remains largely empirical.
items.ai_summary: A theoretical framework for attention-based time series forecasting uses exact coefficient matrix factorization to derive a patch-selection criterion balancing representation and estimation errors.

items.title: Improving Context-Shift Robustness of Convolutional Networks via Context-Regularized Cross-Entropy
items.description: Image classification models often encounter objects in diverse and unpredictable contexts at test time, which may differ substantially from those seen during training.
items.ai_summary: Context-Regularized Cross-Entropy uses spatial feature attribution to suppress contextual regions and improve convolutional network robustness under context shift.

items.title: La-JEPA: Compact Robot Policies with Latent World Modeling
items.description: World-action models adapt pretrained video generators, and vision-language-action models build on pretrained vision-language backbones; both tie policy architecture and inference cost to large transformers designed for generation rather than control.
items.ai_summary: La-JEPA is a compact world-action model trained in the feature space of a pretrained encoder, achieving high robot control performance while using fewer parameters than generation-oriented models.

items.title: AI-Native Task-Oriented Semantic Communications over a Relay: Benefits and Vulnerabilities
items.description: Semantic communication (SemCom) using a relay node is considered, where the relay assists in conveying task-relevant information from a source to a destination, with meaning defined by classification labels.
items.ai_summary: A joint end-to-end design for relay-assisted semantic communications optimizes inference accuracy and perceptual quality while revealing vulnerabilities to learned Byzantine attacks.

items.title: Interpretable Multimodal MRI-Clinical Fusion for Functional Outcome Prediction After Acute Ischemic Stroke
items.description: This study evaluates the added prognostic value of day-1 multimodal MRI for predicting three-month functional outcome after acute ischemic stroke (AIS). Sixty-six AIS patients with ADC, DWI, FLAIR, and clinical data were analyzed.
items.ai_summary: Multimodal MRI and clinical data fusion models predict three-month functional outcomes after acute ischemic stroke, with FLAIR-clinical fusion achieving the highest prognostic performance.

items.title: A Generative Foundation Model for Multimodal Tokamak Tasks
items.description: Tokamak experiments record diverse measurements, including waveforms, profiles, fields, and scalars, which are used to reconstruct the plasma, forecast its evolution, recover associated control signals, and estimate disruption risk.
items.ai_summary: GenToka is a generative tokamak foundation model that jointly generates schema-selected target signals using a shared conditional diffusion Transformer to improve plasma task prediction.

items.title: Detecting Weather Fronts from Satellite Observations: What Does Reanalysis Add?
items.description: Weather fronts are transition regions between air masses with contrasting thermodynamic properties and are associated with mid-latitude precipitation and severe weather.
items.ai_summary: A machine learning model for pixel-wise weather front detection demonstrates that incorporating ERA5 reanalysis fields significantly improves performance compared to using satellite observations alone.

items.title: MCUFlowNet: Hardware-Aware Neural Architecture Search for Optical Flow on Microcontrollers
items.description: Dense optical flow allows small drones to avoid obstacles. However, few dense optical flow networks are designed for microcontrollers (MCUs) with neural accelerators, whose on-chip SRAM limits the input resolution.
items.ai_summary: MCUFlowNet is a family of hardware-aware optical flow networks designed via a neural architecture search framework to run efficiently on microcontrollers.

items.title: Detecting Silent Faults at the Environment-Trainer Boundary in Reinforcement Learning
items.description: Robot reinforcement learning increasingly runs environments outside the trainer: in another process, on another machine, in another language. Many faults at this boundary raise no error. We make the boundary a wire protocol and ask what notices a fault in it.
items.ai_summary: A step ledger kept and compared at the environment-trainer boundary catches silent faults in reinforcement learning runs that standard learning-curve and reward checks miss.

items.title: Fault-Guided Cross-Layer Prediction for Unsupervised Anomaly Detection
items.description: Feature reconstruction is widely used for unsupervised industrial anomaly detection in the single-class setting, where only normal images from one product category are available for training.
items.ai_summary: A single-class anomaly detector leverages block-to-block hidden-state transitions in frozen vision transformers to expose transportable information limits and identify industrial defects.

items.title: Describe Your Facial Expressions by Linking Image Encoders and Large Language Models
items.description: This paper presents a novel task of describing human facial expressions of a facial image in natural language, which captures the nuances of facial actions and emotional states beyond traditional emotion categories or facial action units (AUs).
items.ai_summary: A three-stage training framework links image encoders and large language models using synthetic image-text pairs to generate detailed natural language descriptions of human facial expressions.

items.title: How Far Can Untrained Neural Networks Go in Anomaly Detection? From Tables to Pixels
items.description: Anomaly detection (AD) is often framed as a representation-learning problem, where strong performance is expected to require learned features or AD-specific optimization.
items.ai_summary: PRISM is an anomaly detection framework combining fixed random nonlinear features with Mahalanobis scoring to achieve strong tabular and visual detection without neural weight optimization.

items.title: Who Can Evaluate AI Independently? A Framework for Analysing Evaluation Infrastructure
items.description: AI evaluation is increasingly central to AI safety and governance, yet taking part in an evaluation does not by itself confer authority over its design, its execution or the resources it depends on.
items.ai_summary: The PAAI framework analyzes how infrastructure arrangements and resource control distribute authority over AI evaluations across diverse institutional settings.

items.title: Beyond K/V Caches: Cross-Model State Handoff in Hybrid Linear-Attention LLMs
items.description: Production deployments often use different models to balance cost and quality through cascading, routing, and switching models during long conversations. Context accumulates across turns. Each switch requires the target to repeat prefill over this context.
items.ai_summary: Hybrid State Transfer is a proposed method for hybrid linear-attention large language models that enables fast and accurate cross-model state handoffs during conversational cascading and routing.

items.title: FreeOcc: Decoupling Ego-Motion for Efficient 4D Occupancy Forecasting via Continuous Flow Matching
items.description: Current 4D occupancy world models use heavy cross-attention or deep recurrence to disentangle ego-motion from scene dynamics. This requires significant computational capacity.
items.ai_summary: FreeOcc is a lightweight continuous-time world model for 4D occupancy forecasting that uses explicit geometric decoupling and continuous flow matching to achieve efficient state-of-the-art performance.

items.title: ProtoGestalt: Interpretable Prototypes for Facial Phenotyping and Diagnosis of Rare Genetic Disorders
items.description: Rare genetic disorders are difficult to diagnose due to their diversity and overlapping clinical features.
items.ai_summary: ProtoGestalt is an interpretable prototype-based framework for facial phenotyping and rare genetic disorder diagnosis that links predictions to anatomically meaningful facial regions.

items.title: Create Your Own Work Stack: Deploying Self-hosted AI and Tooling in a Tech Startup
items.description: Self-hosting AI is often presented as a way to reduce inference costs and increase control, but deployment introduces its own costs. We report our experience deploying a hybrid AI stack at Grayhat Developers, a small software company with an AI-intensive development workflow.
items.ai_summary: Case study on deploying a hybrid AI stack shows that offloading low-complexity coordination and information retrieval tasks to local open-source models reduces commercial AI workload costs.

items.title: Identifying Neural Dynamics Using Nonlinear Interventional State Space Models
items.description: State-space models (SSMs) recover low-dimensional latent dynamics from high-dimensional observations, but latents are generally not identifiable from observational data alone.
items.ai_summary: This paper proves that interventional state-space models achieve affine and nonlinear latent identifiability under general injective emissions and interventions, improving neural dynamics identification.

items.title: Reinforcing End-to-End Autonomous Driving Safety via Negative-Aware Planning in a Unified World-Action Model
items.description: World-action models (WAMs) jointly model future traffic states and driving actions for end-to-end autonomous driving in intelligent transportation systems.
items.ai_summary: NegWAM is a safety post-training framework for unified world-action models that uses near-expert negative trajectories to improve robustness and safety in autonomous driving planning.

items.title: Towards Practical 20 kbps Generative Video Compression via Adaptive Tokenization and Entropy Modeling
items.description: Video compression at ultra-low bitrates remains challenging due to the loss of perceptually important details under limited bit budgets.
items.ai_summary: This method adapts pretrained video representations into compression-oriented representations using a discrete video tokenizer and entropy model to achieve high-performance generative video compression at ultra-low bitrates.

items.title: National-scale mapping of tree species composition in Switzerland from high-resolution aerial imagery and multimodal data
items.description: Tree-species composition shapes forest productivity and how forests respond to climate disturbances such as drought, windthrow and insect outbreaks. Yet most national forest maps assign each pixel a single dominant species and cannot show the share of accompanying species.
items.ai_summary: A deep-learning model combining high-resolution aerial imagery, airborne laser scanning, and multimodal data produces a national-scale map of tree species composition and basal-area shares across Switzerland at 30-meter resolution.

items.title: PersonaAgent: Retrieval-Augmented Transaction Anomaly Scoring with Refreshable Multi-Entity Persona Memory
items.description: In large-scale payment networks, entities (card, merchant, etc.) and their interactions play a key role in transaction anomaly detection. However, transaction patterns between different entities usually change more frequently than the production model refresh schedule.
items.ai_summary: PersonaAgent is an agentic transaction anomaly detection framework that uses a refreshable multi-entity persona memory to capture recent behavior signals and improve payment network fraud scoring.

items.title: Gradient Boosting for Efficient Rank Discovery in Tensor Network Kernel Machines
items.description: Tensor network kernel machines (TNKMs) combine nonlinear features with low-rank tensor representations to model complex relationships efficiently.
items.ai_summary: GB-CPKM is a gradient boosting framework for tensor network kernel machines that sequentially adds fixed-rank learners to efficiently increase model capacity without explicit rank searches.

items.title: Gabor Gabor: E-Gaborformer, a Strictly Causal Speech Recognizer with Gabor-Dictionary Convolutions and Delta-Rule Memory
items.description: Real-time voice agents need a speech recognizer that never waits for future audio and whose memory per call does not grow with the length of the call.
items.ai_summary: E-Gaborformer is a strictly causal speech recognition encoder that uses Gabor-dictionary convolutions and constant-state memory to achieve high accuracy and low word error rates in real-time voice agents.

items.title: ATHAAR: A Medieval Scientific Arabic Manuscript Dataset for Handwritten Text Recognition
items.description: Despite recent progress in handwritten text recognition, medieval Arabic scientific manuscripts remain an open challenge for current vision-language models (VLMs) due to cursive ligatures, variable diacritization, and more importantly the lack of training data.
items.ai_summary: ATHAAR is a manually annotated dataset of medieval Arabic scientific manuscripts designed to evaluate and improve handwritten text recognition and vision-language models across diverse scripts and numerals.

items.title: SAE Interprets MoE: Sparse AutoEncoders Reveal That MoE Experts Exhibit Human-Interpretable Fine-Grained Specialization
items.description: Sparse autoencoders trained on Mixture-of-Experts layer outputs reveal concentrated, interpretable expert contributions that subdivide coarse domains into finer responsibilities.
items.ai_summary: Sparse autoencoders applied to Mixture-of-Experts model outputs reveal that individual experts exhibit human-interpretable, fine-grained functional specialization well below coarse domain boundaries.

items.title: Value or Attention: Investigating Layer-wise Relevance Propagation for Graph Attention Networks
items.description: Graph Attention Networks (GATs) are increasingly used in domains where scientists need to read a model's reasoning, from medicine to materials science, yet the routing they learn remains opaque to most explainers.
items.ai_summary: Layer-wise Relevance Propagation for Graph Attention Networks introduces a product rule that separates value content relevance from attention routing relevance to improve model explainability.

items.title: MUSS: A Multi-scale and Sequence-based Model for Single-cell Gene Regulation
items.description: Modeling gene regulation in single cells requires jointly representing DNA sequence, chromatin accessibility, and gene expression across regulatory scales.
items.ai_summary: MUSS is a sequence-based multi-scale model that integrates DNA sequence, chromatin accessibility, and gene expression to decode cell-type-specific gene regulation and predict unseen expression.

items.title: Linguistic boundaries emerge from pressure-constrained processing dynamics
items.description: Human cognition organizes continuous experience into bounded units while maintaining continuity across them.
items.ai_summary: Computational simulations and human experiments demonstrate that linguistic boundaries emerge from interacting cognitive demands involving unresolved dependencies, integration costs, and semantic updates.

items.title: DictLLM: Post-training Compression of Large Language Model with Dictionary Kernels
items.description: Efficient deployment of large language models (LLMs) on mobile devices requires balancing performance with compute and memory constraints.
items.ai_summary: DictLLM is a post-training compression scheme that decomposes weight matrices into a shared dictionary and sparse coefficients to reduce memory usage and deploy large language models efficiently.

items.title: TerraMesh-Masks: Open-Vocabulary Segmentation for Earth Observation
items.description: Open-vocabulary segmentation (OVS) enables models to segment a variety of concepts specified in natural language, removing the need for fixed label sets and fine-tuning.
items.ai_summary: TerraMesh-Masks is a large-scale open-vocabulary segmentation dataset comprising sixteen million binary masks aligned with multimodal Earth observation samples to improve spatial modeling.

items.title: Spatiotemporal Dynamics-Aware Industrial Anomaly Detection and Reasoning
items.description: Industrial Anomaly Detection (IAD) is a long-established problem that aims to detect defects in industrial products during manufacturing for quality control. Most existing studies focus on static visual patterns as the basis for detection.
items.ai_summary: MUSTARD is a multimodal framework that integrates spatiotemporal dynamics and optical-flow-guided keyframe selection to detect and reason about motion-based defects in industrial manufacturing.

items.title: Optimal Competitive Ratios for Chasing Convex Functions with Quadratic Growth
items.description: Chasing convex function has attracted much attention in recent years, which can be formulated as a game between a learner and an adversary.
items.ai_summary: Clipped Proximal Descent and tight competitive analyses establish optimal dimension-free competitive ratios for chasing convex functions with quadratic growth under Euclidean and squared Euclidean movement costs.

items.title: Doubly-robust causal inference for multi-valued treatment regimes with recurrent neural networks
items.description: We propose a doubly-robust method to estimate the causal effects of multi-valued treatment regimes on patient outcomes. A multi-valued treatment regime assigns personalized treatments from a set of competing options based on a patient's history.
items.ai_summary: Researchers propose a doubly-robust causal inference method that uses recurrent neural networks and longitudinal targeted minimum loss-based estimation to evaluate multi-valued treatment regimes on patient outcomes.

items.title: Can an LLM Actually Reason and Program about Neural Network's Weights or is it just memorization on steroids? Exploring "Weight-Space Programming"
items.description: Large language models (LLMs) have recently been reported to read and write the raw weights of neural networks directly, a capability termed weight-space programming.
items.ai_summary: Researchers analyze a large language model's ability to read and write raw neural network weights, finding that it performs accurate local arithmetic but relies heavily on memorized dataset priors.

items.title: NutriVisRAG: Multimodal Exemplar Grounding for Nutrient Estimation with Vision-Language Models
items.description: Diet is a major determinant of health, yet accurate dietary assessment from free-living meal images remains challenging.
items.ai_summary: NutriVisRAG is a retrieval-augmented generation framework that uses a vision encoder to provide visually similar annotated meal exemplars for estimating nutrient values with vision-language models.

items.title: When Imperfect Automated Fact-Checking Backfires: Social Learning in the Presence of Misinformation
items.description: Automated fact-checking tools, cheap and fast but imperfect, are increasingly available on social platforms. We study when such tools can backfire in a sequential social learning model of misinformation.
items.ai_summary: Researchers study a sequential social learning model to show how imperfect automated fact-checking tools can sometimes backfire and reduce the likelihood of correct information cascades.

items.title: Performance metrics in machine learning: a scenario-based guide from the confusion matrix to calibration, regression and uncertainty
items.description: Performance metrics can yield different conclusions from the same predictions. This methodological tutorial explains the effects of class prevalence, decision thresholds, aggregation rules and software conventions through controlled scenarios.
items.ai_summary: This methodological tutorial explains the effects of class prevalence, decision thresholds, and aggregation rules on machine learning performance metrics through controlled scenarios and classification examples.

items.title: KeHoSu: Keyed Homoglyph Substitution for Authenticated Text Provenance over Copy-Paste Channels
items.description: Nowadays, large language models produce text at scale, and much of it is redistributed across platforms. A moderator who finds a suspicious comment, post or article may want to know which platform generated it and for which account.
items.ai_summary: KeHoSu is a keyed homoglyph substitution method that embeds platform, user, and authentication metadata into text via confusable characters to track attribution across copy-paste channels.

items.title: Secure Formal Raising: Protecting the Development of AI through Executable Properties
items.description: Model raising revisits Turing's developmental view of machine intelligence. Formal Raising (FR) has recently been proposed to complement this view with explicit behavioral properties. This paper extends that proposal to the security of the raising environment.
items.ai_summary: Secure Formal Raising is a security framework that uses four-valued evidence and executable properties to protect the development environment of machine intelligence models.

items.title: Should We Pay This Much for Robustness? Efficient Proxy Certificates with Marginal Guarantees
items.description: Modern classifiers remain sensitive to small input perturbations, while strong model-agnostic robustness certificates such as randomized smoothing are often too expensive for deployment, requiring an extensive number (e.g. 2000) of model forward passes per input.
items.ai_summary: Researchers propose a proxy certification framework using robust conformal risk control to provide efficient model robustness guarantees while drastically reducing test-time computation costs.

items.title: Reproducing Kernel (Quasi-)Banach Spaces with the $\ell^p$ Coefficient Norms
items.description: This paper advances the theory of reproducing kernel Banach spaces (RKBSs) by investigating the general $\ell^p$ regularization framework, with a particular focus on the non-convex regime $0 1$, we construct RKBSs using a fixed countable dictionary, establish minimizer…
items.ai_summary: This paper advances the theory of reproducing kernel Banach spaces by investigating the general l^p regularization framework for both convex and non-convex regimes.

items.title: GTAFL: Addressing Test-Agnostic Long-Tailed Federated Learning in Medical Image
items.description: In healthcare, protecting patient privacy is crucial due to the sensitivity of medical data and its extensive accessibility. Federated Learning (FL) offers a decentralized and privacy-preserving training paradigm, making it an ideal solution for healthcare applications.
items.ai_summary: GTAFL is a federated learning framework that uses adaptive re-sampling, expert retraining, and self-supervised learning to handle test-agnostic long-tailed distributions in medical image data.

items.title: Learning Dynamics of On-Policy Distillation
items.description: On-policy distillation (OPD) is emerging as an important paradigm for language-model post-training, combining dense teacher supervision with training on student-generated trajectories.
items.ai_summary: This research paper proposes a mechanistic analysis framework for on-policy distillation in language models, mapping how feedback loops shape student learning dynamics and downstream performance.

items.title: Probabilistic Relevance Decisions for Semantic Retrieval
items.description: Dense similarity supplies reusable corpus representations, while probabilistic relevance decisions offer query-dependent document scoring. We compare dense-only BGE-M3 with TypeSafe Jev Noul and OpenAI Decisions Predicate scores on the official BEIR SciFact test benchmark.
items.ai_summary: This research paper evaluates probabilistic relevance decisions alongside dense-only retrieval methods on the BEIR SciFact benchmark, finding that probabilistic scoring improves ranking effectiveness.

items.title: Automatic keyphrase extraction and annotation: modern theoretical approaches and practical solutions for text and speech
items.description: The exponential growth of textual and audiovisual information has made the task of automatic keyphrase extraction (KE) increasingly significant.
items.ai_summary: This research paper provides a comprehensive review of automatic keyphrase extraction and annotation methods, synthesizing statistical, machine learning, and large language model approaches for text and speech.

items.title: Deformable Contact-Aware 3D Object Placement
items.description: Current language-guided 3D object placement typically predicts a rigid 6-DoF pose, ignoring the physical reality that indoor placements are dictated by contact. Consequently, predicted poses often float, interpenetrate supports, or fail to deform soft surfaces.
items.ai_summary: This research paper proposes Deformable Contact-Aware Placement, a 3D object placement framework that uses a coupled rigid-deformable simulator to drop objects into physically accurate equilibrium positions based on semantic intent.

items.title: When GeoFMs Meet VHR: Benchmarking Foundation Models on Very High Resolution Earth Observation Imagery
items.description: Geospatial foundation models are a widely adopted starting point for remote sensing tasks. Most are pretrained on Sentinel-1/2 and Landsat imagery at a ground sampling distance (GSD) of 10m or coarser.
items.ai_summary: This research paper introduces VHR-Bench to evaluate geospatial foundation models on very high resolution Earth observation imagery, showing that specific pretraining regimes effectively transfer to fine-grained tasks.

items.title: Towards Multiscale Molecular Representation Learning through Geometry-Based Fragmentation for Polymer Property Prediction
items.description: It is well established that molecular substructures can contribute unequally to chemical and physical properties, with specific motifs or side chains often playing dominant roles.
items.ai_summary: This research paper proposes a geometry-based molecular fragmentation method and attention mechanism to construct multiscale representations for improved polymer property prediction without using predefined chemical rules.

items.title: Reviving the Discarded High-Resolution Feature for Transformer-Based Tiny Object Detection
items.description: Tiny object detection remains challenging because tiny instances occupy only a few pixels, and their fine-grained details are easily lost during feature downsampling.
items.ai_summary: This research paper proposes ReDHF, a framework that revives discarded high-resolution features using cross-scale fusion, shallow supervision, and query interaction to significantly improve tiny object detection in DETR-like detectors.

items.title: WeLM-Image: A Unified Image Generation Model towards Visual Intelligence
items.description: We present WeLM-Image, a unified image foundation model that integrates multimodal understanding into text-to-image generation, instruction-guided editing, and multi-reference synthesis.

items.title: EDGAR: Efficient Diffusion-Driven Gaussian Avatar Refinement via Synthetic Failure
items.description: EDGAR is a conditional diffusion framework with a fusion block and Mixture-of-Experts that refines degraded Gaussian head avatars by injecting self-supervised identity features, using refined multi-view renderings as pseudo-targets to optimize a single avatar.

items.title: Towards Foundation Decision Models: Drex
items.description: Drex open decision models return probability distributions over user-supplied options without autoregressive decoding, using supervised fine-tuning, RLAF, and consistency losses to improve accuracy, robustness, and latency.

items.title: Franklin Templeton uses OpenAI to support investment research
items.description: Starting with equity research, Franklin Templeton is developing AI workflows to help portfolio managers compare research views and examine investment risks.
items.ai_summary: Franklin Templeton is developing AI workflows using OpenAI technology to help portfolio managers compare research views and examine investment risks.
